@@31713163 <h> So There 's a Locust Plague Too ? <p> A volunteer sprays pesticide in eastern Kenya -- which is suffering from its worst locust outbreak in 70 years . Photo : Tony Karumba/AFP via Getty Images <p> It 'd be easy to quip biblically about the simultaneous breakout of pandemic and plague if not for the vast human toll that the intercontinental crises are exacting . As the coronavirus continues to spread on six continents , a desert locust outbreak has inundated East Africa with hundreds of billions of bugs , causing food shortages in Kenya , Somalia , and Ethiopia . " It was like an umbrella had covered the sky , " Joseph Katone Leparole , a 68-year-old living in central Kenya , told the New York Times . <p> In our age of overlapping crises , it should n't be a surprise that climate change can be identified as a factor in the upsurge , the technical term used for such a natural disaster that is just below plague . It began in 2018 , when a pair of cyclones came in from the Indian Ocean and hit the " empty quarter " of the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ of Saudi Arabia , Yemen , and Oman . In a speech before the African Union in February , U.N . general secretary Ant ? nio Guterres explained the unfortunate cycle : " Warmer seas mean more cyclones , generating the perfect breeding ground for locusts . " <p> " When you have rains associated with cyclones , they 're much stronger than normal , " said Keith Cressman , the senior locust-forecasting officer at the United Nations ' Food and Agriculture Organization . " When those rains fall in desert areas with sandy soil , that will flood the soil . Once those floods recede , the soil retains so much moisture that it allows desert locust females to lay their eggs probably for a period of around six months . " <p> From these ideal conditions , the bugs moved south into Yemen ( already in a food crisis , Yemenis turned to them as a protein source ) and into the Horn of Africa . The spread was rapid : A single locust can travel up to 90 miles in a day and eat its own weight @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , thanks to the excessive rains . They also turned north , across the Persian Gulf into Iran , and into India and Pakistan last summer . National emergencies have been declared in Pakistan , Jordan , and Somalia to help mobilize a response : The only effective control operation once a swarm is in motion is to spray pesticide directly on the bugs from the air . <p> To help understand the crisis , Intelligencer spoke with the FAO 's Cressman about some of the bugs ' idiosyncrasies and what to expect in the coming months . <p> The FAO projects that the number of locusts could grow 400 times by June if not treated . Could you break that down ? <p> The life cycle of a locust is about three months , so after three months the adults are ready to lay eggs again . With each three-month generation , there 's a 20-fold increase in locust numbers . Locust females lay around 300 or more eggs -- more than 90 percent of them die or the resulting hoppers do n't make it to adulthood . Out @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ there 's about 20 locusts in the new generation that make it . It 's an exponential increase , so after three months you have 20 times , after six months you have 20 squared , so that 's 400 times . After nine months , you 'd have 20 cubed , which is 8,000 times . When you get that type of exponential breeding , then those locust numbers rapidly increase , and that 's how swarms form , basically . <p> So with these new generations , countries in East Africa that have already been inundated could face even more locusts ? <p> Absolutely . There 's a generation in progress now and breeding in Ethiopia , Somalia , and in Kenya . Conditions will probably remain favorable there because of a cyclone in northeastern Somalia in December . Conditions are probably favorable in those three countries until June , so that will allow another generation to occur before then . <p> How are the outbreaks in Pakistan , Iran , and China connected to those in East Africa ? <p> For China , it 's a completely @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in Iran and Pakistan , yes . What 's going on now in Pakistan is old swarms leftover from last summer that have been slowly maturing and now they 're ready to lay eggs , not in the deserts on the border of India and Pakistan but in the desert closer to Iran and Afghanistan . <p> There 's an FAO map that shows them traveling directionally from the horn of Africa over Arabian sea . Can they travel over water ? <p> No problem . In the late ' 80s , they went from West Africa to the Caribbean . They crossed the Atlantic in about ten days . <p> Photo : United Nations <p> How does that work if there 's no food ? <p> They eat a lot before or after ! The way it worked crossing the Atlantic was , they had enough fuel in the tanks but still needed to rest sometimes , so they 'd rest onboard ships , and then they 'd take off again . If there were n't any ships , they 'd land on the surface of the ocean , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ top of the first swarm and rest , and the second swarm would take off and continue flying and the first swarm would drown . <p> My impression was that they choose to go where food is . Do they have choice as a unit where they 're going or is it randomized by wind ? <p> They seem to decide whether they want to take off or fly with the prevailing wind or not , in which case they 'll sit on the ground . They can somehow sense winds when they come from different directions , but they ca n't fly like birds against the wind . So they are a victim of the wind , but still they do control motion to an extent . <p> Without human intervention , how does a locust outbreak end ? <p> There would have to be a failure of the seasonal rains -- that 's usually how mother nature helps to bring these things under control . Sometimes the winds will push locusts into areas they just do n't want to be in . For instance , if they got @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ into cold areas where they would die , or areas that are very tropical where they would pick up a lot of pathogens and die . They 're very susceptible to funguses . Like those guys that got pushed across the Atlantic ocean in the ' 80s , they died immediately when they landed . <p> What happens in a country like Iran where there 's a simultaneous outbreak of locusts and the coronavirus . <p> Fortunately , different parts of the government are responding , so the Ministry of Agriculture is dealing with locusts and the Ministry of Health has to deal with the coronavirus . The resources and manpower are in completely different sectors of the economy . But any additional challenges that a country faces , they can have impacts on the control operations , and they might not be as effective as hoped . <p> What about states in open conflict or with major security issues , like Yemen or Somalia ? <p> Yemen is very critical because it 's a frontline country for desert locusts . Desert locusts are there every year , and there @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in the wintertime in the interior . It 's a country that has a really spectacular habitat for desert locusts , and when it rains , those locusts take advantage of it . <p> That 's probably one of the reasons why the locust infestation shifted from the empty corridor in 2019 across to the Horn of Africa in the summer , because they stopped off in Yemen for a generation of breeding in the spring . Because of the conflict , there 's very little that can be done . It 's just not safe for the national locust teams to to operate throughout the country to undertake the survey for control operations . There are a few limited areas they can work in , but it simply is n't enough . <p> Fortunately , in Somalia , the key locust breeding areas are in the north of the country , which is a region that 's much easier to operate in . It 's much safer , so national teams can get in there and do the survey and control operations . However , in the south and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ challenging . Those parts of the country do n't see locusts often , maybe once every few decades , so they also have very little capacity . <p> What about in South Sudan , where there is already a food shortage ? <p> The good news is , it 's not really their typical habitat . It 's not dry enough , and they do n't have so much sandy soil . It 's more of a clay soil , and there 's much more vegetation cover , so this makes it hard for the females to find bare , empty places to lay their eggs . And we 've seen this with those locusts that got into northeastern Uganda and the southeast of South Sudan : They flew around , and the females became so desperate that they just kind of dropped their eggs on top of the soil , which means that they immediately dry out and die . Desert locusts do n't do this very often . These guys are masters of survival . They 're professionals , so this means that those females are really desperate @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ transit zone . Later on in the spring , a new generation of swarms will likely form in northern Kenya . Once it drys out there , they will be moving back into Somalia , back into Ethiopia , and probably into north Sudan to get really into the Sahara and the deserts they prefer . <p> What 's the most effective form of prevention and treatment if an outbreak is already in motion ? <p> When you have these cyclones , it comes back to climate change : We 're starting to see more patterns of severe weather , which means unusually heavy rainfall , cyclones , t hese things . You ca n't prevent them really . So we 're going to have to develop better mechanisms to respond to them better . Basically it means that countries are going to have to be very well prepared . Then the international community has to step in . <p> The U.N . is calling for $138 million to mitigate the crisis . In his own kitchen , he always kept an empty milk carton into which he would toss the peelings , tough stems and end pieces from vegetables . At the end of the day he would tuck the carton into the freezer , and when it was full he would dump it into a pot and make stock . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You could follow his example and add those kitchen trimmings when making strong beef stock , the basis for today&amp;rsquo ; s Decadent French Onion Soup . Simply add a green salad to turn this soul-warming dish into a meal . The recipe is adapted from Justin Joyce and Stephan MacIntyre , the talents behind Burgoo , which lists the dish under comfort food , not soups , at its five bistros. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;5754;TOOLONG ... title= " A golden topping of toasty croutons and gooey cheese crowns a bowl of Decadent French Onion Soup . " data-portal-copyright= " Robert Shaer " **28;5790;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239707 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Decadent French Onion Soup&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; You will need six individual ovenproof soup bowls for this recipe , ideally ones that narrow at the top . This classic shape helps to keep the bread and cheese afloat as the soup bakes . Be sure to warn guests that the bowls are burning hot &amp;mdash ; and have ice at the ready in case they forget . I buy my stock at the Granville Island Stock Market ; see today&amp;rsquo ; s second recipe or Kitchen Hack for other options . ( Adapted from Burgoo : Food for Comfort by Justin Joyce and Stephan MacIntyre , Figure 1. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac14 ; cup extra-virgin olive oil &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac14 ; cup butter &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 6 cups thinly sliced white onions ( about 8 medium ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 4 fat garlic cloves , chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 cups dry red wine &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sea salt and freshly&amp;nbsp ; ground pepper &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 6 cups Strong Beef Stock ( recipe follows ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 cups grated mozzarella cheese &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1/2 cup grated Emmental cheese &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1/2 cup grated Gruy&amp;egrave ; re cheese &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 6 slices rustic baguette , cut into in 1-inch cubes &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat olive oil and butter in a large , heavy stockpot over low heat . Add onions and saut&amp;eacute ; , stirring often , for 30&amp;nbsp ; minutes . Raise the heat to medium-high , stir in garlic and cook , stirring often , for about 10&amp;nbsp ; minutes , until onions and garlic are brown and caramelized and all the liquid is evaporated . Pour in wine , season with generous pinches of salt and pepper and boil , stirring , until most of the liquid is evaporated , about 5&amp;nbsp ; minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat the oven to broil or 450&amp;deg ; F. Set 6 ovenproof soup bowls on a baking tray . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add the beef stock to the pot , bring to a boil , reduce heat to low and simmer , uncovered , for 30&amp;nbsp ; minutes . Divide soup evenly among prepared bowls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a small bowl , combine the mozzarella , Emmental and Gruy&amp;egrave ; re , mixing well . Divide bread chunks among the bowls , carefully floating them on the soup to create a raft . Divide mixed cheeses among bowls , sprinkling it evenly over the bread . Bake for 6 to 8&amp;nbsp ; minutes , until cheese is golden and bubbly . Serve immediately . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Serves 6 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Strong Beef Stock&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If don&amp;rsquo ; t have a butcher who can provide the needed bones , substitute oxtail and/or short ribs . You don&amp;rsquo ; t want to leave the simmering broth unattended , so make this recipe on a day when you can be home . ( Adapted from Epicurious.com. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 4&amp;nbsp ; pounds meaty beef bones &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 unpeeled carrots , cut into 2-inch pieces &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 large unpeeled onion , quartered &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 head garlic , halved crosswise &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac12 ; cup dry red or white wine &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 celery ribs , cut into 2-inch pieces &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 bay leaves &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tablespoons black peppercorns &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Salt &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat oven to 450&amp;deg ; F. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spread bones , carrots , onion and garlic in a large roasting pan and roast for 20 minutes . Stir well and continue roasting until deeply browned , about 20 minutes more . Transfer to a large stock pot . Place roasting pan on stovetop , deglaze with wine and add pan scrapings to stock pot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add celery , bay leaves , peppercorns and about 12 cups water to pot , covering solids completely . Cover pot and bring just to a boil . Reduce to a low simmer and cook , with lid slightly ajar , for 8 to 12 hours , adding water if needed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Set pot aside off heat to cool before straining through a fine-mesh sieve , discarding solids . Refrigerate for several hours or overnight so you can remove solidified fat from the top . Season to taste with salt before using . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Makes about 8 cups &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Kitchen Hack : Enhancing Canned Broth&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; You can make a fine onion soup with canned broth but you must doctor it : Dilute 3 cans of condensed beef broth ( such as Campbells ) with only 1 can of water and add &amp;frac14 ; cup of dry white wine to cut the sweetness. &lt;/p&gt; Kasey WilsonWed , 18 Mar 2020 18:13:02 **45;5820;TOOLONG ... Gismondi : Slow thoughts on wine in a fast-changing worldhttp : **35;6527;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;6564;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;6600;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1240041 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Self-isolating , self-quarantine , social distancing , flattening the curve , and COVID-19 are terms we never thought much about 90 days ago , or perhaps had even heard of , and now it&amp;rsquo ; s all you hear , day and night &amp;mdash ; and I&amp;rsquo ; m supposed to write about wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I think about the speed with which the virus can spread , it reminds me how relatively slow the wine business can be , and what a good thing that is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It takes three to four years to establish a working vineyard . If you follow the French protocol , ( there&amp;rsquo ; s another one of those words ) , it takes a minimum of seven years before you can make a respectable wine , and 12 to 15 years before you can produce a Grand Vin , a term they use to describe their best wines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a world that moves too fast in so many ways , vineyards offer a chance to slow down &amp;mdash ; whether you work in them , walk through them or even merely enjoy a glass of wine that can be traced to a specific site . It can be comforting in many ways , especially at these times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the days ahead , as we stick close to home and our lives slow down , a glass of wine could turn out to be the highlight of our day . At the very least , it&amp;rsquo ; s time we could spend away from the doom and gloom of COVID-19 news sweeping across the globe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For those who look for silver linings , it is possible wine could be reborn during this crisis . It is no secret its been struggling in the marketplace from challenges by spirits , cocktails , hard seltzers and abstainers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The current rage is White Claw , a flavoured drink whose ingredients include seltzer , a gluten-free alcohol base , and a variety of refreshing fruit flavours made from natural fruit juice . So far , the flavours include mango , black cherry , lime , ruby red grapefruit , or raspberry &amp;mdash ; and it&amp;rsquo ; s flying off the shelves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you reread the previous paragraph and think about wine ( and perhaps many of the columns on this page over the last two or three years ) it will be no surprise White Claw and its ilk are so popular . It is a product responding to young consumer&amp;rsquo ; s wants , and a growing number of voices in the wine community are seeking more transparency about what ingredients are in our wine and where it the product originates . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We have been touting refreshing , red-fruited wines , as opposed to black fruits . We have talked about the need for lower alcohol wines , and we have expressed plenty of concern over origin and appellations , and that the notion of place is where we should be headed . Add in sustainable production , organics , biodynamics and diversity , and you understand the challenge facing an industry working on a three to seven-year model . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just a look at the growing number of vegans and vegetarians in the marketplace . In what world are they going to order a piece of meat to temper the tannins or alcohol in their red wine ? Gluten-free is another example where wineries that make gluten-free wine , or at least wine with levels that fall below global standards ( which is the vast majority of producers ) , do not go to the trouble telling anyone on the label . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Each of these issues that are important to consumers has been given short shrift by many wineries , leaving them particularly vulnerable to an active , nimble refreshment market that can turn out a new drink on a dime. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not the end of the world for wine , just as COVID-19 will not be the end of the world for humanity , but there will be lessons to be learned along the way , including changing just a bit , as opposed to the living in the past . Even slow and steady can be overwhelmed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the meantime , consider supporting your local wineries and buy direct . They will ship it right to your door , which may be the safest way to enjoy a glass of wine this month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;6630;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;6672;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;6708;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;6739;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;6775;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;6803;TOOLONG " &gt;S ... our quarterly wine and food **32;6833;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Weekend wine picks&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;6867;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;6903;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Selbach Riesling ( Fish Label ) 2017 , Mosel , Germany&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $19.99 90/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 00717215001707 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After another year of the fish label , it&amp;rsquo ; s challenging to find the words to describe just how delicious and unassuming this Riesling is . Pulse to coarsely grind . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **38;7595;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;8 manicotti pasta&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) olive oil , divided&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 onion , minced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 ( 5 oz/142 g ) package baby spinach&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 eggplant&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;7635;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 cups ( 1.5 L ) tomato sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cook the manicotti according to the package instructions . Preheat the oven to 375&amp;deg ; F ( 190&amp;deg ; C ) . &amp;nbsp ; In a skillet over medium heat , 1 1&amp;frasl ; 2 tbsp ( 22.5 mL ) oil , then add the onions and sweat for 4 minutes . &amp;nbsp ; Add the baby spinach and keep cooking for 2 minutes . In the same skillet over medium heat , heat the remaining 1 1&amp;frasl ; 2 tbsp oil , then add the eggplant slices and fry for 7 minutes , until softened , flipping halfway through . COVID-19 is taking a bite out of the city 's restaurantshttp : **29;8185;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;8216;TOOLONG ... title= " A collective of nearly two dozen restaurants has united in an initiative they are calling " Breaking Bread " to encourage the community to support independent restaurants , their staff and suppliers during the COVID-19 pandemic . Photo : Courtesy of Breaking Bread " alt= " A collective of nearly two dozen restaurants has united in an initiative they are calling " Breaking Bread " to encourage the community to support independent restaurants , their staff and suppliers during the COVID-19 pandemic . Represented here , from left to right : Caf ? Medina , Juke Fried Chicken , Beetbox , L'Abattoir , Havana , Belgard Kitchen , Wildebeest , Nuba , Heritage Asian Eatery , Origo Club . Photo : Courtesy of Breaking Bread " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;8252;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1240057 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; While we&amp;rsquo ; re all hunkered down at home , self-isolating during the coronavirus pandemic , some of our most vulnerable neighbours could well be going hungry . And in a bitter twist of fate , they&amp;rsquo ; re the very people who normally keep us fed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very scary time , &amp;rdquo ; says Robert Belcham , the chef-owner of Campagnolo restaurant and president of the B.C. Chef&amp;rsquo ; s Table Society . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a time of trying to take care of our customers and take care of our people . But we have to take care of our business , too , or there will be no business to come back to . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Restaurants across B.C. started seeing empty tables and cancelled reservations in January when attendance at Lunar New Year plummeted . Since then , it has just gotten progressively , and rapidly , worse as COVID-19 has spread across the planet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not just the result of people staying home in an attempt to &amp;ldquo ; flatten the curve&amp;rdquo ; of a viral pandemic . Trips , cruises , conferences , trade shows , festivals and other events have all been cancelled , taking with them the customers who would normally be paying the wages of chefs , servers , bartenders , baristas and sommeliers , as well as the people who make the wine , roast the coffee beans and bake the bread . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In other words , the very people who give Vancouver its unique and welcoming flavour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In Vancouver , more than most cities , restaurants &lt;em&gt;are&lt;/em&gt; the culture , &amp;rdquo ; says Justin Tisdall , the owner and operator of the fast-casual restaurant Juke Fried Chicken and Beetbox. &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a viable career , to be a server or to be a chef in one of the most passionate food cities in North America . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It all reminds Belcham of 2009 , after &amp;ldquo ; the markets crashed and the world came to an end , it seemed like at the time , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; But this is different . Back then it was just about money . You can&amp;rsquo ; t just throw money at this . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To stem the bloodletting , many restaurateurs have voluntarily and significantly stepped up their already stringent hygiene , service and sanitary practices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everyone understands that all of our livelihoods are at stake , so everyone is taking it really seriously , &amp;rdquo ; says James Iranzad , founder of Gooseneck Hospitality , which employs 170 people across five restaurants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For instance , they&amp;rsquo ; ve always disinfected surfaces ; now they do it much more often , and visibly , so people can see staff spraying door handles and debit machines every few minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Everyone who touches food wears gloves when they do so . Staff are sent home if they have even the slightest hint of a sniffle . Tables have been removed so there is more room between them to prevent the virus spreading . Web orders for takeout are being encouraged so people don&amp;rsquo ; t have to wait in a crowd &amp;mdash ; and takeout cutlery is individually wrapped , even if it is less eco-friendly. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; re little things but they all add up , &amp;rdquo ; Tisdall says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s up to us to protect everyone we can . And it&amp;rsquo ; s changing every day , so we might have to change how we deal with it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All of this comes on the heels of several challenging years for the restaurant industry . Just in the last year , some 20 restaurants have closed , including favourites like West and Mamie Taylor&amp;rsquo ; s , falling prey to wave after wave of soaring costs for food , labour , taxes and real estate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And then something like this , &amp;rdquo ; Belcham says . &amp;ldquo ; People don&amp;rsquo ; t realize how tight the margins are . Especially in the last couple of years &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s been getting worse and worse and worse . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And however COVID-19 plays out , an enormous number of restaurant workers will be affected . According to 2018 figures from Restaurants Canada , 191,900 people work across some 14,500 restaurants , bars and caterers in B.C. This comprises seven per cent of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s workforce &amp;mdash ; and a quarter of workers between the ages of 15 and 24. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those numbers increase significantly when resort , tourism and hotel workers are included . And that has the B.C. Hospitality Foundation increasingly concerned , especially since the organization relies on people in the industry for the donations they use as last-resort funding for hospitality workers dealing with medical issues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We were not prepared for this . I don&amp;rsquo ; t think anyone was prepared for this , &amp;rdquo ; says Dana Lee Harris , BCHF executive director . &amp;ldquo ; British Columbia has a vibrant and close-knit hospitality community and &amp;hellip ; we need to make sure these people have income . We will do our very best to help hospitality workers that reach out to us and need help financially when they are hit with a financial crisis because of a health condition . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those interested in offering donations should visit the website at &lt;a href= " http : **29;8282;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;8313;TOOLONG ... . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;How to help&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are other ways to support local restaurants , and the people who work for them , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;If you feel well , and you 're comfortable going out : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Dine out at your favourite independent restaurants . Yes , the chains are hurting , too , but their owners have a bigger financial cushion to protect themselves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; In fact , about two dozen independent restaurants have united in an initiative called Breaking Bread ( &lt;a href= " http : //breakingbreadvan.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;8346;TOOLONG &; ... ) , which is offering special prix fixe menus from March 14 to 31 , hoping to attract diners ( dine in or take out ) so they can continue to pay staff and suppliers . Line an 8-inch round cake with parchment paper . Do not grease the sides of the pan ! Measure chocolate into a large bowl . In a small pot bring the butter to a roaring boil . Pour the butter over the chocolate , let sit for a minute or so , then whisk until smooth . &amp;nbsp ; In a standing mixer fitted with the whisk attachment , mix together the egg whites and half of the brown sugar on medium speed until stiff peaks form . &amp;nbsp ; Transfer egg whites to a separate bowl . In the standing mixer bowl , add the remaining sugar and the egg yolks . Gismondi : B.C. sustainable certification a step in the right directionhttp : **31;8708;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;8741;TOOLONG ... title= " B.C. Certified Sustainable Wine could hit the shelves as early as January , 2021. " alt= " B.C. Certified Sustainable Wine could hit the shelves as early as January , 2021. " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;8777;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1233613 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The wine world has left Vancouver and not a moment too soon for many travellers trying to make their way home through the coronavirus haze . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most of the world&amp;rsquo ; s prominent trade shows &amp;mdash ; including VinItaly , Prowein , Raw Wine London and the Grands Jour de Bourgogne &amp;mdash ; were cancelled or postponed while 162 wineries were in the city . It left local organizers and benefactors in the very fortunate position of pulling off the 42nd annual winefest just in time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Will the three-month ( or maybe more ) moratorium on trade shows trigger a rethink of how the wine trade conducts its business worldwide ? The model is ancient and its carbon footprint is vast , and for an industry big on sustainability perhaps it behooves all of us to spend the next three months ( while we are in effect quarantined at home ) , to sit down and think what the next 50 years of wine could look like if we put the planet first . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Climate change has forced a lot of us to think about the future and how we might live better on this Earth , but it would appear the time to change how we exist , maybe even survive on this planet is fast approaching . Who knows , maybe some good will come of the coronavirus as it exposes the many weaknesses we are a slave to because we loathe the thought of change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is some promising news on the home front . Very shortly , British Columbia wine drinkers will be able to quickly identify bottles made with people and the planet in mind . Beginning April 1 , earth-friendly vineyards and wineries will take stock of their sustainability efforts and apply for certification , with B.C. Certified Sustainable Wine hitting the shelves as early as January , 2021. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The new certification was developed by volunteer Sustainable Winegrowing B.C. committee&amp;nbsp ; ( SWBC ) members , representing all aspects of the B.C. wine industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When we started promoting sustainable practices in 2008 , we knew the wine industry was going to grow , &amp;rdquo ; said SWBC chairwoman Karen Gillis , vineyard operations manager for Andrew Peller Ltd. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; SWBC has become a hub for wine industry knowledge , sharing best farming practices that contribute positively to the land , our neighbours and our economy . Certification is the next step . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Criteria to become a certified vineyard or winery will be comprehensive , including high standards for water conservation , ecological diversity , soil health , worker safety , social benefit , and more . More important , a third-party will audit participants who will be required to track their progress , and must continually improve to stay certified . So far , so good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jane Campardo of Okanagan Crush Pad , has been volunteering for eight years with SWBC. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; After a decade of leadership , our wine industry is ready to game up to the next level . We are holding ourselves accountable to some of the most rigorous sustainability standards in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We listened to growers and wineries to make our certification process as meaningful and easy-to-use as possible . It&amp;rsquo ; s set up so that the smallest family business or the largest multi-holding winery can participate . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The certification process applies to both vineyards that grow grapes and wineries that make wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a wine to showcase the B.C. Certified Sustainable Wine logo on the bottle , it must be made with at least 50 per cent certified grapes ( until 2025 , when it increases to 75 per cent ) , and the winery must also have passed the auditing process . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is a start &amp;mdash ; but , seriously , half sustainable is half unsustainable . One hundred per cent sustainable should be the goal , and no herbicides and no pesticides should be the end game as soon as possible . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I think the high price of B.C. wine demands nothing less . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;8807;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;8849;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;8885;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;8916;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;8952;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Weekend wine picks&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;8980;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9016;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Ken Forrester Old Vine Reserve Chenin Blanc 2018 , Stellenbosch , Coastal Region , South Africa&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $21.99 89/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 6009607660383 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Reserve comes off 39-year-old bush vines from six different vineyards around Stellenbosch . Food ReviewsAnthony Gismondi : Coronavirus impacts Vancouver wine festivalhttp : **32;12416;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;12450;TOOLONG ... title= " Coronavirus has impacted the show , with several principles stuck in Italy and Croatia . " alt= " Coronavirus has impacted the show , with several principles stuck in Italy and Croatia . " data-portal-copyright= " CARLOS JASSO " **28;12486;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1228291 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today&amp;rsquo ; s column was filed on the go at the 42nd Vancouver International Wine Festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although the big International Tasting Room had not opened yet , ( more on that buzz next week ) , a lot was happening across the city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Coronavirus has impacted the show , with several principles stuck in Italy and Croatia . I&amp;rsquo ; m sure it&amp;rsquo ; s just the beginning of travel troubles for the global wine business . From wine shows to tourists , it is going to be a challenging year for wine producers and consumers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here is some news in brief : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The French wineries in the city to headline the festival are rightfully concerned about coronavirus , since many have significant interests in China as an export market , and from all accounts that market is essentially closed with little or no business being conducted . One producer told me they just opened an office in China and the entire team is sitting around at home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; * The festival kicked off , as always , with its Bacchanalia Gala Dinner and Auction held at the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver . The nine wine multi-course dinner was the backdrop for both live and silent auctions that eventually tallied more than $233,000 for the festival 's charitable beneficiary , Bard on the Beach . The sold-out raffle for two Delta One international business class tickets , donated by Delta Air Lines , raised an additional $20,000 . The total money raised for the performing arts was on target cross the $10 million mark . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;* Michel and Tina Gassier hosted an exceptional dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant , featuring several Domaine Gassier wines from their home estate in Costiere di Nimes in the southern Rhone Valley . Gassier spoke mostly about a sense of place and his philosophy about winemaking . He likens the effect of terroir or its print on the wine to " a musical score , and it is always deeper , more complex and more interesting than one created by man . The winemaker needs to learn to understand it and nourish it , to let its vibrato resonate through the wine . Later , much like a conductor , the winemaker can give free rein to his creativity through the art of blending . " You will find most of the Gassier in private wine shops and , like most of the dinner attendees , you will be shocked by their quality and value . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; At Chambar Restaurant , the crack sommelier staff and chef Nico Schuermans and his team pulled off a fabulous Ventous Tour de Feast , hosting Fr&amp;eacute ; d&amp;eacute ; ric Chaudiere of Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Pesqui&amp;eacute ; . Pesqui&amp;eacute ; is situated on the hills of Ventoux on the southeast side of the Rhone Valley . Chaudiere made an unusually large impression on attendees by pouring all his wines in magnums . We learned that there is evidence of vine cultivation at Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Pesqui&amp;eacute ; that dates to 2000 years ago . The recent discovery of a pottery workshop and wine pottery from the Roman era ( 30 B.C. ) in the C&amp;ocirc ; tes du Ventoux Appellation confirms that the region is one of the oldest wine-producing areas in France . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Not to be outdone , Gerard Bertrand led a master class on the Languedoc to just under 100 people from the local trade , who had a chance to hear the passion and that drive that has made Bertrand a significant player in the French wine business today . &amp;nbsp ; With 15 estates and now almost 2500 hectares of vineyard farmed biodynamically , he is the largest producer of biodynamic wine in the world . Bertrand&amp;rsquo ; s home base is Chateau l&amp;rsquo ; Hospitalet , a traditional 16th century building that is now a hotel . It is surrounded by a vineyard , 1,000 hectares of pines , bushland and rocky hillsides . The site is entirely farmed biodynamically , and is a shining example of what can be done in agriculture to protect natural biodiversity . The winery restaurant , L&amp;rsquo ; Art de Vivre , highlights the products of the Languedoc region , accompanied by Bertrand&amp;rsquo ; s growing list of grand cru wines . It&amp;rsquo ; s an oasis you should put on your wine bucket list . You will not be disappointed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Back to the tasting room ! Vive la France . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;12516;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;12558;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;12594;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;12625;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;12661;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;12692;TOOLONG " &gt;2 ... Among the very classic dishes in The Buddhist Chef is his vegan riff on Beef Bourguinon , prepared with the meaty non-meat , portabello mushrooms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13287;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;13323;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Portabello **26;13353;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 portobello mushrooms , quartered&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 carrots , sliced into rounds&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 onion , thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) vegetable oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) ground cumin&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? teaspoon ( 1 mL ) ground allspice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Black pepper , to taste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 ? cups ( 375 ml ) red wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 ml ) vegetable broth&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? cup ( 60 ml ) soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) tomato paste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) maple syrup&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 bay leaves&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) cornstarch&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) water&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Fresh parsley leaves , to garnish&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat the oven to 400&amp;deg ; F ( 205&amp;deg ; C ) . In a large ovenproof pot , combine the mushrooms , carrots , onions , oil , cumin , salt , allspice , and black pepper . Roast for 30 minutes . Transfer to the stove , then stir in the red wine . Simmer for 5 minutes over medium-high heat . Add the vegetable broth , soy sauce , tomato paste , maple syrup , and bay leaves . Bring to a boil , lower the heat , and simmer for 15 minutes . In a small bowl , combine the cornstarch with the water . Add the cornstarch mixture to the pot , stirring constantly . Bring back to a boil , then remove from the heat as soon as the sauce has thickened ( about one minute ) . Remove the bay leaves . Garnish with parsley and enjoy on its own or with pasta or rice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes two hearty servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Wine match&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stick with the same red wine used in your bourguignon recipe . Never cut corners on cooking wine ; if you don&amp;rsquo ; t want to drink it , don&amp;rsquo ; t put it in the food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13381;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;13417;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Bartier Bros . Merlot Cerqueira Vineyard 2018 , Okanagan Valley , $21.99&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The density of this Merlot is always impressive . Creamy and silky , naturally dry , savoury , desert blue fruits . Love the mineral notes and salt that cleans up the finish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13447;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;13483;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Hester Creek Character 2018 , Golden Mile Bench , Okanagan Valley , $20.95&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The flavours are a bright mix of dark , savoury fruit , dried herbs with a dusting of vanilla . You can drink this now , and the winery suggests you do it with smoked ribs or pulled pork . Food ReviewsKasey Wilson : There 's nothing like a bowl of chili on a cold winter dayhttp : **37;14963;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;15002;TOOLONG ... title= " Jalape ? o peppers and sriracha earn Katie Mitzel 's vegetarian chili its " killer " sobriquet. " alt= " Jalape ? o peppers and sriracha earn Katie Mitzel 's vegetarian chili its " killer " sobriquet. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;15038;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1227495 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s nothing like a warming bowl of chili after coming in from the slopes , and it was a long-ago family ski trip that earned my chili a nickname that has stuck with it to this day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The day before our spring-break drive to Whistler , I made a hearty dish-in-one chili in my sturdy , retro-yellow enamelled cast-iron Dutch oven . I put it in the fridge overnight and the next day set it beside two boxes of groceries that were bound for the cabin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My husband packed the car and we set out , but soon stopped at a neighbour&amp;rsquo ; s house to drop something off . In rearranging the cargo , he set the Dutch oven on the roof of the car &amp;mdash ; and you can guess what happened next . Soon after we pulled out , we heard a loud bang , looked back and saw the pot on the pavement with chili spread everywhere . From that day on , we&amp;rsquo ; ve called it Roof Rack Chili . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mine is a meaty chili , but you&amp;rsquo ; ll hardly miss the meat in Katie Mitzel&amp;rsquo ; s Killer Vegetarian Chili , one of many appealing recipes in Rocky Mountain Cooking , a cookbook inspired by her 20 years as a backcountry chef . You&amp;rsquo ; ll want to try her one-layer carrot cake with toasted coconut and her loaded baked potato soup , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Roof Rack Chili&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Like most highly seasoned dishes , chili tastes better the second day . You can cut this recipe in half , but it 's great to have in the freezer . Serve with garnishes such as shredded cheese ( Monterey Jack , Cheddar or mozzarella ) , diced avocado , chopped red onions , sliced radishes , lime wedges , sour cream and crushed red pepper flakes . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac14 ; cup ( 50 mL ) vegetable oil &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 large onions , peeled and chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 4 fat garlic cloves , peeled and minced &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 4 lbs ( 2 kg ) &amp;nbsp ; lean stew meat , cut into small pieces &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3 lbs ( 1.5 kg ) bulk pork sausage &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 ( 28oz/796 mL ) cans diced tomatoes &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 ( 6oz/156mL ) cans tomato paste &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3 to 6 tbsp ( 50 mL &amp;mdash ; 100mL ) chili powder &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3 tsp ( 15 mL ) ground cumin &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) dried oregano &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 ( 14oz/398 ) cans baked beans &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tsp ( 10 mL ) salt &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tsp ( 10 mL ) sugar &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) unsweetened cocoa powder &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3 ( 19oz/540 mL ) cans kidney beans , drained &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a large , heavy saucepan or Dutch oven , heat oil over medium heat . Saut&amp;eacute ; onion and garlic until soft but not brown , about 5 minutes . Add beef and sausage . Cook until meat is brown , breaking up sausage with a wooden spoon . Pour off fat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stir in tomatoes , tomato paste , chili powder , cumin , oregano , baked beans , salt , sugar and cocoa powder . Adjust heat and simmer , partially covered , for 2 hours , stirring often . If the chili becomes too dry , add a little water as it cooks , Stir in kidney beans and pinto beans . Cook 30 minutes longer or until the meat is very tender May be refrigerated or frozen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Makes 16 servings &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;15068;TOOLONG ... title= " Jalape ? o peppers and sriracha earn Katie Mitzel 's vegetarian chili its " killer " sobriquet. " alt= " Jalape ? o peppers and sriracha earn Katie Mitzel 's vegetarian chili its " killer " sobriquet. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;15104;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1227494 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Killer Vegetarian Chili&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;The array of vegetables , beans and seasonings in this chili will have everyone hoping for a little bit more of this delicious one-pot meal . ( Adapted from Rocky Mountain Cooking : Recipes to Bring Canada 's Backcountry Home by Katie Mitzel , Random House , 2019. ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) vegetable oil &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 large onion , peeled and chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 4 garlic cloves , peeled and minced &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 celery ribs , chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 carrots , peeled and chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 cups ( 500 mL ) sliced button mushrooms &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 red bell pepper , seeded and chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 yellow bell pepper , seeded and chopped &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 fresh jalape&amp;ntilde ; o peppers , seeded and chopped ( see Kitchen Hack ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 cup ( 250 mL ) vegetable stock ( I buy it at The Stock Market on Granville Island ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) white wine vinegar &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) Dijon mustard &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac14 ; cup ( 50 mL ) ketchup &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 ( 28oz/796 ml ) cans whole plum tomatoes &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 ( 14oz/398 ) can diced tomatoes &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 ( 19oz/540 ) cans&amp;nbsp ; kidney beans , drained and rinsed &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 ( 19oz/540mL ) cans black beans , drained and rinsed &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 to 3 tbsp ( 25 mL to 50 mL ) brown sugar &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tbsp ( 25 mL ) molasses &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;frac14 ; cup ( 50 mL ) chili powder &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 tsp ( 5 mL ) each : ground cinnamon , ground cumin and dried thyme leaves &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3 tbsp ( 50 mL ) sriracha or your favourite hot sauce ( optional ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sour cream and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese for serving &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a large Dutch oven over medium heat , warm the oil . Stir in onion , garlic , celery and carrots and cook until onion becomes translucent , about 5 minutes . Add mushrooms , peppers and stock . Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes and then stir in vinegar , mustard and ketchup . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , dump the plum tomatoes into a bowl and crush them with your hands , removing stems . Add tomatoes with their juices to the pot along with the beans . Stir in brown sugar ( to taste ) , molasses , chili powder , cinnamon , thyme and sriracha . ( The hot sauce is optional , but this is called killer chili for a reason , so I say go for it . ) Using a wooden spoon or long-handled spatula to get under the ingredients , stir the chili , mixing well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Turn down the heat and cook , uncovered , for 30 to 40 minutes . Taste for seasonings . If desired , add more brown sugar or molasses to cut down the acidity of the tomatoes or a pinch more cinnamon to enhance the deep flavour profile and develop the aromatics . Serve with a dollop of sour cream and garnish with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Serves 6 to 8 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Kitchen Hack : Seeding Chili Peppers&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Using a knife to remove the seeds and ribs from a hot pepper takes a very steady hand . Here&amp;rsquo ; s safer and effective alternative : Cut the chili in half with a knife . Starting opposite the stem end , run the edge of a small melon baller down the inside of the chili , scraping up the seeds and ribs . Cut off the core with the scoop . &lt;/p&gt; Kasey WilsonWed , 04 Mar 2020 19:00:15 **45;15134;TOOLONG ... But probably not for much longer . Owner John Bishop is retiring , and if he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t find a buyer soon , the legendary Kitsilano restaurant will close Aug. 1 . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wrote that letter ( about retiring ) about two years ago , &amp;rdquo ; said Bishop , 75. &amp;ldquo ; It started to occur to me that , &amp;lsquo ; Gee , this is a tough business now . &amp;rsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; d never had to give much thought to the financial stuff at all , really , but these days ( the costs of ) zoning and property taxes and all that stuff is just mounting up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And I thought , &amp;lsquo ; Well , maybe it&amp;rsquo ; s time . &amp;rsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m fed up with losing sleep every night just because of the ability to pay bills . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Bishop&amp;rsquo ; s opened at 2183 West 4th in December 1985 , Bishop said rent and property taxes were around $2,000 per month ; now costs are about 10 times that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We pay a third of the building&amp;rsquo ; s taxes , that&amp;rsquo ; s the biggest chunk we have to fork out , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; And then licensing , all this stuff mounts up . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , it&amp;rsquo ; s been a great run . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Aside from the economics of it , I enjoy it probably more than ever , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; Last week I sat with a couple who were so interesting , had travelled so much and we shared a lot in common that way . I&amp;rsquo ; ve been trying to do a little bit more of that , enjoy the whole thing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Personal interaction like this is part of what made Bishop&amp;rsquo ; s special , a restaurant that retained a loyal clientele where many competitors fell by the wayside . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re not very large &amp;hellip ; 45 seats , &amp;rdquo ; said Bishop . &amp;ldquo ; On a busy night we&amp;rsquo ; ll probably do 70 meals or something like that . Gismondi : What is up with wine , and where is it heading in 2020 ? http : **35;15737;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;15774;TOOLONG ... title= " It looks like consumers are turning away from wine and seltzers are on the rise , which means wine producers need to start listening to what those consumers want . " alt= " It looks like consumers are turning away from wine and seltzers are on the rise , which means wine producers need to start listening to what those consumers want . " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;15810;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1223825 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s wine week in Vancouver , but not all is well , down on the farm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dr. Elisabeth Thach , MW , a distinguished professor of wine&amp;nbsp ; and management at Sonoma State University , posed a question in Business.com recently , that I have been thinking about for a couple of years now , namely , &amp;ldquo ; is wine at the tipping point ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She points to U.S. retail data that suggests &amp;ldquo ; volume is flattening . &amp;rdquo ; Thach goes on to say the wine category trend line is falling and , according to Danny Brager of Nielsen ( the data folks ) , spirits are back in the lead followed by massive growth in malt-based seltzers , part of the beer category . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The popular drink , darling , is White Claw , a 90 calorie , 5 per cent alcohol seltzer , that grew by 290 per cent in volume sales in the past year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ironically , White Claw is owned by British Columbia wine mogul Anthony von Mandl , who has a long history of developing category-leading drinks ( Mike&amp;rsquo ; s Hard Lemonade ) as well as distributing category-leading wines , not to mention ownership of several showpiece B.C. wineries. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of particular interest to wineries is a direct to consumer ( DTC ) shipping report from Sovos and Wines Vines Analytics , suggesting the &amp;ldquo ; highly lucrative DTC wine channel has matured a bit with a modest 4.7 per cent volume increase compared to double-digit growth in 2016 and 2017. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All of which leads to the question : What is up with wine , and where is it heading in 2020 ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thach thinks the answer lies &amp;ldquo ; partially in changing consumer demographics and behaviours , but also in the lack of response by the U.S. wine industry to meet consumer desires . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One result is a slowing in legal drinking age growth in the U.S. population . Add to that a burgeoning health and wellness trend , and a Wine Intelligence survey that says 37 per cent of American wine drinkers report they are reducing the amount of alcohol they drink , and it all adds up &amp;ldquo ; to a huge wake-up call to the entire wine industry . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s hardly breaking news , but when you pile it all up , the future of wine seems cloudy . Not that it needs to grow every year ; we would be happy if it levelled off for a decade , and other critical issues became the focus , such as price versus quality . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wine is way too expensive for what&amp;rsquo ; s in the bottle , from the bottom to the top of the market . It&amp;rsquo ; s driving young consumers to relatively cheap seltzers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thach points to a few issues that require the attention of the wine industry , and by that , she means all wineries ( large and small ) need to pay attention to consumer needs and not hide behind the excuse that &amp;ldquo ; we are a small terroir-driven winery that only sells DTC. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ingredient communication is one area that could help . Terms such as &amp;ldquo ; gluten-free , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; natural flavours , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; no artificial sweeteners , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; paleo-friendly , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; low carb , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; low calorie , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; plant-based , &amp;rdquo ; and &amp;rdquo ; sustainably produced&amp;rdquo ; are just a few of the phrases that consumers seek out as part of a widespread health and wellness trend , yet we see little or no progress from regulators or wineries to embrace such terminology on labels . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lower alcohol wines are another area that could be vigorously explored . We know great wine can be made between 8 and 12.5 per cent alcohol by volume , yet we see so few examples in 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There doesn&amp;rsquo ; t need to be wholesale change , but when you are selling your best products in a package that requires the buyer to purchase another device to open your product , it gives you an idea of how thick the mud is on the shoes of the modern wine industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I leave it to Lulie Halstead , CEO of Wine Intelligence , who , after reviewing much of the latest data on wine sales , said : &amp;ldquo ; wine is growing increasingly reliant on baby boomers &amp;mdash ; those in their 60s and above &amp;mdash ; to drive volume in the sector . Pian delle Vigne is quietly aged in 3000 to 8000 L oak casks , long free from any oak influence , to promote a pure-fruit Sangiovese Brunello . The mid-palate is all black cherry , plums and licorice with soft , dense , fine-grained tannins . Drink 2022-2027 and beyond . It has a magnetic quality that will attract plenty of attention . Mushrooms and pasta anyone ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;16407;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;16449;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;16485;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;16516;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;16552;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;16580;TOOLONG " &gt;S ... our quarterly wine and food **32;16610;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; **27;16644;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; There is a visceral pleasure in cutting into a warm egg yolk through absolutely tender pasta . This is a show-stopping first course that is typically only served in high-end restaurants , but you can do this with help from Randy Shore . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16673;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16709;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Egg Yolk Ravioli&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Egg pasta&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 3/4 cups ( 225 g ) 00 pasta flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 large eggs , lightly whisked&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a large bowl , make a pool in the flour and add 3/4 of the egg mixture , about 130g . Set the remainder of the eggs aside for the ricotta filling . Mix the eggs with a fork incorporating flour as you go . When a batter forms , fold in the rest of the flour . Knead by hand until a smooth dough forms . Tightly wrap the dough in plastic and set aside . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **36;16739;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) ricotta cheese&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) finely grated Parmesan cheese&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Scant 1/4 cup ( 50 g ) raw egg&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Salt and pepper&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;8 egg yolks&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 cup ( 125 mL ) butter&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2-3 slices of thick bacon or guanciale , cubed&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp lemon zest&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) flat-leaf parsley&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a bowl , combine ricotta , Parmesan and egg from the dough recipe . Season with salt and pepper . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dust a cutting board with flour . Use a pasta sheeter to make 6-inch ( 15-cm ) wide pasta sheets . Keep going until you get to setting 7 , then lay the pasta on the floured cutting board . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add the ricotta mixture to a piping bag or a plastic freezer bag ( just nip a 1/4-inch or 1 cm hole in the corner ) . Pipe a circle of ricotta on the pasta dough wide and high enough to hold an egg yolk . Two layers is about right . Repeat leaving plenty of space between the rings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place an egg yolk into each well . Moisten your fingertip with water and make a wet circle around each ricotta well . Carefully place a sheet of pasta on top and seal the ravioli . Avoid leaving air pockets . Cut away the excess dough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a wide pan , melt butter and fry the bacon . Mince the lemon zest with the parsley and set aside . In a large pot of gently boiling , salted water , cook the raviolis for 2 minutes and 30 seconds . Carefully remove , drain and serve topped with butter , bacon and the parsley mixture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 4-8 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Wine match&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Luxurious pillows of cheese with a touch of bacon call for fresh , white wines that can match the texture and cut through the rich , creamy flavours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16777;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16813;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Le Vieux Pin Va ? la Ros ? 2018 , Okanagan Valley , $25 &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A bone dry ros&amp;eacute ; that is a raspberry/rhubarb affair with a spicy strawberry undercurrent ; the perfect foil to take on this creamy dish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16843;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16879;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Life Cycle of a Hobo 2018 , East Kelowna , Okanagan Valley , $26&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A Riesling-like M&amp;uuml ; ller-Thurgau bright in peachy , apricot , green fruit will refresh the palate and cut through the creamy , cheesy notes of the ravioli. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;16909;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;16951;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;16987;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;17018;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;17054;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;17082;TOOLONG " &gt;S ... our quarterly wine and food **32;17112;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Anthony GismondiFri , 28 Feb 2020 19:00:58 **45;17146;TOOLONG ... hour ? la fran ? aishttp : **32;17193;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17227;TOOLONG ... title= " The Sidecar is still one of the greatest of classic cocktails . " alt= " The Sidecar is still one of the greatest of classic cocktails . " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;17263;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1212076 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Think of France , especially on the heels of the Vancouver International Wine Festival , and we tend to think of wine . But France is also a land of spirits , liqueurs , aperitifs , digestifs and , of course , cocktails . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The French have been enjoying mixed drinks for at least 2,000 years , ever since the ancient Romans brought grape vines to what was then Gaul and introduced the practice of stirring honey and spice into their wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over time , the French started creating blended beverages in the form of , say , vermouth or herbal liqueur . It was only in the 1920s , when Prohibition drove America&amp;rsquo ; s top bartenders to Europe , that the alchemy of French drinking changed forever &amp;mdash ; and for the better &amp;mdash ; with the introduction of the cocktail . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Enjoy l&amp;rsquo ; heure du cocktail with these three renowned French drinks . &lt;/p&gt; **28;17293;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Perhaps the most influential of the barkeeps to flee the desert of dry America was Harry MacElhone , late of New York City&amp;rsquo ; s Plaza Hotel . He landed in Paris , where he found himself working in a saloon on the rue Daunou ; in 1923 , he bought the place , named it Harry&amp;rsquo ; s New York Bar and ( maybe ) invented the classic cocktail called the Sidecar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The way the story goes , one day an army captain roared up to the doors of the bar , chilled from his ride in the sidecar of a motorcycle , and demanded something to warm him up . MacElhone combined brandy , cura&amp;ccedil ; ao and lemon juice in a glass with a sugared rim , and history was made . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the Paris Ritz also claims to have created the Sidecar ( and serves a version made with pre-phylloxera Cognac for a mere 1,500 euros or so ) . London&amp;rsquo ; s Buck&amp;rsquo ; s Club has also been credited with the drink . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To confuse things even further , aside from the absence of bitters , the Sidecar is also awfully similar to the Brandy Crusta , which originated in New Orleans in the 1850s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In any case , when made properly ( which , fair warning , is rarely the case ) , the Sidecar is still one of the greatest of classic cocktails . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17323;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17359;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h4&gt;Sidecar recipe&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt; Traditionally , this was one of the classic 1:1:1 drinks , but those proportions taste strangely unbalanced today . Modern Sidecars use more brandy , and often skip the traditional sugar rim and cocktail cherry garnish , though of course you can always add them if you wish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 oz ( 60 mL ) Cognac ( or other fine brandy ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 oz ( 30 mL ) Cointreau&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 oz ( 30 mL ) freshly squeezed lemon juice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pour the ingredients into a cocktail shaker with ice . Shake well and fine-strain into a chilled cocktail glass . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 1 . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;French 75&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The French 75 is a swish sort of Tom Collins made from gin , Champagne , lemon juice and sugar , although some rebels will replace the gin with brandy . It dates back to the First World War , or maybe the 1920s , or maybe the 19th century , when a citrusy punch known as a Champagne Cup was all the rage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; MacElhone is often credited with creating the cocktail and , sure , a &amp;ldquo ; 75&amp;rdquo ; cocktail makes its first appearance in his book , Harry&amp;rsquo ; s ABC of Mixing Cocktails . However , it was made , a little gruesomely , with Calvados , gin , grenadine and absinthe . MacElhone himself credited Buck&amp;rsquo ; s Club , though the drink became truly famous when the French 75 recipe was published in 1930&amp;rsquo ; s The Savoy Cocktail Book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What is certain is that it was named for a piece of First World War French artillery , a 75mm Howitzer field gun called the Canon de 75 mod&amp;egrave ; le 1897 , which was exceptionally fast and accurate &amp;mdash ; just like the kick of this bright brunch favourite . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17389;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17425;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h4&gt;French 75 recipe&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt; Essentially a Tom Collins made with sparkling wine instead of soda water , this is a bright , refreshing and elegant cocktail . If you like , you can also replace the gin with cognac for a drink that is deeper and richer in flavour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 to 2 oz ( 30 to 60 mL ) London dry gin&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) simple syrup , or to taste ( see note ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;0.5 oz ( 15 mL ) fresh lemon juice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 oz ( 125 mL ) brut Champagne or other sparkling wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place gin , sugar , and lemon juice into a cocktail shaker with ice , and shake well . Fine-strain into a flute , top with bubble and garnish with slice of lemon zest . Alternative , pour base drink over cracked ice in a collins glass , then add the sparkling wine and garnish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 1 . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Note : &lt;/strong&gt; To make simple syrup , heat equal amounts of sugar and water together until the sugar fully dissolves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Kir/Kir Royale&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Kir , or Kir Royale , has a very different sort of backstory . It was , in fact , the cocktail of the French resistance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1940 , the Nazis marched into Dijon and confiscated Burgundy&amp;rsquo ; s famous red wine to enjoy at their own tables . Not unreasonably , this annoyed Canon Felix Kir , a Catholic priest who had dedicated himself to the resistance through activities such as aiding the escape of 4,000 prisoners of war from a nearby camp , and was variously arrested , condemned to death , and seriously wounded for his efforts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of his acts of resistance was to reclaim Burgundian &amp;ldquo ; wine&amp;rdquo ; by combining cr&amp;egrave ; me de cassis ( blackcurrant liqueur ) with a bone-dry local white wine called Aligot&amp;eacute ; de Bourgogne and proclaiming it the official beverage of Dijon&amp;rsquo ; s city hall . It was proudly consumed at all state occasions and became known , to one and all , as Kir. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After the war ended in 1945 , Kir was elected Dijon&amp;rsquo ; s mayor , a post he held until he died in 1968 at the age of 92 . He never stopped promoting the Kir and , somewhere along the way , someone brilliantly decided to create a version with Champagne , known as the Kir Royale. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So raise a glass &amp;agrave ; votre sant&amp;eacute ; and enjoy France&amp;rsquo ; s great contributions to the cocktail canon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17455;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17491;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h4&gt;Kir Royale recipe&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cr&amp;egrave ; me de cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur originally from Burgundy , but there&amp;rsquo ; s an excellent version made right here in B.C. by Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Odd Society Spirits . It&amp;rsquo ; s based on the secret recipe of Herv&amp;eacute ; Martin , formerly the personal chef to the Late King Leopold III of Belgium . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;0.25 to 0.5 oz ( 7 to 15 mL ) cr ? me de cassis&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 oz ( 125 mL ) brut Champagne or other dry sparkling wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place liqueur in the bottom of a flute and top with sparkling wine . If you like , garnish with a slice of lemon zest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 1&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;17521;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;17563;TOOLONG " &gt;M ... from the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festival edition of **26;17593;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;17621;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Food ReviewsRestaurant review : ' Fawn over fresh ' in a pasta templehttp : **34;18198;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;18234;TOOLONG ... title= " Lamb and swiss chard maltagliati does not disappoint .
