" data-portal-copyright= " Mia Stainsby " **28;18270;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1220642 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Oca Pastificio&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; 1260 Commercial Dr. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Open for dinner , Wednesday to Sunday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;More info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //ocapastificio.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;18300;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Traffic snarls everywhere foiled our plan to be early birds for dinner at Oca Pastificio . We arrived around 6:30 p.m . Too late ! We put our names on a waiting list and cursed the traffic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Oca Pastificio on a Friday night is pretty much a waiting game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thankfully , Commercial Drive is lively into the evening so we bought some groceries and then cooled our heels at Turk&amp;rsquo ; s Coffee Bar nearby until we got the text &amp;mdash ; table&amp;rsquo ; s ready ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Expectations ran high , given the restaurant&amp;rsquo ; s DNA . Owner/chef Greg Dilabio had worked at one of my favourite restaurants , La Quercia in Kitsilano , for eight years and that restaurant&amp;rsquo ; s chef/owner Adam Pegg is a partner at Oca Pastificio . Dilabio also worked at Kissa Tanto , where he was the pasta guy officiating a marriage of Japanese and Italian cuisine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I phoned Dilabio for an interview , he was at La Quercia borrowing kitchen space for his own prep . The partners had both worked at the Slow Food restaurant Osteria Storica Morelli in Trentino , Italy , and on the 50 Top Italy list of best Italian restaurants in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s about the region , he makes pasta to order , &amp;rdquo ; Dilabio says of the chef Fiorenzo Varesco. &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s how we like to do things , too . I&amp;rsquo ; d always studied pasta but there I refined technique and became comfortable making pasta ( dough ) during service . I make pasta and rice to order and it can be done if you time things properly . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Oca Pastificio is a pasta temple . There are some appetizers and antipasti plates but if you avoid gluten , this isn&amp;rsquo ; t the place for you . &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t do gluten-free other than risotto . I haven&amp;rsquo ; t &lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; &lt;/span&gt; figured it out . We&amp;rsquo ; re a pasta restaurant , &amp;rdquo ; he says . He&amp;rsquo ; s partial to pastas of southern Italy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18333;TOOLONG ... title= " Greg Dilabio , chef/owner of Oca Pastificio , works the pasta machine . " alt= " Greg Dilabio , chef/owner of Oca Pastificio , works the pasta machine . " data-portal-copyright= " Mia Stainsby " **28;18369;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1220644 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The pastas are rolled and extruded during service . &amp;ldquo ; I believe there&amp;rsquo ; s nothing better than fresh pasta . There&amp;rsquo ; s a reason why people fawn over fresh , &amp;rdquo ; he says . He rolls sheets of pasta in a tight space between the kitchen and dining room . Some are handcrafted into noodles , others , like tortellini and cappellacci , form into origami shapes in his hands . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All the while , Dilabio is all smiles , heeding social media organizer extraordinaire Marie Kondo and sparking joy . A pasta extruder in the kitchen , meanwhile , squeezes out other forms of pasta like the rigatoni that evening . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He honours tradition but without complete obeisance . &amp;ldquo ; The more you understand history and tradition , the easier it is to bend rules and make it work without confusing people , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; I want to serve what makes me happy and there&amp;rsquo ; s always room for me to keep exploring . It took me a long time to get there with spaghetti . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pastas change daily , depending on what he finds at the markets ( mostly along Commercial Drive ) and the menu is displayed in chalkboards. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We started with an antipasti platter with a five kinds of cured meats , olives , pickles , pickled zucchini and house-made focaccai ( $21 ) ; some meats were sliced so finely , they were gossamer and sheer . A lovely beginning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then a cauliflower sformato with almonds and anchovy ( $15 ) , which our server , Antoine Dumont ( migrated from La Quercia ) described as a less airy souffle . It was more like a flan , nestled in a salad of herbs , cauliflower and almonds . Really lovely . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for pasta , the lamb and swiss chard maltagliati ( $21 ) intrigued and did not disappoint . More silkiness ! The pasta ( cut into small squares ) was delicate yet had bite . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18399;TOOLONG ... title= " Antipasti platter , part of the pasta tasting option for the table at $60 per person . " alt= " Antipasti platter , part of the pasta tasting option for the table at $60 per person . " data-portal-copyright= " Mia Stainsby " **28;18435;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1220646 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Braised beef rigatoni ( $21 ) wasn&amp;rsquo ; t quite as impressive . Fresh , yes , but the noodles were a little clingy . But the braised beef shin ( with veal jus , cream , parsley ) created a tasty sauce . &lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s a pasta tasting option for the table ( $60 per person ) with antipasti , five pastas and dessert . The chalkboard menu is a vocabulary lesson &amp;mdash ; I learned about puntarelle ( chicory-like leaf ) , maltagliati ( pasta shape ) , sformato ( Italian flan ) and taralli ( pretzel-like cracker ) on my visit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For now , there are two desserts : Almond semi-freddo and orange panna cotta ( both $8 ) . The former was presented in two thin flat slices . One thicker slice would have appealed more . The panna cotta , on the other hand , was a beauty with orange segments and candied orange rind , a contrast of delicate and intense flavours . Dilabio says it&amp;rsquo ; s made the traditional way . The original Piedmontese dessert was bound with egg whites instead of the cheater modern method with gelatin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The wine and beverage is what you might expect &amp;mdash ; Italian to the core and modestly priced . There&amp;rsquo ; s Prosecco , Peroni beer , Negronis and Amaro , and a short selection of wines that reflects a range of major Italian styles and regions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I visited , there were two tables with large groups and the noise level was hard to deal with . &amp;ldquo ; We are a small room and we don&amp;rsquo ; t take reservations , so large groups are very rare , although not impossible , &amp;rdquo ; Dilabio said . &amp;ldquo ; I feel you may have been in on one of those rare occasions . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **27;18465;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **34;18494;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **25;18530;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;18557;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;18590;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;18619;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;18650;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18692;TOOLONG ... coming to popular Thai restaurant in **25;18727;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;18754;TOOLONG ... here to read the latest restaurant **28;18790;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;18820;TOOLONG ... here to read the latest local , national and international food **25;18856;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;18883;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Email &lt;a href= " **28;19664;TOOLONG " **46;19694;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Anthony GismondiWed , 26 Feb 2020 19:00:06 **45;19742;TOOLONG ... Barnaby : The art of constructing a great vegetable burgerhttp : **34;19789;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19825;TOOLONG ... title= " Karen Barnaby 's black bean burger . " alt= " Karen Barnaby 's black bean burger . " data-portal-copyright= " Karen Barnaby " **28;19861;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222114 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; I will confess that I&amp;rsquo ; m not a big burger eater , of either the meat or vegetable persuasion . I sorely miss the &amp;lsquo ; &amp;rsquo ; 80s when I could order a medium-rare beef burger . I can&amp;rsquo ; t do that now , so I petulantly rarely bother . Vegetable burgers generally vary too widely in taste and texture , &amp;nbsp ; and I like reliability . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Making a beef burger is fairly easy &amp;mdash ; a vegetable based one , and especially a vegan one , not so much . Because I like challenges , I decided to go the vegan route . The burger I wanted to create was not one that imitated meat , I wanted it to be identifiable as a bean burger that was savoury , had texture and held together well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To construct a vegetable burger &amp;mdash ; and I&amp;rsquo ; m saying construct because they have to be built &amp;mdash ; you need ingredients that bind them together . Breadcrumbs , oats , sweet potatoes , legumes , and semolina are commonly used . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After a few trials , I chose wheat gluten as the binder . I know gluten is a polarizing ingredient , but it gave me binding power . It is used in the countless vegetarian meat analogs that are sitting in grocery coolers all over the country , and that&amp;rsquo ; s where I got the idea . For centuries , it has been used as a non-meat protein in China and Japan , where it&amp;rsquo ; s known as mian jin or seitan. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With the binder settled , I chose black beans and brown rice for colour and texture . Moisture is the enemy ; too much moisture prevents the burger from holding together . I roasted the cooked black beans and the mushrooms to drive off the water . The mushrooms also provided a savoury flavour along with the granulated garlic , nutritional yeast , tomato paste , soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce . All of these ingredients are high in naturally occurring umami. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In putting it all together , I tried mixing all the ingredients and forming a log which was wrapped and steamed . Nope , too fussy and mushy . I tried baking which was marginally better . Then I realized that I could cook the wheat gluten , mushrooms and seasonings then fold in the rice and beans to preserve the texture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a toasted bun with lettuce , tomatoes and onions , it pretty much lived up to what I wanted a bean burger to be ; savoury , tender and texturally satisfying . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you Google &amp;ldquo ; vegan burger recipe&amp;rdquo ; you get 439,000,000 results . Here&amp;rsquo ; s to burger number 439,000,001. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19891;TOOLONG ... title= " Picture : Karen Barnaby . " alt= " Picture : Karen Barnaby . " data-portal-copyright= " Karen Barnaby " **28;19927;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222113 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Black Bean Burgers&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 x 14 oz ( 398 mL ) cans black beans , rinsed and drained&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 lb ( 500 g ) medium sized mushrooms&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 lb ( 250 g ) onions , approximately 1 large , peeled and sliced into 1/4-inch ( 0.6 cm ) half moons&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 Tbsp ( 60 mL ) extra-virgin olive oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) cooked brown rice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;5 Tbsp ( 75 mL ) vital wheat gluten or wheat gluten -- check the package to confirm that it has around 75% protein&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 tsp ( 2.5 mL ) salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) smoked paprika&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) sweet paprika&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) granulated garlic&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 tsp ( 2.5 mL ) ground black pepper&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) nutritional yeast&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) tomato paste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) tahini&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) vegetarian Worcestershire sauce ( use regular if it 's not a concern for you ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) water&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat the oven to 350 F ( 175 C ) . Spread the beans out in a single layer on a rimmed , parchment lined baking sheet . On a separate rimmed baking sheet , toss the mushrooms and onions with the oil and spread out evenly . Place the both in the oven and roast until most of the beans split open and skins starting to crisp , about 20 minutes . Remove from oven . Give the mushrooms a stir and return to the oven until they are brown and shrivelled , about 35-40 minutes total time . Some of the onions will look black , and that&amp;rsquo ; s fine . Remove from the oven and reduce the temperature to 300 F ( 150 C ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place the wheat gluten , paprikas , garlic , pepper , yeast , tomato paste , tahini , soy sauce , Worcestershire and water into a food processor . Pulse until the mixture comes together evenly . Add the mushroom mixture and pulse until chopped a bit smaller than a pea . ( You can also chop them by hand if a food processor is unavailable , and mix the wheat gluten mixture by hand . Then , combine the two mixtures. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Liberally oil an 8 x 8-inch ( 20 x 20 cm ) baking pan or line with parchment paper . Press the bean mixture evenly into the pan and smooth the top . Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes . Remove foil and let sit until cool enough to handle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Combine the gluten mixture , rice and beans . Mix well with your hands until thoroughly blended . Pick up a patty-sized portion and form it into a patty . A tiny bit of cracking around the edge is fine but if there are a lot of cracks in the patty and the mixture seems dry , add 1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) of water to the mixture and test again . If more moisture is needed , add water in 1 tsp ( 5 mL ) increments. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Form into 8 small or 6 larger patties , 1/2-inch ( 1.25 cm ) is a good thickness but they will heat through faster if 1/4-inch ( 0.6 cm ) thick . You can use a ring mould or round cookie cutter for shaping . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat a liberal amount of your oil of choice in a large , non-stick frying pan over medium heat . Add the patties without overcrowding and turn the heat to medium-low . Low heat is important as the burgers brown quickly . Carefully flip and brown the other side . Keep warm in a low oven and cook the remaining patties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Serve on buns with the condiments and toppings of your choice . The patties can be frozen for up to three months . Cook them from frozen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 6 or 8 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;19957;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;19999;TOOLONG ... from Postmedia food columnist Karen **28;20035;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;20065;TOOLONG " &gt;S ... our quarterly wine and food **32;20095;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;20129;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Kelowna 's Indigenous World Winery honours First Nations traditionshttp : **30;20283;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20315;TOOLONG ... title= " Robert and Bernice Louie in the Indigenous World Winery barrel room in West Kelowna. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20351;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222029 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A small Indigenous-owned winery in West Kelowna is generating major buzz and garnering international awards while honouring traditions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Robert Louie , 68 , who was the elected chief of the Westbank First Nation for 24 years , and his wife Bernice , 48 , are the force behind the Indigenous World Winery brand . Descendants of the Syilx , the Indigenous first peoples of the Okanagan and Similkameen valleys , the couple have five children , two of whom work with them in the winery. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wanted to create a legacy for my family and for my people that promoted Indigenous culture , and honoured our ancestral stewardship of the land , &amp;rdquo ; said Louie. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The couple had long been interested in winemaking , and purchased the acreage in West Kelowna in 2012 . They started the growing grapes and building the winery a year later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20381;TOOLONG ... title= " Indigenous World Winery in West Kelowna. " alt= " Indigenous World Winery in West Kelowna. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20417;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222031 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We want to be very respectful of our culture as we create our wines , and that means being respectful of the lands , practicing water preservation through drip line systems , and honouring our people and our history through everything we do , including our naming . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Louie says he wants to &amp;ldquo ; embody&amp;rdquo ; the Syilx familial naming tradition by passing family names down to the vineyard&amp;rsquo ; s wines . Louie&amp;rsquo ; s traditional name Simo means &amp;ldquo ; connected to the land . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They named their first signature Bordeaux varietal blend Simo &amp;mdash ; and the 2014 vintage has won multiple awards , including double gold at the 2019 All Canadian Wine Championships . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name was given to Louie by his stemtema , or maternal grandmother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She gave me that name as a young boy , I knew the history of it , and it&amp;rsquo ; s been passed down through our family from time immemorial , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Louie , who was born at home on the Westbank First Nation reserve in the Okanagan , started working in the fruit picking industry at the age of 5 , &amp;nbsp ; and by the time he was a young teenager he was working with grapes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He took time to earn a law degree at the University of Victoria , where he was the first Indigenous graduate of their law program and first Okanagan Silyx member to be called to the bar , and later served as councillor and elected chief , all the while &amp;ldquo ; toying&amp;rdquo ; with the dream of the Indigenous winery. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20447;TOOLONG ... title= " Robert and Bernice Louie in the vineyard at Indigenous World Winery in West Kelowna. " alt= " Robert and Bernice Louie in the vineyard at Indigenous World Winery in West Kelowna. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20483;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222044 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Louie credits winemaker Jason Parkes , who he calls &amp;ldquo ; the best in the industry , &amp;rdquo ; with helping the family develop the product that is making its mark on the world . Connecting the winery to his culture added a special responsibility . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was very important we have to compete at the world level , and I knew it would have to be a product that is the best we could possibly make . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other labels the winery produces include a white blend called Hee-Hee-Tel-kin , which shares the traditional name of the couple&amp;rsquo ; s youngest son Trenton , who works in the winery . The name means &amp;ldquo ; big stag deer with the massive antlers that resides in the high alpine , an elusive deer and somewhat spiritual and rarely seen , &amp;rdquo ; said Bernice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I really wanted to honour the women in the family , so I had special Charmat tanks from France brought over to create the sparkling wines . The first one is named after our youngest daughter Cassandra , a sparkling Pinot Noir called La&amp;rsquo ; p Cheet , which means &amp;lsquo ; the sparkle off of the high mountain water creek&amp;rsquo ; , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another sparkling wine is named for the couple&amp;rsquo ; s eldest daughter Kassina. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Her traditional name is Ho-we-nam Ho-we-nem , which means hummingbird because she is busy like a hummingbird , &amp;rdquo ; said Bernice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The couple are also developing a line of craft alcohols called Indigenous Spirits , including vodka and gin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Louie , who frequently shares his story as a speaker , said he&amp;rsquo ; s been questioned by youth over his choice to go into the alcohol industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They say &amp;lsquo ; why are you in it ? &amp;rsquo ; or &amp;lsquo ; how come you make booze and sell it to the people ? &amp;rsquo ; My response is that booze is not bad if you take care with it and honour it : this industry employs people , provides a livelihood , and helps the local economy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition to honouring through naming , the winery celebrates National Indigenous Peoples Day , and hosts special events with Indigenous dancers , story telling and drumming . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Indigenous World winery welcomes visitors daily to their vineyards , where they also run the Red Fox club restaurant , featuring native cuisine and wine tastings. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;20513;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;20555;TOOLONG ... you need to know about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;20591;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20622;TOOLONG ... about First Nations **27;20657;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;20686;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;20722;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;20750;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **33;20778;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;20813;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? NewsAnthony Gismondi : Personalities of the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festivalhttp : **32;20967;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;21001;TOOLONG ... title= " Clovis Taittinger will represent the family firm pouring , among others , Champagne Taittinger N/V Brut at the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festival . " alt= " Clovis Taittinger will represent the family firm pouring , among others , Champagne Taittinger N/V Brut at the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festival . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;21037;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1222568 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " http : **34;21067;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;wine festival&lt;/a&gt; week in Vancouver , and that means a city full of global wine personalities pitching their wares . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is little doubt wine is experiencing a bit of downturn among younger consumers who , for one reason or another , are making different choices from abstinence to cannabis and everything in between . Vancouver International Wine Festival edition of Salut , our quarterly wine and food **32;21997;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; **27;22031;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Sichuan pepper comes in two distinct varieties , so you are going to want to pay attention . The red ones are mild , zippy and lemony , while the green ones are piney , powerful and create a numbing , tingling effect in your mouth . Neither is hot like a chili pepper , but both complement extreme heat . Which one you choose will greatly influence the flavour of this traditional Sichuan noodle dish , adapted by Randy Shore , author of the diner-driven cookbook Home and Away . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;22060;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;22096;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Dan Dan Noodles with Meat Sauce&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) light soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? tsp ( 2.5 mL ) baking soda&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 to 8 oz ( 160 to 226 g ) pork , minced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) grated ginger&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 to 1 tsp ( 2.5 to 5 mL ) ground Sichuan peppercorns&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tsp ( 10 mL ) black vinegar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) chili bean sauce ( aka doubanjiang or toban djan ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) dark soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) chicken stock , divided&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) corn starch&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) duck fat or lard &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) cracked chilies&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;12-16 oz ( 340-454 g ) fresh ramen noodles&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Chili oil , to taste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a bowl , combine light soy sauce with baking soda . Mince pork and add to bowl along with ginger and Sichuan pepper . Mix , cover and refrigerate at least two hours . In a bowl , combine vinegar , chili bean sauce , dark soy sauce , 1 cup stock and corn starch . Whisk until combined and set aside . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a small saucepan on medium heat , warm remaining chicken stock and season to taste with salt . In a wok on high heat , warm fat . Add pork and chili flakes and fry until cooked through . Lower heat to medium , stir sauce mixture to incorporate the cornstarch and then add to wok . Stir until thickened , about three minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile in a large pot , bring three quarts of water to a boil . Cook ramen noodles according to package directions , drain and divide between bowls . Top with meat sauce , Ginger Relish and chili oil . Serve hot chicken broth on the side , to use as needed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 2 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Ginger Relish&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) chopped green onion&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) minced fresh ginger&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) canola oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) light soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? tsp ( 2.5 mL ) kosher salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? tsp ( 1 mL ) sherry vinegar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a small bowl , combine green onion , ginger , oil , soy sauce , salt and vinegar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Wine match&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sichuan pepper , chili flakes and ginger relish call for a glass of cooling wine , or one with some residual sugar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;22126;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;22162;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Van Westen Vineyards Vino Grigio 2018 , Naramata Bench , Okanagan Valley , $19.90&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fresh and bright , with a collection of ripe Naramata Bench orchard fruit flavours with creamy , ripe honeydew and baking spices . Perfect for taming the heat in the Dan Dan noodle dish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;22192;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;22228;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Road 13 Roussanne 2017 , Similkameen Valley , $26&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Exotic , unctuous white wine whose rich , honeyed pear , pineapple , creamy lees , and vanilla flavours both freshen and complement the chili/ginger flavours in what is a noisy dish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;22258;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;22300;TOOLONG ... about 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;22336;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;22367;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;22403;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;22434;TOOLONG " &gt;2 ... But , other times , he stumbles upon wines that make the cobwebs and dirt-floored cellars more than worthwhile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Big name , great vintage , well kept . I put it up to look at the fill . Fill is good . Most of the time , a good cellar gives that , &amp;rdquo ; he says , motioning toward the frayed and damaged edges of a wine label that he found in just such a way . The bottles , he says , often show their age , but the elixirs inside them &amp;mdash ; well , they&amp;rsquo ; ve more than benefited from the passage of time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A good cellar has to be humid . And humidity destroys the labels . But , you don&amp;rsquo ; t drink the labels , &amp;rdquo ; Michelin explains . &amp;ldquo ; When the bottle came out from the Chateau , it was there . This is an &amp;rsquo ; 85 , so in 35 years , it lost half-a-centimetre , which is nothing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This was close to the earth , just by the label . When you take a look at the bottle , you know whether it was well-kept or not . Ninety per cent of the final result is the way it has been kept . Especially when it&amp;rsquo ; s 100 years old . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the bottles that no longer have a label , whether rendered illegible by age or having disappeared altogether , Michelin has a unique trick for discovering what&amp;rsquo ; s inside . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All the wines of Bordeaux have the vintage on the cork &amp;mdash ; the name of the chateau and the vintage year , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; I can sell that to people who trust me , and I sell it half-price . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trust is a big part of the business . Michelin&amp;rsquo ; s customers have to be confident the wines they&amp;rsquo ; re buying are well worth the price tag they command on the resale market , which can regularly see bottles fetching thousands of euros per bottle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After all , the wines his customers buy are for drinking not just for show , he assures. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Ninety per cent of our customers are wine lovers . And they drink , &amp;rdquo ; Michelin says proudly . &amp;ldquo ; We give a warranty on our wines , so if there is a trouble , they can bring them back . But , most of the time , they come back to say it was really good and to have another one . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After discovering a particularly spectacular bottle on a buying trip , Michelin knows which of his international clients will be eager to own it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We know who they are going to . Just like antiques . Especially for old bottles , &amp;rdquo ; Michelin says . &amp;ldquo ; For example , I just found some very old bottles from a high-end vintner and I know who will buy them . I&amp;rsquo ; ll send a few emails to the U.S. , to Hong Kong , to Japan and to Australia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And the customers will say , &amp;lsquo ; OK , I want it . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sometimes , more than one buyer makes a bid for the bottle . &amp;nbsp ; In an instance like this , Michelin sells the rare bottles on a first-come-first-serve basis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because we don&amp;rsquo ; t want to make trouble with our customers . Sometimes our customers will say , &amp;lsquo ; You know , I can pay more , &amp;rsquo ; but we don&amp;rsquo ; t make auctions , &amp;rdquo ; he says with a smile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Located within the Latin Quarter of Paris , the small boutique and wine cellar at 48 , rue de la **33;23719;TOOLONG ; ve has earned a reputation for providing sought-after vintage wines . After starting the business in 1994 at another location , Michelin and his wife , Dominique , moved the operation to its current location in 1997. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The space belonged to a &amp;ldquo ; famous wine merchant , &amp;rdquo ; according to Dominique , named Jean Baptiste Besse who counted Ernest Hemingway among his patrons . After Besse&amp;rsquo ; s death , his children didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to continue the business , so they sold the cellar &amp;mdash ; and all the wines contained within it &amp;mdash ; to the Michelins. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23754;TOOLONG ... title= " A view of wine in the cellar of De Vinis Illustribus in Paris . " alt= " A view of wine in the cellar of De Vinis Illustribus in Paris . " data-portal-copyright= " Aleesha Harris " **28;23790;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1213539 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23820;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23856;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The establishment has a varying amount of stock at any one time , offering three types of wine : old vintages purchased from private cellars ; &amp;ldquo ; high-end young wines&amp;rdquo ; from the vintners of Burgundy ; and a small selection of &amp;ldquo ; everyday wines&amp;rdquo ; that the Michelin&amp;rsquo ; s would recommend to friends and neighbours for regular drinking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Michelin is a member of several tasting juries , which allows him to taste many new wines . From these , he makes a small selection of recent releases in order to bring back to the shop . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really the best of French wines in a range of budgets , which is affordable , &amp;rdquo ; Dominique says . &amp;ldquo ; At a good value . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Open to the public by appointment only , the Michelins also offer limited wine-tasting experiences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not exactly like a wine shop , it&amp;rsquo ; s not at all like a wine bar , it&amp;rsquo ; s not a restaurant &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s something different , &amp;rdquo ; Dominique says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really a place dedicated to wine , especially old vintages , rare wines . And also the best of French wines . That means we are really focused on French wines and we have very few wines from abroad . Even if we love them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Love wine the Michelins definitely do . That much becomes apparent within minutes of stepping through the door of De Vinis Illustribus . For Michelin , it has been a long time in the making . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A few months after graduating with his law degree in the &amp;rsquo ; 70s , a friend of Lionel&amp;rsquo ; s approached him to help work at a wine auction . The friend purchased a small batch of the old wines on offer in the sale . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We came back and he bought a baguette , some cold cuts and he started opening the bottles , &amp;rdquo ; Michelin recalls fondly . &amp;ldquo ; And we had a chance to drink those old bottles . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Enjoying the experience , he returned to the auctions to buy old wines for himself . It was through the auctions that Lionel was introduced to a small private wine club where members sampled only rare vintage wines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There , I had a chance to drink the best French wines , ever . The iconic brands &amp;hellip ; Ch&amp;acirc ; teau d&amp;rsquo ; Yquem 1848 , Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Latour 1929 , Chateau Mouton 1945 . We had them all , &amp;rdquo ; he recalls . Needless to say , the experience further fuelled his personal wine passion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Even if I was working in telecommunications because it was my job , I used to go out buying and buying and buying , &amp;rdquo ; he says . That predilection for purchasing rare vintage wines served Michelin well when they opened their business . &amp;ldquo ; Our private cellar was something like 5,000 old bottles . And we gave those bottles to the company . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Michelin credits his time buying and trying those wines in the early years with providing him with an edge on his sommelier peers today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I had a chance to drink all the big names in France , &amp;rdquo ; Michelin says . &amp;ldquo ; Sometimes a person will come to me and say , &amp;lsquo ; I had the chance to try a Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Latour 1986 , &amp;rsquo ; and I&amp;rsquo ; m able to say , &amp;lsquo ; Yes , but the &amp;rsquo ; 85 is better and the &amp;rsquo ; 82 , I had it . And I had the &amp;rsquo ; 70 , and the &amp;rsquo ; 66 , and the &amp;rsquo ; 64 , and the &amp;rsquo ; 61 , and the &amp;rsquo ; 45 , and the &amp;rsquo ; 29 and the 1870. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And then I can tell you , yes , your &amp;rsquo ; 86 is great &amp;mdash ; but , when you drink the &amp;rsquo ; 82 , you forget the &amp;rsquo ; 86 . And that&amp;rsquo ; s how , now , we can explain what is the best wine for the money . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;23886;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;23928;TOOLONG " &gt;M ... from the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festival edition of **26;23958;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **28;23986;TOOLONG " **35;24016;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;24053;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Food ReviewsStaff BlogsKasey Wilson : Vive La France ! http : **33;26636;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;26671;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;26707;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1216540 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the last week of February , Vancouver gives itself over to a week-long celebration of wine . This year the lineup of festive meals , informative seminars and terrific tastings will showcase 1,450 wines from 163 wineries in 16 nations , with France in the spotlight as the 2020 theme country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harry Hertscheg , executive director of the &lt;a href= " http : **34;26737;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Vancouver International Wine Festival&lt;/a&gt; , expects competition to be keen for tickets to the more than three dozen events featuring French wines . &amp;ldquo ; France is one of the most popular regions , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; It sells out before we know it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;26773;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;26809;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you want to get a handle on France before time , dive into Let&amp;rsquo ; s Eat France ! by Fran&amp;ccedil ; ois-R&amp;eacute ; gis Gaudry ( Artisan , 2018 ) . Subtitled &amp;ldquo ; 1,250 specialty foods , 375 iconic recipes , 350 topics , 260 personalities , plus hundreds of maps , charts , tricks , tips and anecdotes and everything else you want to know about the food of France , &amp;rdquo ; it is a feast for food lovers and Francophiles alike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are classic recipes , such as pot-au-feu , eight essential composed salads , &amp;nbsp ; p&amp;acirc ; t&amp;eacute ; en cro&amp;ucirc ; te , &amp;nbsp ; blanquette de veau , choucroute , and ratatouille ; profiles of French icons like Colette , Brillat-Savarin , Bocuse , the Troigros dynasty and Victor Hugo also a list of great chefs who died before they were aged 60 ; a region-by-region index of cheeses , charcuterie and recipes ; poster-size guides to the breads of France , the wines of France , the oysters of France &amp;mdash ; even the&amp;nbsp ; frites&amp;nbsp ; of France . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You&amp;rsquo ; ll meet endive , the belle of the north ; discover the croissant timeline ; understand the art of tartare ; find a chart of wine bottle sizes , from the tiny split to the Nebuchadnezzar ( the equivalent of 20 standard bottles ) ; follow the family tree of French sauces and discover the meaning of &amp;ldquo ; take it in the baba&amp;rdquo ; or &amp;ldquo ; bad taste&amp;rdquo ; in &amp;ldquo ; The Erotics of Cooking&amp;rdquo ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are recipes for two French classics : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Languedoc Beef Stew with Red Wine , Herbs and Olives&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; This adaptation of the classic French daube is a favourite holiday dish of writer Fiona Beckett at her summer home in France . She adds a little extra wine at the end to lift flavour after long , slow cooking . Serve with mashed potatoes and slow-roasted carrots . ( Adapted from Wine Lover&amp;rsquo ; s Kitchen : Delicious Recipes for Cooking with Wine by Fiona Beckett , Rylands , Peter &amp;amp ; Small , 2017. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 lb ( 1 kg ) thickly sliced braising or stewing steak&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) all-purpose flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;5-6 tbsp ( 75-90 mL ) olive oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 large onion , thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 large garlic cloves , crushed&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) tomato paste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1 L ) Faug ? res or other full-bodied fruity red wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) beef stock&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) herbes de Provence&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 thin strip orange zest&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 bay leaves&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) black olives&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 heaped tbsp ( 45 mL ) roughly chopped flat leaf parsley&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Sea salt and freshly ground pepper&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trim any excess fat from the beef , then cut the meat into large cubes . Put the flour in a shallow dish and season it with salt and pepper . Dip the cubes of beef in the flour to coat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat , add beef and fry on all sides until it is browned . You will need to do this in batches , adding extra oil as you go . Transfer beef to a cast-iron casserole . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat 2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) olive&amp;nbsp ; oil in the same skillet , add onion and cook for 3 to 4 minutes , until softened but not browned . Add garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute , stirring . Add 1 cup plus 1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) of the wine plus the stock , herbes de Provence , orange zest and bay leaves . Bring to the boil , then pour the sauce into the casserole . Heat the casserole over a medium heat and bring the sauce back to the boil . Reduce the heat , cover and simmer very gently for 2 to 3 hours until the meat is completely tender . Check occasionally to ensure there is enough liquid , and add a little stock or water if it&amp;rsquo ; s too dry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; About 30 minutes before the stew is cooked , stir in olives . Just before serving , season to taste with salt and pepper , then stir in parsley , and remaining wine and cook for a further 5 minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 4-6&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Chocolate Mousse&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; This delightful recipe has many virtues : zero added sugar , zero cream and zero butter &amp;mdash ; but plenty of chocolate . It&amp;rsquo ; s a mousse in its simplest form . ( Adapted from Let&amp;rsquo ; s Eat France by Fran&amp;ccedil ; ois-R&amp;eacute ; gis Gaudry , Artisan , 2018. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;9 oz ( 250 g ) semi-sweet dark chocolate&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 eggs , separated&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 15 mL ) espresso&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 pinch salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chop chocolate and melt it over a double boiler . Pour chocolate into a large mixing bowl to cool slightly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Beat egg yolks and stir them into the cooled chocolate until thoroughly combined . Add espresso and stir to combine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With an electric mixer , beat egg whites with the pinch of salt , starting on medium speed , then increasing to medium-high once the whites start to foam . Continue beating until whites hold firm peaks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Using a spatula , gently stir one-fourth of beaten egg whites into chocolate mixture , then gently stir in the remaining egg whites . Spoon mixture into serving dishes and refrigerate for at least 3 hours , &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 6&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Kitchen Hack : Choosing the right wine glass&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Restaurants usually offer white wine in smaller glasses than red wine to maintain the lower temperature of the white . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;26839;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;26881;TOOLONG ... national and international food **25;26917;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;26944;TOOLONG ... latest restaurant **28;26980;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;27010;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;27234;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1213736 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Vancouver International Wine Festival&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Feb 22 to March 1 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : //vanwinefest.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **28;27264;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; The French are back to headline the 42nd Vancouver International Wine Festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They no longer dominate the import market as they did in the 1980s and 90s , but rising tariffs and taxes in the United States and even more uncertainty in China suggest they may be happy to pay more attention to the Canadian market after years of neglect . If ever there was a chance for distributors and buyers to strike for French wines that have disappeared from the mainstream market , now is the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Current turmoil and the ever-persistent increase in competition globally aside , there is no denying French wine has the cachet and the selection to continue to attract consumer attention , not to mention owning some of the most notable addresses in the wine business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Names like Bordeaux , Burgundy , Champagne , the Rhone , Loire and Languedoc have withstood the test of time , and many have been adopted for better or worse by the rest of the wine world to describe their wines . Terms like Burgundian style , Bordeaux blend , and even Champagne-style instead of merely sparkling wine have subliminally kept the French in the game even in places where they have little market presence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What you will discover this week about France versus the rest of the world is that the only difference these days is one of style . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While it may be a bit too simplistic to say , New World wines are richer , riper and typically more alcoholic on the palate ; it is no less accurate ( or naive ) to claim that French wines tend to be leaner in structure , bear more acid , firmer tannins and in most cases , are often crafted to accompany food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In that spirit , we explore the New World versus Old World challenge as it pertains to four principal grape varieties you will find inside the International Tasting Room , adding some tasting room picks you can check out yourself . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the end , wine&amp;rsquo ; s biggest ally is the curiosity of consumers . That should make it a lot easier for Old World producers like France to re-establish itself in British Columbia this week , because it seems everyone here remains curious about wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27294;TOOLONG ... title= " Vineyard in Chinon , Loire Valley , France . " alt= " Vineyard in Chinon , Loire Valley , France . " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;27330;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1213743 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Sauvignon Blanc&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sauvignon Blanc tasted outside of France is repeatedly described as being Sancerre or Pouilly Fume-like. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The challenge is many consumers are simply unaware that the fresh , mineral , crisp flavours of Sancerre , Pouilly Fume , Touraine are linked to Sauvignon Blanc because under French appellation law producers emphasize the origin ( Sancerre or Loire ) and not grape variety . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the New World , the best examples mimic the Loire-style offering smoky , mineral , pear and green apple flavours , leaner structure and higher acidity . Some of the best examples are coming out of Casablanca , Leyda and Limari in Chile ; Marlborough in New Zealand ; Constantia/Coastal Region of South Africa ; and British Columbia&amp;rsquo ; s Similkameen Valley . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Food brings both styles closer together . Clams , green lip mussels , goat&amp;rsquo ; s cheese , pasta and chicken salads rule the New World , while ch&amp;egrave ; vre , any fish in sorrel sauce , onion tarts and mussels would be the French equivalent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27360;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;27396;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27426;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;27462;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;New World : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Clos du Soleil Winery 2018 Fume Blanc , Similkameen Valley , $19&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Old World : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Joseph Mellot 2018 Sancerre La Chatellenie , Loire Valley , France , $40&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27492;TOOLONG ... title= " Vineyards , near Corton in C ? te de Beaune , France . " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;27528;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1213742 " /&gt; **31;27558;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Chardonnay is the perfect vehicle for New World-Old World grape detective work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The past decade has witnessed an enormous shift in New World Chardonnay production as the best Chardonnay vines have been pushed to the coolest , most marginal ( in terms of weather ) vineyard sites where acidity and fruit are intensified long before the grape gets to the winery . The result is more intensely flavoured fruit and more vibrant , mouth-watering acidity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sonoma Coast , Monterey and Santa Barbara lead the California transformation , while parts of New Zealand ( Nelson , Central Otago and Hawke&amp;rsquo ; s Bay ) ; and Australia , ( Victoria , Tasmania and Adelaide Hills ) are equally as impressive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for the unknown but soon to be front and centre , it is Chardonnay from Canada&amp;rsquo ; s Niagara Peninsula , Prince Edward County , and the Okanagan Valley . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best of France is labelled Corton-Charlemagne , Puligny Montrachet , Chassagne Montrachet , Chablis , Macon , C&amp;ocirc ; te Chalonnaise , and lately Limoux and the Jura . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The French style is evolving as well with less sulphur and a cleaner style if not necessarily fruitier . Less overt oak , more lees and bread dough characters give them a complexity edge and it makes for excellent food wines . Lobster , tuna , oysters and Caesar salad are more New World dishes , while the French prefer their Chardonnay with wild salmon , turbot , sole , oysters , white bean pur&amp;eacute ; e , and onion tarts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27591;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;27627;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27657;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;27693;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;New World : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Bodega Catena Zapata 2017 Catena Alta Chardonnay , Mendoza , Argentina , $44&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Old World : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Maison Louis Latour 2017 Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru , Cote de Beaune , France , $255.99&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;27723;TOOLONG ... title= " Vineyards in the autumn , Burgundy , France . When the French get it right , their Pinot can be mind-altering. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The challenge for consumers is a blizzard of producers that share a small number of appellations . But if Burgundy is the temple of Pinot Noir production , the rush is on globally to pull even . Central Otago , Martinborough , Canterbury , Nelson and Marlborough lead the New Zealand challenge , while Russian River , Monterey and Santa Barbara County in California and most of Oregon&amp;rsquo ; s Willamette Valley lead the United States . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Look to Tasmania and Yarra Valley in Australia and Leyda and Casablanca in Chile as well as the Okanagan Valley and Cowichan Valley in British Columbia and Niagara and Prince Edward County in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In France , Pinot Noir food matches include rabbit , Maigret de canard , pheasant and coq au vin . Some 14 years later , Babette learns that she has won 10,000 francs in a lottery and decides to cook a &amp;ldquo ; real French dinner&amp;rdquo ; for the town&amp;rsquo ; s few , and increasingly querulous , residents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What follows is a remarkable seven-course feast that overcomes the unhappy villagers&amp;rsquo ; resentments , regrets and suspicions of earthly pleasure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;29536;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;29572;TOOLONG &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;29608;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;29650;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;29686;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film , directed by Gabriel Axel , went on to win the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film . Now it&amp;rsquo ; s being remade by the Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alexander Payne ( Sideways , Downsizing ) , who plans to set his version in small-town Minnesota . No word yet , though , on whether he will recreate the movie&amp;rsquo ; s most famous dish , the cailles en sarcophage. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The origins of the dish are uncertain &amp;mdash ; Dinesen herself may have dreamed it up , for all we know &amp;mdash ; but it has since joined the pantheon of legendary French foods . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I never heard of it before I watched the movie , so I can&amp;rsquo ; t say where it was from , but I would say the Perigord because truffle is involved , and foie gras , and Cognac , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was impressed not just by the dish itself , but by the way Babette &amp;mdash ; who , it is revealed , was once the greatest chef in Paris &amp;mdash ; produces it . Not only does she have all the precious ingredients shipped to a remote village in Jutland , she cooks them in less-than-ideal conditions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That part of the dinner is very exciting and moving because she&amp;rsquo ; s cooking over fire and without proper equipment , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; After seeing the movie , I wanted to do it my own way , and within the logistics of serving 100 people a night . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That meant , for instance , finding the right quail , which Poirier eventually tracked down at Thiessen Specialty Poultry in Mount Lehman. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a jumbo quail , bigger than what you&amp;rsquo ; d find at the grocery store , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the film , Babette tucks &amp;ldquo ; a big slab of foie gras and a layer of truffle&amp;rdquo ; into each deboned quail , but that would be much too costly , so Poirier instead makes a stuffing of foie gras and sausage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And where Babette serves it with figs , he uses grapes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The first time I had quail was in a classic restaurant where it was paired with grapes and honey , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says nostalgically. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;29717;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;29759;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;29795;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a dish that can take several hours , even days to prepare , so he suggests some shortcuts for home cooks . Rather than making puff pastry and foie gras terrine from scratch , you can purchase good-quality pre-made versions instead . He also suggests preparing it in stages , for instance , by starting the pastry cases the day before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The thing with these dishes is it&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of preparation , and then it&amp;rsquo ; s just assembly , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You can break it down over two days , three days , just little jobs . And when it comes to the day of , it&amp;rsquo ; s pretty simple . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He adds : &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very festive dish and decadent as well . It takes a lot of time to prepare , but it&amp;rsquo ; s worth it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s just the sort of classic haute cuisine Poirier learned cooking with Normand Laprise at Montreal&amp;rsquo ; s celebrated Toqu&amp;eacute ; ! and Rob Feenie at Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Lumi&amp;egrave ; re , and celebrated last year at a collaborative dinner with Canada&amp;rsquo ; s original Top Chef , Dale MacKay , that paid homage to France&amp;rsquo ; s greatest chefs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It included : Paul Bocuse&amp;rsquo ; s famous truffle soup with its puff pastry dome ; Marie-Antoine Car&amp;ecirc ; me&amp;rsquo ; s eggs Rossini ( poached eggs with foie gras and truffle sauce on brioche ) ; the rich , creamy baked lobster thermidor created by Auguste Escoffier ; and a syrup-soaked savarin , named for the legendary food writer Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin , who famously wrote , &amp;ldquo ; Tell me what you eat , and I will tell you what you are . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was pretty good , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says with a laugh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of course , these are not everyday dishes , but rare and special indulgences &amp;mdash ; just like Babette&amp;rsquo ; s Feast , which could never be truly recreated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Babette spends every last centime of her 10,000-franc winnings to create that one meal for those 12 people . When the sisters learn this , one of them says , tearfully , &amp;ldquo ; Now you will be poor the rest of your life , &amp;rdquo ; to which Babette replies , &amp;ldquo ; An artist is never poor . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And neither is any person who gathers friends , family and even the occasional stranger around the table , to share food and wine and each other&amp;rsquo ; s company . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think it&amp;rsquo ; s important , as that movie showed , to sit around the table and take your time , even if it&amp;rsquo ; s just once a week , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says . &amp;ldquo ; It brings people together and that&amp;rsquo ; s the power of food . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;The Babette 's Feast menu&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the 1987 Danish film Babette&amp;rsquo ; s Feast the seven-course menu consisted of : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Potage &amp;agrave ; la Tortue ( turtle soup ) , served with Amontillado sherry &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Blini Demidoff au Caviar ( buckwheat pancakes with caviar and sour cream ) , served with Veuve Cliquot Champagne &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Cailles en Sarcophage ( quail stuffed with foie gras and truffles and baked in puff pastry ) , served with Clos de Vougeot Pinot Noir from Burgundy &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Endive salad &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Savarin au Rhum avec des Figues et Fruit Glac&amp;eacute ; e ( rum-soaked sponge cake with figs and candied cherries ) , served with more Champagne &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Cheese and fruit with Sauternes &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Coffee with Cognac &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;29826;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;29868;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;29904;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;29935;TOOLONG ... title= " Photo by Amy Ho . " alt= " Photo by Amy Ho . " data-portal-copyright= " Amy Ho " **28;29971;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1212146 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Recipe : Cailles en Sarcophage ( Stuffed Quails in Puff Pastry ) &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Recipe by chef J-C Poirier of Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s St. Lawrence restaurant . This will take at least four hours to prepare ; ideally , you should start the recipe the day before so you can refrigerate the pastry overnight and prevent it from shrinking during baking . Serve with Pinot Noir , preferably from Burgundy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Pastry : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 lb ( 454 g ) store-bought all-butter puff pastry , thawed&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 egg yolk&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) water&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Brine : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1 L ) water&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? cup ( 60 mL ) kosher salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) brown sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 bay leaf&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 sprigs thyme&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Quails : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 jumbo quails , deboned ( you can find quail at fine butchers , who will also debone it for you on request , although you will have to special order it ahead of time. ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 Tbsp ( 60 mL ) butter , divided&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 shallots , peeled and finely chopped&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) cognac or brandy&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) white wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1L ) good quality chicken stock ( if using a powder base , add 6 sheets of gelatin that have been soaked in cold water to give sticky texture to sauce that can only be achieved with broth derived from bones ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) honey&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Salt and pepper , to taste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 Tbsp ( 15 mL ) cornstarch ( optional ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) water ( optional ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? lb ( 115 g ) foie gras terrine or torchon ( such as Rougi ? from Quebec ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; ? lb ( 230 g ) mild pork sausage , casings removed&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;36 seedless green grapes ( peeled if you have the patience ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Mustard greens or arugula , to garnish&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prepare the puff pastry cases : &lt;/strong&gt; Roll the puff pastry to a thickness of 4 to 5 mm ( a little less than 1/4 inch ) . Using a round ( and preferably fluted ) pastry cutter of 10 cm ( 4 inch ) diameter , cut the pastry into 12 discs . Slightly twist the cutter on a floured worktop to make sure the disc is cut in a perfectly neat shape . The pastry disc should detach easily from the puff pastry sheet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Arrange six of the pastry discs on a Silpat baking mat placed on top of a baking sheet . Beat the egg yolk with the water to make an egg wash , then , using a pastry brush , glaze the discs with the egg wash . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place the other six pastry discs on a floured worktop and cut a hole in the centre of each with a smaller pastry cutter , preferably with a diameter of 6 cm ( 2.5 inches ) . You should now have six pastry rings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Carefully arrange the rings on top of the pastry discs . Glaze with the egg wash and store in the fridge for at least two hours and preferably overnight before baking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat oven to 400 F ( 200 C ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Remove pastry from the fridge and apply another brush of egg wash . Place small ring moulds ( height 5 or 6 cm , or about 2.5 inches ) in the four corners of the baking sheet and place a second baking sheet on top of the moulds . This will help control the rise of the puff pastry shells while baking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bake at 400 F ( 200 C ) for 10 minutes , then reduce the heat to 350 F ( 175 C ) and cook for another 15 minutes . Remove the top baking sheet and bake for a further 10 minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Make sure the base of the pastry shells is well cooked , then remove from the oven and leave to cool on a rack . Reserve until ready to use . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prepare the quails and sauce : &lt;/strong&gt; Make the brine : In a small sauce pot on high heat , bring to a boil 1 cup ( 250 mL ) of the water along with the salt , brown sugar and herbs . Mix in the remaining 3 cups ( 750 mL ) water , transfer to a deep bowl and cool in the refrigerator . Once the brine is chilled , add the deboned quails , making sure they are completely submerged in the liquid . Macerate for 1 hour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During that time , start making the sauce . In a medium saucepan over medium-high heat , melt 2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) of the butter and sweat the shallots for 3 minutes until soft and cooked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deglaze the pan with the cognac and flamb&amp;eacute ; the alcohol , being careful to keep it away from anything that could ignite . Add the white wine and continue cooking until liquid is reduced to &amp;frac14 ; cup ( 60 mL ) . Add chicken stock and continue cooking until you have 2 cups ( 500 mL ) of sauce . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stir in the honey and season with a good pinch of salt and freshly cracked pepper . If at this point your sauce is too thin for your liking , mix the 2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) cornstarch with the 2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) water . Bring sauce back to a simmer and whisk in the cornstarch slurry a little at the time until you achieve your desired consistency . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Set sauce aside until ready to serve . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat oven to 425 F ( 220 C ) . Remove quails from brine and pat dry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cut the foie gras terrine into 6 equal portions ; also divide the sausage meat into 6 equal portions . Wrap the sausage around the foie gras to form a ball , then gently stuff each ball inside each quail . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Re-shape the quails into their original form as much as possible . Transfer them to a baking tray lined with Silpat or parchment paper . Gently truss the quails with butcher twine , making one loop starting from the back to the front of the bird , and tie a knot . This will help the birds hold their shapes during cooking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Season with a little bit of salt and pepper and place in oven . Bake 20 to 25 minutes , depending on the size of the quails . The internal temperature should be 135 F ( 57 C ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Remove the from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes ; and keep warm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a saut&amp;eacute ; pan over medium high heat , melt the remaining 2 Tbsp ( 30 mL ) butter and add the grapes . Lower the heat and cook gently for 4 to 5 minutes until warm all the way through . Add the sauce to the grapes and keep warm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Put the puff pastry cases back in the oven for 2 minutes , then take them out and put them on serving plates . Remove butcher twine from the quails and transfer each one into its dedicated sarcophage ( puff pastry case ) . Spoon sauce around the quails , along with 6 grapes per portion , and garnish with a few leaves of mustard greens or arugula. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 6&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;30001;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30043;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;30079;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;30110;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ?
