Email &lt;a href= " **28;30139;TOOLONG " **46;30169;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Joanne SasvariTue , 18 Feb 2020 19:00:36 **45;30217;TOOLONG ... Gismondi : The nebulous nature of the term terroirhttp : **33;30264;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;30299;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;30335;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210452 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some words are synonymous with wine . Words like chaptalization , corked , cru , fermentation , lees , oaky , oxidized , plonk , pruning , racking , riddling , tannin and yeast &amp;mdash ; but none are more talked about , or controversial , as the term terroir , the all-encompassing French word for the place and factors that influence grapes as they grow . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is not exclusive to wine ; think coffee , chocolate , agave , tea and , lately , cannabis , but wine and terroir can be obsessive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; French wine producers will arrive in Vancouver in little more than a week , and as France is the theme country of the 2020 Vancouver International Wine Festival , you can bet the concept of terroir will be widely explored during their stay . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The notion of terroir is much broader than what has been discussed at nauseam for the last decade or two , where most of the talk has been focused solely on the soil . Is it chalk , or volcanic ? Is it laced with minerals ? Is it deep or shallow ? Is it young or old ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The questions go on forever , but the concept of terroir is more profound and more inclusive of factors beyond the soil . And we should mention it is not exclusive to France . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Climate is a key to terroir , and one needs only look at the worldwide shift to move north or south , depending on which hemisphere you live in , to get to cooler , more extreme vineyard sites thought to be the best medium to express terroir. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Biodynamics have also taught us that the flora and fauna and microflora that thrive near the vines can also have a significant effect on the health of the vines and , eventually , the grapes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As you can see , it&amp;rsquo ; s a bigger story than just soil . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then there is the wild card &amp;mdash ; the human factor . Hundreds of decisions go into winemaking , from when to prune to when to pick to how to ferment your grapes using natural or modified yeas. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are questions about barrels , barrel size , concrete , amphorae , stainless steel , how long to age the wine , and many more . Little discussed but equally important is&amp;nbsp ; tradition and the passing down of information from one generation to another . In the end , it all factors into the terroir equation and , eventually , the wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This month you will hear about the chalk in Champagne , the famous granitic soils of Beaujolais , and the galets roul&amp;eacute ; es ( round pebbles ) of the Rhone Valley . In the Languedoc , the wind and the sun as well as the altitude and distance of your vineyard from the Mediterranean Sea all figure in the terroir , not to mention the aromas of wild herbs from the dry scrubland &amp;mdash ; la garrigue &amp;mdash ; that surrounds the vineyards of the south . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The French might be interested to know that here in British Columbia we are celebrating 30 years of VQA wines . The letters stand for Vintner&amp;rsquo ; s Quality Alliance , but the message is far simpler ; VQA means 100 per cent British Columbia . You have to start somewhere , and guaranteeing the origin of local wines proved to be a watershed moment for B.C. wine producers in 1990. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today our wines are far beyond VQA . We have timidly outlined a few regions and even the odd sub-region , but it is fair to say many of the wines produced locally far exceed their official origins . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That is to say , they are brimming with terroir and sense of place , but we have failed to recognize them because , like many , we can not agree on where and what terroir is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All of which brings us back to the nebulous nature of the term terroir and the brilliance of the concept as expressed by the French . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Terroir is a word that was never meant to be literally translated . In fact , you can only come to understand it when you are standing in a vineyard and you can feel the wind , the sun on your face and the dirt beneath your feet , or when you are drinking a wine that originates from that special site . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Call it what you like , but the best wines in the room this month will reek of terroir and not all will be from France . Best of all , you will notice it when you taste it . Just don&amp;rsquo ; t try to explain it to anyone . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;30365;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30407;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;30443;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30474;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;30510;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30538;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;30574;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Weekend wine picks&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30605;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30641;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Domaine Guisset 2016 , Roussillon , South of France , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $19.99 91/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 3760102322246 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 2016 blends 66 per cent Syrah with 20 per cent Carignan and 14 per cent Grenache , turning out a scant 5800 cases . The vinification is traditional from de-stemmed stalks to the daily dump and reloads of the fermenting fruit at the halfway point . Post-fermentation maceration is 7-10 days , followed by eight months in stainless steel for the Carignan and Grenache and one and two-year-old barrels for the Syrah . The colour is dark , the nose complex and inviting , with an electric red fruit demeanour followed by a stony , mineral finished wrapped into garrigue . A charcuterie plate , grilled beef , or lamb chops would be an excellent match for this real wine , as would a decade in your cellar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30671;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30707;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Ch ? teau Pesqui ? Ventoux Les Terrasses Grenache-Syrah 2018 , Ventoux , Rhone Valley , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $19.99 90/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 3760149591032 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Pesqui&amp;eacute ; Ventoux red grows at roughly 300 m above sea level on various estate terroirs along the hillsides of Mount Ventoux . The stony limestone soils flecked with iron oxide sands and clays offer up a refreshing wine that is organically grown and will be Demeter certified biodynamic next year . The mix is 60/40 Grenache/Syrah macerated 15 days and then aged for several months in stainless steel and cement . Expect ripe and fleshy black raspberry , black cherry , and mulberry tempered by a mineral crushed stone undercurrent and a clean peppery finish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30737;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30773;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;G ? rard Bertrand Saint Chinian Syrah Mourv ? dre 2016 , Languedoc , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $23.99 89/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 351412 0107893 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Saint Chinian is a place made for G&amp;eacute ; rard Bertrand and his love of the Languedoc . Wine has been made there since the Middle Ages , and this Syrah/Mourv&amp;egrave ; dre planted over calcareous/schist soils is dialed . Vinification is traditional , with destemming before a one-month maceration . Only one-third of the wine ages for nine months in barrels ; the rest is kept in large vats to maintain its fruity aspects . I love the smoky , savoury red fruit and black licorice nose . The attack is similar , with smoked meat , espresso , blackcurrant , and prune . When you think it will be big and boisterous , the finish remains fresh with a mineral undercurrent . Impressive for the price . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30803;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30839;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Ch ? teau Argadens Bordeaux Sup ? rieur 2016 , Bordeaux , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $24.99 90/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 3394150048720 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Argadens red is a modern Bordeaux based on the concentration of fruit with a supple , balanced texture . The vineyard average age is now over 30 years old , and its planted to Merlot , Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc sitting on clay-limestone soil in a single plot . The site is the highest among the rolling hills of the Entre-Deux-Mers wine region . The blend is 63/32/5 , almost mirroring plantings in the vineyard . The nose is harmonious , expressing dark fruits with well-integrated oak at this stage ; indeed , it is a wine you can age for five to 10 years . It&amp;rsquo ; s not Palmer or d&amp;rsquo ; Angludet , but there are similarities in style . Real wine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30869;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30905;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Domaine Duseigneur Chateauneuf-du-Pape Catarina 2016 , Rhone Valley , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $67.99 94/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;UPC : &lt;/strong&gt; 3385191000303 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Catarina label is a blend of fruit grown among pebbles , sand , and limestone from three separate plots near the village of Ch&amp;acirc ; teauneuf-du-Pape . On average , the biodynamically farmed vines are 60 years old . It is mostly Grenache , with less than 10 per cent of Syrah , Mourv&amp;egrave ; dre , and Cinsault . The aging is carried out in old French oak demi-muids for 12 months , where the oxygen egress is more critical than any oak flavours . The 2016 specializes in beautiful black raspberry , with a smooth , supple palate and a fresh , mineral base . A classy wine with a long future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;30935;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30977;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;31013;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;31044;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;31080;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;31108;TOOLONG ... about the 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;31144;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; **27;31175;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Half The Sugar combines the skills of cookbook author and healthy food advocate Jennifer Tyler Lee and Stanford University paediatrics professor Anisha Patel . Sprinkle the salt evenly over the cucumber and toss well to combine . Let sit for 15 minutes . Rinse under cold running water , drain and toss with the vinegar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; About 30 minutes before you wish to eat , cook the rice according to the package directions . Set aside , covered , to keep warm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whisk together the soy sauce , sesame oil , and honey in a medium bowl . Cut the fish into 1/2-inch cubes and place in a large bowl with the green onions , sesame seeds , and nori . Add the sauce to the mixture and toss to combine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To serve , set out bowls and have everyone place a scoop of rice in their bowl and then top with some of the poke on one part of the bowl and their choice of shelled edamame , cubed avocado , cubed mango , pickled ginger , wasabi paste , sriracha , and ponzu sauce . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 4 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Wine match&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pok&amp;eacute ; bowls with cubed mango , pickled ginger , wasabi paste , sriracha , and ponzu sauce require a B.C. aromatic white . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;31270;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;31306;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Hatch Dynasty White 2018 , Okanagan Valley , $29.99&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The goal of Dynasty White is extravagant opulence , and it is the perfect ready-to-drink white for this opulent pok&amp;eacute ; bowl . Chowdown Vancouver shines spotlight on sustainable seafoodhttp : **33;31903;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;31938;TOOLONG ... title= " The Chowder Chowdown , presented by the Ocean Wise Conservation Association 's seafood program , sees a selection of B.C. " alt= " The Chowder Chowdown , presented by the Ocean Wise Conservation Association 's seafood program , sees a selection of B.C. 's most-notable chefs compete using their favourite sustainable chowder recipes . " data-portal-copyright= " Leila Kwok " **28;31974;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1214104 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2020 Ocean Wise Chowder Chowdown Vancouver&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Feb. 20 , 7 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Vancouver Aquarium &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; $79 + tax ; &lt;a href= " http : **34;32004;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sustainability isn&amp;rsquo ; t a competition . Rather , it&amp;rsquo ; s a goal that , collectively , we all should be working toward . But , when the sustainability conversation is centred around the &lt;a href= " https : **33;32040;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Chowder Chowdown&lt;/a&gt; . Well , then it&amp;rsquo ; s game on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The annual competition sees 13 of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; most-notable&amp;rdquo ; chefs go head-to-head in a two-hour cooking session to create their favourite seafood chowder recipes in the hopes of taking home top honours in categories such as People&amp;rsquo ; s Choice , Best Beer Pairing &amp;mdash ; and the ultimate honour &amp;mdash ; Chowder Champion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is one of my favourite events , &amp;rdquo ; Chef Dai Fukasaku of &lt;a href= " http : **27;32075;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Fukasaku of Prince Rupert , &lt;/a&gt; who is competing in the year&amp;rsquo ; s competition , says . &amp;ldquo ; It gives us an opportunity to showcase our northwest seafood , and to meet with chefs who share the same philosophy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Taking place Feb. 20 at the Vancouver Aquarium , the event is presented by the Ocean Wise Conservation Association&amp;rsquo ; s seafood program . ( Another event will be held in Toronto on Feb. 26 , after which a coast-to-coast Chowder Champion title will be awarded , according to a news release. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , it&amp;rsquo ; s not just a taste of savoury seafood chowders that are a major draw of the ticketed event . It&amp;rsquo ; s the chance to raise money for the &lt;a href= " https : **33;32104;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Ocean Wise sustainable seafood program&lt;/a&gt; &amp;mdash ; and to offer expanded insight into sustainable seafood , in general . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32139;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32175;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Sustainable seafood is seafood that is fished or farmed with minimal impact to the marine environment , &amp;rdquo ; Stacy Johnston , sous chef for Ocean Wise , explains . &amp;ldquo ; Sustainable seafood from the wild is harvested in a way that limits bycatch of other species , is taken from a healthy fish stock and managed in a proper , responsible manner . Sustainably farmed species are those which require minimal inputs and have the lowest possible potential impacts to other species and important habitats . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sustainably sourced seafood products have the least impact on the ocean and environment &amp;mdash ; and provide buyers with a connection to the people who are procuring it , according to Fukasaku. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; By knowing who harvested our seafood , I can pay utmost respect to the seafood and the ingredients talk by itself , &amp;rdquo ; Fukasaku says . &amp;ldquo ; It has genuine nutrition value , it is local &amp;mdash ; fisherman to table &amp;mdash ; and it is tastier . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sustainability sourced seafood , adds Chef Chris Andraza of Fanny Bay Oysters , who was last year&amp;rsquo ; s co-champion and will be returning this year to defend the title , is no longer an optional idea . It&amp;rsquo ; s a necessity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There should not be any other option at this point , &amp;rdquo ; Andraza says . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; The ocean is the most important part of the planet , it&amp;rsquo ; s the lungs and the only reason we are here . If we overfish and take life out of the ocean , we can be certain to feel that on land . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have to respect nature , and without knowing where our food is coming from , that will never happen . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And the need to support sustainable fishing practices will only intensify as the population grows , Johnston says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Over one billion people depend on seafood for their primary source of protein . As our population continues to grow , we&amp;rsquo ; ll need to depend even more on our oceans to feed us , &amp;rdquo ; Johnston says . &amp;ldquo ; If we continue to support unsustainable fishing practices , we will lose this precious resource and damage our oceans and food supply beyond repair . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At his eatery in Prince Rupert , which is referred to as one of the first sushi restaurants in B.C. to go fully Ocean Wise with its ingredients , Fukasaku makes it a top priority to educate and inform diners about the importance of paying attention to the provenance of one&amp;rsquo ; s food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As an owner-operator of a small restaurant , I try to tell our clients about the importance of traceability in seafood and people appreciate us knowing where everything comes from and who harvested it , &amp;rdquo ; Fukasaku says . &amp;ldquo ; Guests always seem to enjoy food more knowing where it comes from . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32205;TOOLONG ... title= " Chef Dai Fukasaku of Fukasaku of Prince Rupert . " alt= " Chef Dai Fukasaku of Fukasaku of Prince Rupert . " data-portal-copyright= " Simon Racliffe " **28;32241;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1214101 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; For those who are curious about how to become better informed about where their seafood selections come from &amp;mdash ; whether at a restaurant or the grocery store &amp;mdash ; the chefs recommend always looking for the logo of a sustainable seafood organization such as Ocean Wise . And , to ask questions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;&lt;i&gt; " &lt;/i&gt;People have the power to vote with their wallet and to hold their suppliers accountable to where their seafood is coming from and if it is being fished or farmed sustainably , " Johnston says . " By asking questions to your local fish monger , your server and your grocer you can choose whether or not to support sustainable fishing and contribute to the health of our oceans . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Three chef tips for getting seafood right at home&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cooking seafood at home can seem like a daunting task . That&amp;rsquo ; s why we asked three B.C. culinary talents to dish on what often stands between a home chef and perfectly prepared seafood. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s what they had to say : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Overcooking is probably the main thing home cooks get wrong . People are used to the feeling of a well-done chicken and use that as a guideline . Seafood should have a little give to it when you do a touch check . That , and take your seafood out 30 to 60 minutes before cooking to let it come to room temperature . This will help make sure your seafood is perfectly cooked throughout . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;em&gt; -- Stacy Johnston , sous chef for Ocean Wise&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Not utilizing the ingredient 100 per cent . Food ReviewsCanadian Spirits : Distillery industry alive and well in B.C. , beyondhttp : **34;32385;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;32421;TOOLONG ... title= " Roots &amp; Wings Distillery in Langley . " alt= " Roots &amp; Wings Distillery in Langley . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;32457;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1194006 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Canadian craft-spirit industry is growing &amp;mdash ; by the week . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a fact that co-authors Stephen Beaumont and Christine Sismondo say they discovered , a bit unexpectedly , while penning the recent release , Canadian Spirits : The Essential Cross-Country Guide to Distilleries , Their Spirits and Where to Imbibe Them &lt;em&gt; ( $29.95 , Nimbus Publishing Ltd. ) &lt;/em&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32487;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32523;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Canadian craft-distilling scene had been growing like crazy for several years prior to our decision to write the book and we felt it was time somebody documented it , &amp;rdquo ; Beaumont explains . &amp;ldquo ; Little did we know that it would expand further by about 30 per cent between the time we came up with the idea and when we finished the book . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cascade of Canadian spirits really kicked off in 2013 , Beaumont writes in the book , when changes to liquor legislation in B.C. allowed for craft distilleries to be exempt from the more than 160 per cent markup applied by the province through the Liquor Distribution Board &amp;mdash ; &lt;a href= " http : **34;32553;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;so long as they use local ingredients and produce less than 50,000 litres per year . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( If they produce more than that amount , the spirits are subject to a markup applied on a sliding scale. ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other provinces soon followed suit , ushering in a broader boom within the craft-distilling industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the relative youth of the country&amp;rsquo ; s craft spirits hasn&amp;rsquo ; t led to an up-and-coming quality level of said sips , Beaumont assures . In fact , the standards set by the more than 165 craft establishments ( all referred to by the author as &amp;ldquo ; actual distilleries , that aren&amp;rsquo ; t simply taking Neutral Grain Spirits or sourcing spirits from elsewhere and repackaging them as their own&amp;rdquo ; ) featured within the pages of the hardcover guide left the authors &amp;ldquo ; pleasantly surprised , &amp;rdquo ; the longtime drinks writer admits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you have an industry as young as Canadian craft distilling , there is always a worry that you&amp;rsquo ; re going to need to sift through a whole bunch of poorly made products to find the gems , but that was simply not the case , &amp;rdquo ; Beaumont says . &amp;ldquo ; In fact , when we were putting together our &amp;lsquo ; Top 5&amp;rsquo ; lists of various spirits types that appear in the front of the book , there were certainly a lot more candidates than there were spaces . Those were tough decisions ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The book features 56 distilleries in B.C. , a number that Beaumont points out makes the province home to almost one-third of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s distilleries. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The B.C. government has put in place a tax structure for distilleries certified as &amp;lsquo ; B.C. Craft , &amp;rsquo ; which is the most favourable and generous in the country , &amp;rdquo ; Beaumont explains of the booming business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32589;TOOLONG ... title= " Rob Rindt and Rebekah Crowley of Roots &amp; Wings Distillery . " alt= " Rob Rindt and Rebekah Crowley of Roots &amp; Wings Distillery . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32625;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1193999 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32655;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Roots &amp; Wings Distillery&lt;/a&gt; in Langley is one of them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It began as a pet project with a lot of research and scheming , then we hit the point where we had to make the decision on if this was a feasible option for both of us , and luckily it was ; as I could not imagine life any other way now , &amp;rdquo ; Rebekah Crowley , who runs the operation alongside her partner , Rob Rindt , says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The South Langley distillery and tasting room serves up a unique selection of spirits , including vodka , gin and whiskey , each one made using homegrown ingredients from their 30-acre farm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have our standard Vital Vodka , which is a potato- and corn-based vodka ; it&amp;rsquo ; s silky and smooth and is really meant to be enjoyed in a martini , with more flavour than a commercial vodka but without the burn , &amp;rdquo ; Crowley explains . &amp;ldquo ; With that as our base , we have infused-vodka options from &amp;mdash ; coffee to horseradish , to truffle to hops to cranberry. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are also in the process of launching our second gin , but just like our first it is soft on the juniper so it makes a great gin for those that aren&amp;rsquo ; t big on the piney taste of juniper . Then , of course , there are the aged spirits from a young whiskey to a cinnamon whiskey to a barrel-aged old-fashioned , to a bourbon-style whiskey . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Aged brandy , rye whiskey and gin are in the works , as well , with a proposed release date within the next year or so . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m a bit of a whiskey girl , &amp;rdquo ; Crowley says of her preferred sip . &amp;ldquo ; We have a limited-edition young whiskey-ish that was aged for a year in small maple syrup barrels . I have it neat . It is lovely . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Crowley admits that neither she nor Rindt had distilling experience when they first got started , she says that what they lacked in know-how , they made up for in interest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( It&amp;rsquo ; s a ) passion project all the way , &amp;rdquo ; Crowley says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s still a bit surreal that I get to create these great spirits to turn into cocktails for people to enjoy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since opening their tasting room in February 2017 with two flavours , Roots &amp;amp ; Wings has expanded to include a lounge offering 10 different spirits and a &amp;ldquo ; revolving&amp;rdquo ; craft cocktail list , a new addition in 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When asked to summarize the current distilling-industry scene in B.C. , Crowley echoed the idea initially mentioned by the authors of Canadian Spirits that , when it comes to craft-distilling , it&amp;rsquo ; s all about expansion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s fantastic ; the growth over the last few years has been amazing , &amp;rdquo ; she says , pointing toward &amp;ldquo ; higher taxes and fees&amp;rdquo ; as pitfalls in the process and &amp;ldquo ; more resources and events that promote local B.C. distilled spirits&amp;rdquo ; as growth factors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And a resource like Canadian Spirits will likely help promote the industry too . At least , that&amp;rsquo ; s the hope of its co-author. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We see this book as having three purposes : a travel guide for people who might want to pay a visit to a distillery or two as they tour this remarkable country ; a guide to craft spirits that might encourage readers to step out of their comfort zones and discover some truly wonderful , Canadian-made spirits ; and a compendium of the many great and fascinating stories behind the people who built these distilleries , &amp;rdquo ; Beaumont says . &amp;ldquo ; If any one of those , or even two or all three , resonates , then I&amp;rsquo ; ll be happy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Craft distilleries in Metro Vancouver -- and beyond &lt;img class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-1194003 " src= " https : **34;32690;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 700 " height= " 918 " srcset= " https : **30;32726;TOOLONG ... 700w , https : **39;32758;TOOLONG ... 114w , https : **39;32799;TOOLONG ... 229w " sizes= " ( max-width : 700px ) 100vw , 700px " &gt;&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Searching for spirited sips in the Lower Mainland. ? Lawrence&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; 269 Powell St. , Vancouver &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Open for dinner daily &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;More info : &lt;/strong&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;a href= " http : **26;34528;TOOLONG " &gt;stl ... , 604-620-3800 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; On my first Cabane au Sucre dinner , I begin with an idiotic move , throwing back a glass of maple syrup &amp;mdash ; really delicious but , oops . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was at St. Lawrence restaurant where chef/owner J.C . Poirier launched the Quebecois tradition . It wasn&amp;rsquo ; t the authentic country sugar shack experience during maple syrup production season but Poirier&amp;rsquo ; s food was miles better than you&amp;rsquo ; d get at the real thing &amp;mdash ; except perhaps at Martin Picard&amp;rsquo ; s Cabane Au Sucre Pied de Cochon , one of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s best restaurants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Red and white checkered tablecloths covered tables and a server matched with a red plaid shirt . On the table , there were little glasses filled with a dark amber elixir which I thought were aperitifs . But it was maple syrup for amping up the dishes that would come marching out of the kitchen . It was gorgeous artisanal syrup which had been collected in buckets and evaporated over a wood fire , the old-fashioned way , produced by a friend of a friend of Poirier. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Such is the allure of this Quebecois tradition that when Poirier launched the Cabane au Sucre , it was to be a three-evening event with two seatings &amp;mdash ; the $125 tickets sold immediately so he added another two nights . Again , poof ! Gone in a day . The last one was held on Jan. 23 but watch for it again next January . Sugaring off season is in the spring but Poirier thought January was the best chance for snow and maple syrup snow taffy in Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Typically Cabane au Sucre restaurants are informal and family oriented. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Most often , they serve breakfast &amp;mdash ; eggs cooked in maple syrup , sausages , ham , beans , nothing fancy , and lots of beer . It&amp;rsquo ; s meant to be fun , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says . &lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34556;TOOLONG ... title= " A cabane au sucre dinner at St. Lawrence , located at 269 Powell St. in Vancouver . " data-portal-copyright= " Mia Stainsby " **28;34592;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1211279 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; His grandfather , father and brother produce small batches of syrup for family and friends and so for Poirier , it&amp;rsquo ; s nostalgia central ; and Cabane au Sucre at St. Lawrence , as you can imagine , is a big proud deal for him . Guests power through six courses &amp;agrave ; la carte and with each of them , there were family-style sides . Added up , there were 15 different dishes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So ! We started with a cocktail , maple oreilles de crisse in a maple syrup can &amp;mdash ; deep-fried pork rind chips &amp;mdash ; so very yummy ! &amp;mdash ; and maple dinner rolls . Sliced pickled pork tongue sat atop crostini with maple mustard and pickled shallots. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34622;TOOLONG ... title= " Maple oreilles de crisse from St. Lawrence , located at 269 Powell St. in Vancouver . Brussels sprouts with Quebec cheese ; baked navy beans with smoked bacon , onion and garlic maple syrup. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s Quebec&amp;rsquo ; s risotto , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier laughs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;34688;TOOLONG ... title= " Split pea and ham hock soup from St. Lawrence , located at 269 Powell St. in Vancouver . As well as the cocktail , we had a glass of &amp;ldquo ; blue collar beer&amp;rdquo ; and a &amp;ldquo ; Maple Jack . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In Quebec , people might have a shot of Jack Daniels , &amp;rdquo ; Poirier says about the latter . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not the best whisky so I mixed maple syrup and lemon juice with it to make it tasty . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you&amp;rsquo ; re thinking that&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of food going down the gullet , yes , quite true . You can control portions by scaling back on the family-style side dishes but seriously , if you want the authentic experience , you&amp;rsquo ; ll leave groaning and unable to breathe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Typically , there is a lot of food and there&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of drinking and it&amp;rsquo ; s loud , &amp;rdquo ; says Poirier. &amp;ldquo ; Quebec people are loud and excessive when it comes to food and drinking . It&amp;rsquo ; s festive . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And a reality check , maple sap running so freely these days thanks to climate change . Food ReviewsStaff BlogsAnthony Gismondi : B.C. wine of the week , wine to cellar and calendar itemshttp : **35;34922;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;34959;TOOLONG ... title= " University of California 's first institute for organic research and education will be established in the UC 's Agriculture and Natural Resources Division . " alt= " University of California 's first institute for organic research and education will be established in the UC 's Agriculture and Natural Resources Division . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34995;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206339 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Get ready to embrace organics as the world farming community continues marching toward sustainability , organics and biodynamics. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest news , sure to be of interest to British Columbia growers , is the announcement that the University of California&amp;rsquo ; s first institute for organic research and education , which will be established in the UC&amp;rsquo ; s Agriculture and Natural Resources Division to the tune of $1 million . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Organic is the fastest-growing sector of the food economy , but funding for research lags far behind support for conventional agriculture . Farmers interested in transitioning to organic or improving the performance of their organic systems often lack the guidance required to succeed . This endowment will allow UC advisers to work directly with farmers throughout the state to implement the latest in organic farming techniques to be applied quickly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The newly minted Canadian Chapter of the International Wine Law Association ( likely better known by its French acronym AIDV or the Association Internationale des Juristes du Droit de la Vigne et du Vin ) will meet in Vancouver during the upcoming Vancouver International Wine Festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given the multiple jurisdictions in the country , the myriad aspects of law and policy touching the wine industry , AIDV Canada was established to coordinate , communicate and advance knowledge on wine law and policy across the country for agents retailers and winery owners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first conference under the AIDV Canada banner will take place on Feb. 24 in Vancouver , with Chris Wilson of Norton Rose Fulbright and Mark Hicken of Vintage Law Group as co-hosts . For more details , go to &lt;a href= " https : //www.aidv.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;aidv.ca&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;B.C. wine of the week&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35025;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;35061;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tinhorn Creek Oldfield Reserve Merlot 2016 , Okanagan Valley&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $28.99 90/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; UPC : 624802011127 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A B.C. Valentine red that runs long and deep on the palate . Red and black fruits , perfect acidity , and firm , dense , yet almost sweet tannins balance the finish . Already impressive , this is a wine you can cellar for a decade . Serve with a favourite steak cut , a pork roast or a Bolognese pasta dish . They are the reason we continue to change up the menu every week , keeping it fresh for our guests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How would you describe the type of food you like to cook ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; I am not necessarily tied down to a specific type of cuisine or style . I pride myself on cooking what is local , seasonal and sustainable . It is incredible what grows here in B.C. , and sometimes even surprising . I take great pleasure in preserving ingredients for next year ; it gives us a bountiful larder to pull from in the winter months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What might diners not know about you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; I always wear funky socks &amp;mdash ; I am currently rocking my Star Wars socks ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Describe a couple of your most recent creations . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; We deal with a farm in Princeton that does the only pureblood Canadian Wagyu beef . It is super small scale and only produces four animals a year . We&amp;rsquo ; ve made a beautiful tartare dish from that animal and served it with pickled cucumbers from Cropthorne Farms on Westham Island , grated horseradish from Local Harvest in Chilliwack , house-made mustard , and shallots. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What 's your favourite local product and how do you use it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; Tree tips &amp;mdash ; it truly embodies our philosophy here at Wildebeest and the Pacific Northwest . Each tree tip is wildly different from the other . We use tree tips in infused vinegar , house-made mustard , ice cream , infused salt , sugar , sauce , and caramel. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : If there 's one important piece of advice you might have for home cooks , what might that be ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; Get outside of your comfort zone with food : Go to the farmer&amp;rsquo ; s market , buy local and in-season ingredients , learn from a farmer , try new vegetables you may have never heard of , and be a local hero . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35833;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;35869;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; **29;35899;TOOLONG **33;35930;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) canola oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;7 oz ( 200 g ) Wagyu beef&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 ? inch ( 3.5 cm ) piece of fresh horseradish&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) gherkins , small dice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) shallots , small dice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Chili flakes , to taste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) whole grain mustard&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 lemon , juiced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Sea salt , to taste&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 medium eggs&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Warm a saut&amp;eacute ; pan on high heat and add canola oil . Once the oil begins to smoke , quickly sear the meat for a few seconds on all sides . Place in fridge to cool . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Once cooled , shave off seared meat and place into freezer for a minimum of one hour , along with horseradish . Once meat has chilled , slice into 1/4-inch ( 1/2 cm ) strips and then dice into 1/4-inch cubes . Place in a large mixing bowl . Season with salt and add in gherkins , mustard , shallots , chili flakes and lemon juice . Once meat is sufficiently seasoned , place into serving bowls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Crack both eggs to separate the yolks . Make a divot with your spoon in the beef mixture and gently place the yolk in it . Remove horseradish from the freezer and gently microplane over meat . Serve with your favourite potato chips or fresh sourdough toast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 2 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;35965;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;36007;TOOLONG ... national and international food **25;36043;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;36070;TOOLONG ... latest restaurant **28;36106;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;36136;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop/PNG " **28;36360;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210165 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Your designer kitchen may be beautiful , but is it actually functional ? Not if you ask many professional chefs . We chatted with three of them , from three very different restaurants , about what really is essential in a kitchen . What they had to say may just change how you plan the most important room in your home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re set up for speed , so it&amp;rsquo ; s obviously functional , &amp;rdquo ; says Andrew Richardson , executive chef of Toptable Group&amp;rsquo ; s Elisa Steakhouse in Yaletown . Richardson , who also oversees CinCin Ristorante + Bar , was able to design the kitchen at Elisa on a relatively generous budget . It is as elegant as it is efficient . &amp;ldquo ; We just try to build systems to make things easier , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A very different kitchen is the one at Farina a Legna in North Vancouver . Alessandro Vianello , executive chef of Kitchen Table Restaurants , took over the former Il Castello Pizzeria&amp;rsquo ; s tiny , open kitchen , which is dominated by a large pizza oven . He had little time , space or budget to renovate before opening last September , but with a few smart changes , made it into an attractive and user-friendly space . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s remarkable to me how we can pump out so much food from this small kitchen , &amp;rdquo ; Vianello says . &amp;ldquo ; You can do a lot with a small space . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36390;TOOLONG ... title= " For Fairmont Chateau Whistler 's executive chef Isabel Chung , a well-designed workflow and meticulous organization are essential to operations in the hotel 's seven kitchens . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of Fairmont Chateau Whistler " **28;36426;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210167 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , as the Fairmont Chateau Whistler&amp;rsquo ; s executive chef , Isabel Chung oversees seven sprawling kitchens , where 10 head cooks and 100 line cooks prepare food for four restaurants , as well as banquets , in-room dining and a staff cafeteria that feeds 800 people . As if that weren&amp;rsquo ; t challenge enough , the building is 30 years old &amp;ldquo ; and each chef has added something , so it feels cobbled together , &amp;rdquo ; Chung says . Plus , it has features such as supporting walls that are virtually impossible to alter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are things in the building you can and can&amp;rsquo ; t change . Kitchen design is very different now than it was then , very different . You can have all these amazing plans , but when it gets into the space . . . . &amp;rdquo ; She sighs . &amp;ldquo ; We use a lot of kitchen designers , but there are still things that don&amp;rsquo ; t work . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Different as all these kitchens are , though , they have similar needs&amp;mdash ; and chances are , so does your home kitchen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Flow &amp; efficiency&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; At home , 90 per cent of the time , I&amp;rsquo ; m a one-woman show in the kitchen . So it&amp;rsquo ; s my ease of use and logical organization that matters , &amp;rdquo ; says Chung. &amp;ldquo ; Here at the hotel , it has to make sense for each of the stations , and it&amp;rsquo ; s still evolving . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;br&gt; The key element in a commercial kitchen is flow . Things need to be organized logically , so food can be prepared efficiently and safely . Work is done at different stations , which are organized in logical progression&amp;mdash ; a single line , perhaps , or in clusters around a central module where the cooking is done . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36456;TOOLONG ... title= " Executive chef Alessandro Vianello leads his team in a discussion in the kitchen at Farina a Legna . " alt= " Executive chef Alessandro Vianello leads his team in a discussion in the kitchen at Farina a Legna . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of Kitchen Table Restaurants " **28;36492;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210169 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Elisa , the kitchen is essentially split in two . Prep work is done at stations hidden behind a wall , with an area for dishes to the far right . &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; re at the end of the line so a cook can just grab and go , &amp;rdquo ; Richardson says . Plating is done in the open kitchen with its majestic Grillworks Infierno wood-fired grill . In front of the grill is the heated &amp;ldquo ; pass , &amp;rdquo ; where plates stay warm as the line of cooks season , slice and arrange steaks and sides before servers pick them up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Farina a Legna , the built-in pizza oven was both an attractive feature and a real obstacle . &amp;ldquo ; We added some menu items that were challenging with the space , with the oven . We had to set up like a triangle where everything comes to a point , &amp;rdquo ; Vianello says . &amp;ldquo ; We didn&amp;rsquo ; t have an extra oven , so we added a convection oven for prep and two induction burners . And we converted the private dining room so it&amp;rsquo ; s a prep pace . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While food should move easily around a kitchen , those who are cooking it shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have to . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The less distance you have to walk anywhere , the more efficient you&amp;rsquo ; re going to be , &amp;rdquo ; Vianello says . &amp;ldquo ; Have the things you use frequently within arm&amp;rsquo ; s reach so you don&amp;rsquo ; t have to bend over or reach into a cupboard . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Line cooks should be able to do their job &amp;ldquo ; without taking more than a step in any direction , &amp;rdquo ; Chung says . &amp;ldquo ; In a professional kitchen , it&amp;rsquo ; s about spacing and efficiency of space . If everything is not within arm&amp;rsquo ; s length of you , it&amp;rsquo ; s too much . Efficiency of space utilization is the most important thing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Gadgets &amp; gear&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; If there&amp;rsquo ; s one thing professional chefs know , it&amp;rsquo ; s that your kitchen probably has too much stuff in it&amp;mdash ; and chances are , it&amp;rsquo ; s the wrong stuff . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Limit the specialty tools and have tools that can do multiple things , &amp;rdquo ; Vianello says . Think : knives , spoons and tongs , rather than , say , a garlic press , avocado slicer and salad chopper. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At home , Chung loves her gadgets . She has two smokers , numerous countertop appliances , at least four rolling pins and a pantry overflowing with baking gear . ( &amp;ldquo ; I have an ungodly amount of sprinkles , &amp;rdquo ; she says . ) But all of it has a purpose , and all of it is in regular use . &amp;ldquo ; I would not let Marie Kondo touch my kitchen , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; My kitchen has a lot of stuff in it , but it all has a functional use . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In commercial kitchens , functionality is more important than beauty ( fancy wood-fired grills aside ) . Things just need to work . Cooktops need to be hot enough , coolers cold enough , mixers powerful enough to meet the demands of high-volume cookery . That said , chefs consider certain appliances essential that home cooks likely wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t , such as a sous vide circulator or tabletop deep fryer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Natural gas is still the standard for cooktops , but increasingly , induction is becoming the preferred choice . &amp;ldquo ; I love working with induction , &amp;rdquo ; Richardson says . &amp;ldquo ; The big thing for me is no heat pollution . It&amp;rsquo ; s a much cooler environment . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vianello adds : &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; re also portable , so they&amp;rsquo ; re good for a smaller space . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And while constant wear and tear drives many chefs to use inexpensive , easily replaceable pots and pans , Richardson isn&amp;rsquo ; t one of them . &amp;ldquo ; All of our cookware is Le Creuset or Staub . The Staubs are wonderful for retaining heat , &amp;rdquo ; he says , noting that he uses Staub cast iron for Elisa&amp;rsquo ; s famous roast chickens and gooey mac and cheese . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because it gets so hot , it develops a great crust and it stays hot for a really long time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Storage &amp; organization&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Your biggest challenge is also the biggest challenge in a commercial kitchen : storage . &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s never enough of it , &amp;rdquo ; Chung says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Elisa , Richardson makes the most of space with hanging hooks , open shelving , plastic bins and a special rack for cutting boards that lets them slide easily in and out . Pots , pans and plates are stacked neatly with the same styles and sizes kept together . Staff have dedicated drawers for their own tools . And storage bins are on wheels . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s important to take them out so we can clean behind them , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of work . The guys spend a lot of time cleaning up every night . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cleanliness is especially important when you have an open kitchen and nothing is hidden from customers . At Farina a Legna , that was a special challenge because the space was so small . &amp;ldquo ; We added a bulkhead for storage , but it&amp;rsquo ; s also a really nice designed feature with mirrors , &amp;rdquo ; Vianello says . He tucked industrial wire shelving behind the pizza oven and installed open shelving under the counter so plates and other essentials are easy to access . &amp;ldquo ; During service , it looks tidy and nice , &amp;rdquo ; he says , &amp;ldquo ; and we did it on a budget . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Everywhere , dry goods are stored in sealed plastic containers and clearly labelled . &amp;ldquo ; In a commercial kitchen , there are so many people using it that everything has to be labelled , &amp;rdquo ; Chung says . &amp;ldquo ; Otherwise , someone is going to put saffron in the chowder and you&amp;rsquo ; ll be sad . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of course , you likely don&amp;rsquo ; t have to produce dinner for dozens&amp;mdash ; or hundreds&amp;mdash ; of people a day . But there are plenty of aspects of commercial kitchens that you can bring home to yours . As Chung says : &amp;ldquo ; I think there are a lot of situations today where we value design over function . I just don&amp;rsquo ; t think I could live with a show kitchen . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36522;TOOLONG ... title= " The kitchen at Farina a Legna had to be designed around the pizza oven inherited from the pizzeria that it replaced . " alt= " The kitchen at Farina a Legna had to be designed around the pizza oven inherited from the pizzeria that it replaced . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of Kitchen Table Restaurants " **28;36558;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210174 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Five tips for a chef-approved kitchen&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Get rid of anything that is n't actually useful . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Store as much as possible in plastic or glass containers , and label them . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Invest in good-quality knives , pots and appliances . Also consider an induction cooktop , which is as effective as natural gas , but wo n't raise the temperature in your kitchen . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Consider your kitchen 's flow . Are essential tools within arm 's reach ? Do you have to take more than a few steps between sink , fridge , stove and prep area ? If so , it might be time to reconfigure your space . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Make your kitchen as easy to clean as it is to cook in. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;36588;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;36630;TOOLONG ... unplanned kitchen reno becomes a serene **27;36665;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;36694;TOOLONG ... finishes and functional features make this kitchen one for the family of the **27;36729;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;36758;TOOLONG ... fare from chef David Robertson 's new **29;36793;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Joanne SasvariSat , 08 Feb 2020 14:44:58 **45;36824;TOOLONG ... Homes and DesignMadeleines : French butter cakes are the perfect anytime treathttp : **35;36871;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;36908;TOOLONG ... title= " Classic French Madeleines from French Pastry 101 by Betty Hung , Page Street Publishing Co. " alt= " Classic French Madeleines from French Pastry 101 by Betty Hung , Page Street Publishing Co. " data-portal-copyright= " Betty Hung " **28;36944;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1208028 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whether you&amp;rsquo ; re hosting a fancy dinner party or just having the neighbours over for coffee , nothing impresses your guests like a plate of madeleines straight from the oven . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love madeleines , &amp;rdquo ; says Betty Hung , co-owner of Beaucoup Bakery and author of the Taste Canada Award-winning French Pastry 101 ( Page Street Publishing Co. ) . &amp;ldquo ; They are like a little treat when you don&amp;rsquo ; t feel like a big , massive dessert . They&amp;rsquo ; re halfway between a cake and a cookie . They&amp;rsquo ; re rich , and not as dry as a cookie . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These sweet , buttery , shell-shaped pastries are a classic of French baking , with a delicate taste and comforting texture that makes them something you will want to reach for again and again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No one is quite sure when or where the madeleine originated , although it&amp;rsquo ; s generally believed they came from Lorraine , in northeastern France , sometime in the early 18th century . But these days , you&amp;rsquo ; ll find them everywhere from Michelin-starred restaurants in Paris to the Starbucks in your local suburban mall . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They are simple&amp;mdash ; but not that simple&amp;mdash ; to make . They start with a sponge-like batter called a genoise , and get most of their lift and volume from beaten eggs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Key is finding the proper baking pan with shell-shaped wells called a moule , which fittingly means both &amp;ldquo ; mould&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; mussel . &amp;rdquo ; Then your challenge is to achieve the distinctive hump that is the mark of a properly baked madeleine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the secrets to making good madeleines is you should make the batter ahead of time and chill it , for flavour development , &amp;rdquo ; Hung says . &amp;ldquo ; The gluten gets a chance to relax and the flour absorbs all the moisture . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Madeleines are best enjoyed as soon as they&amp;rsquo ; ve been baked , as they get stale quickly . A good idea is to scrape the batter into a piping bag and keep it in the fridge ( making sure the ends are tightly closed , of course ) , and just bake a few at a time . The batter will keep for up to three days and it&amp;rsquo ; s super stylish to bake them &amp;agrave ; la minute for your guests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And if plain vanilla seems boring , you can also switch them up with different flavours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You can do lemon madeleines with lemon zest , and with a lemon glaze made with icing sugar , &amp;rdquo ; Hung suggests . You can also flavour the batter with gingerbread spices , rosewater , lavender , orange , matcha , almond or savoury flavours like parmesan , chilies and herbs . You can also dip madeleines in chocolate or mix chocolate chips , fresh berries or chopped nuts into the batter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Best of all , you can enjoy madeleines just about any time you like , for your mid-morning break , your afternoon tea , during cocktail parties or after a long , formal feast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In Paris , they&amp;rsquo ; re available every day , &amp;rdquo ; Hung says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a nice treat when you&amp;rsquo ; re having coffee or tea . I can eat them any time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Recipe : Vanilla Madeleines&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Recipe from French Pastry 101 by Betty Hung , Page Street Publishing Co . Since madeleines are best fresh out of the oven , you can keep the batter in the fridge for a couple of days and bake as needed . Note that you will need a special madeleine pan for this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Makes 24 cookies &lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;1 ? / ? cups ( 200 g ) all-purpose flour&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;2 ? tsp ( 8 g ) baking powder&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; ? tsp salt&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; ? cup ( 150 g ) granulated sugar&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; ? vanilla bean , split and seeds scraped&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;3 large eggs , room temperature&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; ? cup ( 113 g ) unsalted butter , melted and cooled to room temperature&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt; ? / ? cup + 1 tbsp ( 75 g ) whole milk , at room temperature&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Powdered sugar , for garnish ( optional ) &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a medium bowl , whisk together the flour , baking powder and salt . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a separate bowl , measure the sugar and mix in the vanilla seeds with your fingers to evenly distribute them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a large mixing bowl , beat the eggs and sugar vigorously until it becomes frothy , about 2 to 3 minutes . Fold in the dry ingredients with a spatula until the flour is just incorporated . Add in the melted butter and milk , and fold until they&amp;rsquo ; re incorporated . Cover and rest the batter in the fridge for at least 2 hours , preferably overnight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When you&amp;rsquo ; re ready to bake , preheat the oven to 500&amp;deg ; F ( 250&amp;deg ; C ) . Generously butter the wells of the madeleine pans , dust with flour and tap out the extra . Fill a piping bag with batter and pipe it into the pan . If you prefer , you can also spoon the batter into the moulds . Once filled , lightly tap the pan on the counter to level the batter and remove any large air pockets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bake them for 3 minutes , then lower the temperature to 425&amp;deg ; F ( 220&amp;deg ; C ) and bake for 7 to 8 minutes more . Be careful not to over-bake them ; the edges should be golden and the tops should spring back when you press them with your finger . &lt;br&gt; While they are still warm , turn the madeleines out onto a cooling rack . Dust with powdered sugar , if desired . Serve warm ; they are best served the day they are baked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tip : To melt the butter , place it in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water . This is the easiest way to melt butter without having to worry about it boiling over or burning . You can also use a microwave . Place the butter in a microwave-safe bowl and heat for 30 to 40 seconds on high , watching carefully so it does not boil over and spatter. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;36974;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;37016;TOOLONG ... fare from chef David Robertson 's new **29;37051;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; Joanne SasvariSat , 08 Feb 2020 14:16:48 **45;37082;TOOLONG ... Homes and DesignAnthony Gismondi : Wines to woo and wow this Valentine 's Dayhttp : **37;37129;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;37168;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;37204;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206251 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today we preview several wine styles that you might consider for Valentine&amp;rsquo ; s Day along with some matching food ideas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you are planning a night at home &amp;mdash ; which for most wine drinkers usually means more wine for less money &amp;mdash ; you have plenty of time to select the appropriate wine . We also offer some thoughts on food to support the wines , and vice versa , and keep it simple but fun . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s fair to say the cooking at home can be a challenge for those not used to it , but our advice remains steady : keep the menu simple and stick to comfort dishes and the evening will be a success . Failing that takeout is equally acceptable , especially given that you can buy nearly anything you desire already prepared and get it delivered to your door . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ros&amp;eacute ; is always a fun wine at Valentine&amp;rsquo ; s , and we begin with highly affordable and delicious drinking &lt;strong&gt;G ? rard Bertrand C ? te Des Roses Ros ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( $24.95 ) &lt;/em&gt; . Ros&amp;eacute ; is also food friendly , allowing you to serve it with sushi , Jamon , cheese , or even a whole-roasted chicken or pork tenderloin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pinot Noir will be a big seller on the 14th , given its rich , round , supple textures and voluptuous fruit flavours . There&amp;rsquo ; s plenty to choose from in B.C. or further south from Oregon or California . Duck , mushrooms , fowl , and root vegetables all work with Pinot and its soft tannins . The ultimate bargain pick is the &lt;strong&gt;Santa Carolina Pinot Noir Reserva&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( Leyda Chile , on sale at $10.99 ) &lt;/em&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If there is one day made for sparkling wine with a highly attractive ros&amp;eacute ; colour , it is Valentine&amp;rsquo ; s Day . Among my current ros&amp;eacute ; Champagne favourites are the &lt;strong&gt;Louis Roederer Brut Ros ? Champagne 2013&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( $97.99 ) &lt;/em&gt; . A rare infusion style ros&amp;eacute ; made with Pinot Noir grapes that sit around in the tank for 7-10 days before joining some fermenting Chardonnay . Brut&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( $99.99 ) &lt;/em&gt; with its light raspberry salmon colour and nutty , citrus , creamy raspberry aromas and creamy strawberry , baked apple flavours should not be missed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider matching your sparkling ros&amp;eacute ; with store-bought or homemade stuffed pasta . Ravioli , agnolotti or tortellini stuffed with your favourite romantic fillings could include ricotta cheese , mushrooms , lobster or butternut squash . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If there is to be meat , there is nothing simpler or tastier than grilled T-bone steaks or veal chops . Add a Caesar salad and let that big red wine fill in the edges . Any number of California Cabernet Sauvignon will fit the bill , as well as local Cabernet Franc , Merlot or Meritage . We like &lt;strong&gt;Bartier Bros . Cabernet Franc Cerqueira Vineyard &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( &lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;Okanagan Valley , $25.99 ) &lt;/em&gt; , &lt;strong&gt;Rodney Strong Cabernet Sauvignon 2016&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( Sonoma County , California , $27.49 ) &lt;/em&gt; , &lt;strong&gt;Stags ' Leap Cabernet Sauvignon 2015&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( Napa Valley , California , $69.99 ) &lt;/em&gt; , or &lt;strong&gt;Phantom Creek Estates Phantom Creek Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon 2016&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( Oliver , $80 ) &lt;/em&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For extra-added visual impact , not to mention some flavour enhancement , we suggest you decant all the still wines a minimum of 15 to 30 minutes before serving . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dessert should be equally simple as dinner . Strawberries and fresh cream , pannacotta , cr&amp;egrave ; me br&amp;ucirc ; l&amp;eacute ; e , cheesecake , or a few well-chosen high-quality chocolates and you are all set . Now , the rest is up to you . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;37234;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;37276;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;37312;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;37343;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;37379;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;37407;TOOLONG ... 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;37443;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Weekend wine picks&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;37474;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;37510;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;G ? rard Bertrand C ? te Des Roses Ros ? 2018 , Languedoc , France&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $24.95 89/100 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; UPC : 3514123111002 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; C&amp;ocirc ; te des Roses is a celebration of the Mediterranean lifestyle , something Gerard Bertrand has done with style for three decades . This dish is amped up with Korean gochujang chili paste , but you could just as easily use Sichuan doubanjiang. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38073;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38109;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Spicy Stir-Fried Mi Fun with Gochujang&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 oz ( 175 g ) dried rice vermicelli&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;16 to 20 medium shrimp , about 8 oz ( 220 g ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/4 cup ( 60 mL ) cornstarch&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 chives&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) sesame oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1-inch piece of ginger , peeled and thinly shredded&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;11/4 cups ( 120 g ) soybean sprouts , trimmed&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) gochujang&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 ? tbsp ( 50 mL ) sake rice wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;38139;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Put the rice vermicelli in a bowl , and add enough boiling water to cover . Leave to soak for 10 minutes , then drain well . If the noodles are very long , cut in half . Peel the shrimp , cutting into each to remove the vein . Sprinkle with cornstarch , rubbing it in and then rinsing it off . Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels . Add the shrimp and fry until cooked through , about 3 to 4 minutes . Season with salt , if necessary . Add the chives and bean sprouts , and toss to combine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 2 servings. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Wine match&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spicy Stir-Fried Mi Fun with Gochujang , a thick , sticky condiment that&amp;rsquo ; s spicy with a concentrated pungent in flavour , call for wines higher in residual sugar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38166;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38202;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;JoieFarm A Noble Blend 2018 , Okanagan Valley , $25.90&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Juicy , ripe pear fruit with a hint of sweetness balanced with acidity and pepper that will easily take on this dish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38232;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38268;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tightrope Winery Riesling 2017 , Naramata Bench , Okanagan Valley , $22&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Honey , green apples , and pear flavours are the key to balancing the spicy and pungency of the Gochujang coated noodles. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;38298;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;38340;TOOLONG ... from wine expert Anthony **29;38376;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;38407;TOOLONG ... about B.C. **26;38443;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;38471;TOOLONG ... 2020 Vancouver International Wine **29;38507;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;38538;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Email &lt;a href= " **28;38567;TOOLONG " **46;38597;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Anthony GismondiFri , 07 Feb 2020 19:00:57 **45;38645;TOOLONG ... Day recipes : 8 sweet , savoury creationshttp : **31;38692;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38725;TOOLONG ... title= " Satisfy your sweet tooth this Valentine 's Day . Strawberry &amp;amp ; Rose Hearts created by Betty Hung of Beaucoup Bakery. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38761;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1200742 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;If there 's any one thing that 's universally beloved , it 's probably food . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;That 's why we decided to mark this Valentine 's Day by asking a few chefs and companies -- in Vancouver and beyond -- to share their favourite recipes of the moment . &lt;/span&gt; You know , the ones that they ( or their patrons ) can&amp;rsquo ; t get enough of or are hungry to eat on repeat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From sweet spring rolls to even sweeter heart-shaped cookies , here are five lovely recipes to cook up for your loved ones &amp;mdash ; or just for yourself &amp;mdash ; come Feb. 14. &lt;/p&gt; **28;38791;TOOLONG &lt;img src= " https : **34;38821;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38857;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Pandan Spring Rolls&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Created by chef Yen Do of House Special &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) whole milk&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 oz ( 58 g ) fresh chopped pandan leaves&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;5 whole eggs&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/4 cup ( 60 mL ) white sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) cornstarch&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) all-purpose flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;15-20 sheets of spring roll pastry&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Simmer milk in a saucepan . Remove from heat before milk comes to a boil . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whisk eggs , sugar , flour , and cornstarch together in a mixing bowl until sugar is fully dissolved &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Blend fresh pandan leaves with roughly 4 oz ( 115 mL ) of water . Strain through a cheese cloth to extract pandan juice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On low heat , incorporate the egg mixture into simmered whole milk . When thickened , slowly fold in pandan extract . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spoon a small serving of the pandan custard onto one spring roll pastry . Roll into a spring roll . Repeat until custard is used up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Enjoy with condensed milk or confectionary sugar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 4-6. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38887;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38923;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Strawberry &amp; Rose Hearts&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Created by&amp;nbsp ; Betty Hung of Beaucoup Bakery &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Cookie dough&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2/3 cup ( 160 mL ) unsalted butter , softened&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/4 tsp ( 1 mL ) salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/4 cup ( 60 mL ) granulated sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 1/2 tsp ( 12 1/2 mL ) light brown sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) egg whites , room temperature&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) pure vanilla extract&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) all-purpose flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/4 cup ( 60 mL ) light rye flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;38953;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3/4 cup ( 180 mL ) strawberry chocolate , preferably Valrhona Strawberry Inspiration&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) cocoa butte&lt;/em&gt; r &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 1/2 tsp ( 7 1/2 mL ) canola , or other neutral tasting oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **36;38989;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Dried rose petals&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat oven to 325 F ( 160 C ) and place a rack in the middle . Line two baking sheets with parchment paper . Use a separate sheet of parchment paper to make a stencil for the heart shapes you are going to pipe the cookie dough onto later ( about 2 inch or 5 cm large heart rings spaced 1 1/2-inches or 4 cm apart ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To make the dough , beat the butter , salt , both sugars in a stand mixer with the paddle attachment at medium speed for 2-3 minutes . Add in the egg whites , vanilla , and beat on medium speed until the mixture is cohesive . Add in the flour and rye flour and mix until just well incorporated , scraping down the bowl as needed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Transfer the dough into a piping bag fitted with a 1 cm open star piping tip . Place the stencil parchment paper underneath the clean parchment paper on the baking sheet . You should be able to see the heart shapes on the paper below . Slowly pipe cookies onto the parchment lined baking sheet into the shapes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bake the cookies one tray at a time for 20-25 minutes in the preheated oven until the edges are golden brown , rotating the tray halfway through . Cool the cookies to room temperature before glazing them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To make the glaze , heat the ingredients in a double boiler over low heat until it reaches 30-35 C ( 86 to 95 F ) , while stirring the chocolate , and careful not to overheat it . Take it off the heat when the glaze is ready . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dip each cookie half and let the excess drip off . Place the cookies back onto the parchment lined tray . Before the chocolate sets , sprinkle each one with crushed dried rose petals . Let the chocolate set and cool completely before serving . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 20 cookies&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;39027;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;39063;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; **34;39093;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Created by Claire Livia Lassam of LIVIA FORNO e VINO &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 baguette&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;8 good-quality anchovies , packed in oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 cup ( 125 mL ) extra virgin olive oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 cup ( 125 mL ) parsley , finely chopped&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 large balls fresh mozzarella , thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat the oven to 425&amp;nbsp ; F ( 220 C ) . Without ever cutting fully through the baguette , cut it into 1/2-inch ( 1.3 cm ) slices , so it can fan open but stays one large baguette. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Slide a slice of mozzarella in each cut in the baguette , breaking them down if they&amp;rsquo ; re too much larger than the bread . Place them in a heatproof mixing bowl . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat the cream in a small saucepan until it just boils . Turn off the heat and allow the cream to sit for 20 seconds . Pour the cream through a fine-meshed sieve into the bowl with chocolate . With a wire whisk , slowly stir the cream and chocolate together until the chocolate is completely melted . These will keep refrigerated for weeks , but serve them at room temperature . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Makes 48 truffles. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Madagascar vanilla and lime-marinated pineapple&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Created by chef Paul Moran of Dinner With A View &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 whole pineapple&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;.39 oz ( 10 g ) vanilla sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 lime&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1 L ) 17 per cent fat coconut milk&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;9 oz ( 260 g ) coconut oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;7 oz ( 200 g ) raw sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 1/2 oz ( 100 g ) gluten free all-purpose flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 1/2 oz ( 100 g ) shredded coconut&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;10 freeze-dried blackberries&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 bunch fresh mint&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Begin by heating the coconut milk , 160g coconut oil and 100g raw sugar . Stir the liquid mixture into the dry mixture until thoroughly combined . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat a lightly oiled frying pan on medium-high heat . Pour 1/4 cup of the pancake batter on the pan and cook until the bottom side is browned for about two minutes . Flip and cook for another one minute . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Cranberry Sauce&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) cranberries&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) white sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) orange juice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Put together the sugar and orange juice in a sauce pan and heat until the sugar is all dissolved .
