Remove from heat and place sauce in a bowl to cool down before storing in containers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Dry Spice Mix ( for fried chicken batter ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) Cajun Spice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) paprika powder&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) garlic powder&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 tsp ( 2 1/2 mL ) cayenne pepper powder&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 tsp ( 2 1/2 mL ) black pepper&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Put all the ingredients in a mixing bowl and mix well . Set aside and make sure to keep them dry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Buttermilk Fried Chicken&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 lbs ( 32 oz ) chicken thigh&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) buttermilk&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 egg&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) dry spice mix ( from the recipe above ) &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) sugar&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 tbsp ( 30 mL ) pickle juice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) all purpose flour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a mixing bowl , combine buttermilk , egg , salt , sugar and pickle juice together and mix well until all the ingredients are combined . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Coat the chicken thigh with the dry spice mix until they are uniformly coated . In a container , cover the chicken thigh with the buttermilk mix , seal and marinade for at least two hours up to eight hours in the fridge . After marinating , drain the chicken thigh , keep the buttermilk mixture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Coat the marinated chicken thigh with flour , press the flour onto the chicken so it sticks . Put the flour coated chicken back into the buttermilk mixture and , repeat with the flour one more time . Set aside the double-coated chicken and let it rest for five minutes , do the same with the rest of the chicken thighs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat cooking oil in a frying pan on medium heat until the temperature hits 375 F ( 190 C ) then carefully place the double-coated chicken into the oil . Turn the chicken a few times to cook and brown evenly , until the meat is thoroughly cooked and the centre of the meat reaches 165 F ( 74 C ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After cooked , let the chicken rest for two minutes before sprinkling a handful of dry spice mix on the fried chicken to season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;To Serve : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On a dinner plate , stack three cornmeal-buttermilk pancakes on top of each other . Serve with maple syrup and house-made chicken gravy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves four . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;39429;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;39471;TOOLONG ... latest restaurant **28;39507;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;39537;TOOLONG ... national and international food **25;39573;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **28;39600;TOOLONG " **35;39630;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;39667;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Wilson : Easy and romantic Valentine 's Day dinnershttp : **33;39821;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;39856;TOOLONG ... title= " Rustic olive toasts complement Chef Ned Bell 's simple stew of mussels , caramelized onions and cherry tomatoes . " data-portal-copyright= " Kevin Clark " **28;39892;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204781 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you&amp;rsquo ; re spending Valentine&amp;rsquo ; s Day at home &amp;aacute ; deux , either of today&amp;rsquo ; s easy-to-prepare seafood dishes &amp;mdash ; a rustic mussel stew or elegant fish fillets fish en papillote &amp;mdash ; is sure to kindle romance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chef Ned Bell , who created the first recipe , is a big fan of bivalves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Mussels are farmed in protective coves and cultivated on ropes , floating rafts and nets , &amp;rdquo ; he explains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As filter feeders , they will leave the ocean cleaner than they found it . They are also incredibly versatile &amp;mdash ; they can be steamed in white wine , beer or even apple juice in less than five minutes . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s also hard to beat a fillet of fish surrounded by aromatic vegetables and cooked in parchment . En papillote , as we say in French , is one of the most effective way of steaming because it seals in flavours . " alt= " Photograph by Kevin Clark . " data-portal-copyright= " Kevin Clark " **28;39988;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204779 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Mussel Stew with Caramelized Onions and Olive Toast&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; This fragrant stew with its crusty toasts comes together in no time . After purchasing mussels , place them in a bowl , cover loosely with a damp towel and store in the coolest part of the fridge . Don&amp;rsquo ; t clean them until you&amp;rsquo ; re ready to cook . ( Adapted from Lure : Sustainable Seafood Recipes from the West Coast by Ned Bell with Valerie Howes , Figure 1 , 2017. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2lb ( 1 kg ) live mussels&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Olive oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 medium red onion , peeled and thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cups ( 500 mL ) pitted Ni ? oise or Kalamata olives&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 thick slices crusty artisan bread&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 large garlic cloves , peeled and minced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 cup ( 250 mL ) cherry tomatoes&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 cup ( 125 mL ) dry white wine or water&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) chopped flat-leaf parsley&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Zest and juice of 1 lemon&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rinse mussels under cold water and discard any that are broken or are open and won&amp;rsquo ; t close when tapped . Scrub off any debris and pull off beards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat 3 tbsp ( 45 mL ) oil in a large pot over medium-low . Add onions and saut&amp;eacute ; for 20 to 30 minutes , stirring often , until they turn a deep golden brown . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , preheat broiler and set oven rack to the topmost position . Pulse olives in a food processor into a coarse pur&amp;eacute ; e. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brush one side of each bread slice with olive oil . Set it on a baking sheet and broil for 1&amp;nbsp ; to 2&amp;nbsp ; minutes , until golden brown . Top each toast with a spoonful of chopped olives . Turn off broiler and return toasts to oven to keep warm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Increase heat under onions to medium . Add garlic and 1 tbsp ( 15 mL ) oil and saut&amp;eacute ; for 2 minutes . Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes , until softened . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add the wine , bring to a boil over medium-high heat and add mussels . Cover and cook for 2&amp;nbsp ; to 3&amp;nbsp ; minutes or until mussels have just opened . Remove pot from heat and discard any that are unopened . Stir in parsley and lemon zest and juice . Serve with olive toasts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 2&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Fillet of Fish in Parchment&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; These parchment packets are Valentine&amp;rsquo ; s Day gifts in themselves , and when you cut them open the heady aromas will tell your guests how much you love them . ( Adapted from The Pleasures of Cooking for One by Judith Jones , Knopf , 2009. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Olive oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 to 6 smallish new potatoes , cut into ? -inch ( 1.3 cm ) slices&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 -- 6 oz ( 175 g ) skinless fillets of halibut , salmon or red snapper&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 small zucchini , cut into julienne strips&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 medium carrot , peeled and cut into very thin julienne strips&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 green onions , white and tender green parts , cut into strips&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 ( ? -inch or 6 mm ) slices fresh ginger , peeled and cut into julienne strips&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 splashes white wine&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Minced fresh parsley , chives , tarragon or and/or summer savoury&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Preheat oven to 425 F ( 230 C ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Line a small sheet pan with foil , oil it lightly and spread on potato slices in a single layer . Season with salt and pepper and roast for 10 minutes , turning once . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For each serving , cut an 18-inch ( 46 cm ) piece of parchment paper , join the short ends and fold it in half , creasing the centre . Place paper on a work surface , lift top layer and place fish alongside fold . Season fish and top it with zucchini , carrot , green onions , and ginger . Season again and splash with enough wine to bath the fish lightly . Arrange pre-roasted potatoes slices on top and sprinkle herbs over all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bring top piece of parchment down over the ingredients , join the edges and fold them in twice . Pleat parchment all around , forming an airtight semicircular packet . If it gaps , secure with large metal paper clips. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place packets on a sheet pan and roast for 12 minutes . Test with a skewer ; if it goes in easily , the fish is done . Roast a minute or two longer if needed . Present packets on dinner plates and snip the centre open with scissors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 2&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Kitchen Hack : Reheating leftover fish&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; To reheat cooked fish fillets , place them on a wire rack set in a rimmed baking sheet , cover with foil and put in a 275 F ( 135 C ) oven until the fish registers 125 C to 130 C ( 52 C to 54 C ) . A 1-inch ( 2.5 cm ) thick filet will take about 15 minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;40018;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;40060;TOOLONG ... latest restaurant **28;40096;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;40126;TOOLONG ... national and international food **25;40162;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **28;40189;TOOLONG " &gt;S ... our quarterly wine and food **32;40219;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;40253;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? Email &lt;a href= " **28;42069;TOOLONG " **46;42099;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Mia StainsbyWed , 05 Feb 2020 19:00:24 **45;42147;TOOLONG ... BlogsKaren Barnaby : Fried rice an easy family favouritehttp : **31;42194;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;42227;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " Karen Barnaby " **28;42263;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1200306 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A friend of mine returned from teaching in Beijing and asked me if I was an egg first , or an egg last person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I immediately knew that he was referring to cooking fried rice . I told him that I started as an egg first person , but had switched to being an egg last person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The history I have with fried rice is long and filled with failures and triumphs . My family would venture to the Marco Polo restaurant a few times a year and we rarely strayed from almond chicken guy ding , sweet and sour pork , a vegetable chow mein , egg rolls , and fried rice . The rice was brown from soy sauce and deliciously salty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My mother would occasionally cook what I&amp;rsquo ; ll term as Chinese-inspired food and serve it with Dainty Rice Chinese-Style rice in a can . I could barely contain my excitement when the red and white box appeared because I was allowed to make it . The rice was vacuum-sealed and made a satisfying hiss when pierced by the can opener . Inside the can , there were firm little grains of rice . They were transformed into delicious plump grains after being heated in a frying pan with the seasoning packet , oil , and water . It was a miracle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In my teens , my peers also had a fascination with fried rice . While other teens were drinking and getting high on Friday night , we were at each other&amp;rsquo ; s homes , trying to crack the code . We used converted rice , or instant rice , because that&amp;rsquo ; s what was in our parent&amp;rsquo ; s kitchen cupboards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The converted rice was usually undercooked , overcooked , or burned , and the instant rice only resembled rice in appearance . Add to that big glugs of Western soy sauce and you have a brown , salty mess . We didn&amp;rsquo ; t care , we thought we were culinary geniuses. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Across from my high school , Ming&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant was mobbed at lunch and after school with obnoxious teens , yelling out orders for french fries , fried rice and toast . One late afternoon , I was sitting in view of the kitchen and saw Mrs. Ming take a large container out of the fridge filled with beautifully separate grains of rice that were dyed brown by soy sauce and dotted with flecks of green onion . Mr. Ming tossed a scoop into his smoking wok and in seconds , a beautiful dish of fried rice was in front of me . Cook rice , coat it with soy sauce , refrigerate . That was the secret . I could now rest in peace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My Thai mentor Vanipha shook me out of my Canadian-Chinese fried rice daze . I watched her fry garlic in oil until it was golden brown then scramble in an egg . She added cooked rice and fried it until it was glistening with oil . Fish sauce , a drop of oyster sauce&amp;shy ; , a liberal amount of black pepper , green onions , and finely diced seeded tomato were the crowning touch . This was my second coming of fried rice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My current favourites are the pristinely white Chinese-style fried rice seasoned only with salt , and it&amp;rsquo ; s opposite , kimchee fried rice . New favourites are yet to be discovered and while I&amp;rsquo ; m waiting , I&amp;rsquo ; ll get a package of Dainty Rice to see if it lives up to my memory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **30;42293;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **37;42325;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; **28;42364;TOOLONG &lt;img src= " https : **34;42394;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;42430;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Basic Egg Fried Rice&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you want to add cooked , leftover meats , fry them in the oil before anything else is added . It is important to use cold , cooked rice that has been refrigerated for 24-72 hours . Break up the clumps by wetting your hands and squeezing them to separate the rice into grains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 Tbsp ( 45 mL ) neutral flavoured vegetable oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1 L ) cold , cooked rice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;42460;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 eggs , beaten&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 green onions , thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat a large , heavy frying pan on high heat until smoking . Add the oil , swirl it around the pan then add the rice . Spread out and toss the rice with a spatula until heated through . Season with salt , I usually start with 1/4 tsp ( 1 mL ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Make a well in the rice and add the eggs , stir rapidly until the eggs are half done then incorporate the rice . When the egg is evenly distributed stir in the green onion and serve immediately . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Note : &lt;/strong&gt; If you want to be an egg first person , scramble the egg in the pan first and when it&amp;rsquo ; s half cooked , add the rice . My favourite egg last method is drizzling the egg over the rice and stirring until it is cooked on to the grains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 2 as a main , 4 as a side&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;42487;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;42523;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Sheet Pan " Fried " Brown Rice with Shiitake Mushrooms and Kale&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The results are excellent with this dish and there is no stovetop to clean . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 Tbsp ( 60 mL ) neutral flavoured vegetable oil , divided&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2-inch piece of fresh ginger , peeled and minced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;2 cloves garlic minced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1/2 lb ( 250 g ) fresh shiitake mushrooms , stems removed , caps thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;6 cups ( 1.5 L ) coarsely chopped curly kale leaves&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;pinch of salt&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;4 cups ( 1 L ) cold cooked brown rice&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 Tbsp ( 45 mL ) soy sauce&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;3 green onions thinly sliced&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;1 tsp ( 5 mL ) sesame oil&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;toasted sesame seeds&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heat the oven to 500 F ( 260 C ) . 500 F is not a typo . Place an 11 x 17-inch ( 28 x 43 cm ) rimmed sheet pan in the oven while it&amp;rsquo ; s heating . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Place 3 Tbsp ( 45 mL ) of the oil in a large bowl . Add the ginger , garlic , mushrooms , kale and a large pinch of salt . Toss to coat with the oil . Remove the baking sheet from the oven and spread the mixture evenly on it . Bake for 5 minutes . The kale will be brown and crispy in spots . Stir and redistribute the mixture . Bake for 3 minutes longer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add the rice to the vegetable mixture and drizzle with the remaining oil and soy sauce . Stir until well mixed and spread out evenly . Bake for 5 minutes , the rice should be hot and tender . Stir in the green onion and sesame oil . Garnish with the sesame seeds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Serves 2 as a main , 4 as a side&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;42553;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? ( 5 sheets ) powdered gelatin &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 1 &amp;frac14 ; cups ( 310 mL ) heavy cream &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 3/4 cup + 1 tbsp. Suzuki puts himself under microscope for new show on aginghttp : **35;44275;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;44312;TOOLONG ... title= " David Suzuki undergoes an eye exam , one of the many tests he put his 83-year-old self through for a new The Nature of Things episode on aging . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of CBC " **28;44348;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1217817 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; When his boss at the CBC first brought up the idea of aging as a topic for &lt;a href= " https : **33;44378;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The Nature of Things&lt;/a&gt; , host &lt;a href= " https : **33;44413;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;David Suzuki&lt;/a&gt; was interested but not sold on the concept . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The plan presented to the scientist and environmentalist was about how science was going to make us all live way , way longer than the average 84 years for women and 80 years for men . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I looked at the proposal . And it was a typical thing . You know , science is discovering ways of getting fruit flies to live 50 per cent longer , and they&amp;rsquo ; re doing all of these fancy DNA things , and maybe scientists are gon na extend life by 70 or 80 years . And I said , &amp;lsquo ; This is such bull&amp;mdash ; t , &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; the 83-year-old Suzuki , co-founder of the &lt;a href= " https : //davidsuzuki.org/about/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;David Suzuki Foundation&lt;/a&gt; , said over the phone from his Vancouver office . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suzuki explained that humans have evolved to live a certain amount of time and we&amp;rsquo ; ve pushed that mark a bit through science . In the end , though , for him , it comes down to quality not quantity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re living longer , but you know , after the age of 65 or 70 , things are not that great , &amp;rdquo ; added Suzuki . &amp;ldquo ; Who wants another 60 years of a sh&amp;mdash ; y life ? I am much more interested in how do we age well . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So that&amp;rsquo ; s what the new Nature of Things&amp;rsquo ; episode Aging Well Suzuki Style is all about . The show , which is one of the handful of episodes Suzuki hosts each season , airs on Feb. 28 on CBC-TV at 9 p.m. and streams on CBC Gem . The show offers a fascinating and very personal take on getting old . And it&amp;rsquo ; s not surprising that Suzuki , for the most part , does well on the tests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve got the tears of a 20-year-old , &amp;rdquo ; the famed scientist and environmentalist said with a laugh . Another key strength for Suzuki was he had pretty good balance , a major key to aging well and avoiding injury . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44448;TOOLONG ... title= " When it comes to aging well , balance is a key component in keeping seniors going . It took a bit of insecurity to motivate him to take better care of himself . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When I got into the lab , I was sitting , looking through a microscope for hours and I developed a pot ( belly ) when I married Tara ( Cullis ) . I was quite chubby , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki , who admits his younger wife made him take stock . &amp;ldquo ; Here I am , this guy with a big pot . I was doing it for the wrong reasons . I&amp;rsquo ; m doing it to try to stay up to my wife , but I was doing it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suzuki points to the well-worn mantra of exercise being a key to a healthy , longer life . But he also quickly points out that humans seem to be fighting that basic idea at every turn . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The way we&amp;rsquo ; ve constructed society is to go to the opposite end everything is for convenience . Right ? So rather than walking up a flight of stairs , there is an escalator . Or , you know , the car services , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maintaining a healthy diet and healthy relationships also help in the quality-of-life department . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People have to have motivation . They have to have a place in society or something they do with other people , whether it&amp;rsquo ; s going to karate lessons or , you know , those sorts of things that give you a sense that you still have value in society , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki . &amp;ldquo ; For me , it&amp;rsquo ; s being a grandfather . This is the most joyful and &amp;hellip ; most important time in my life because I&amp;rsquo ; ve got these grandchildren ( he has nine in total , three in their 20s and six younger ones ) . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Your later years will also be improved by doing something meaningful , something that could be of value to the rest of society , he says . For Suzuki , that social currency comes in the form of activism , writing books , speeches and , of course , his TV gig . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Well , you know , the Nature of Things , I think that is a huge part of keeping me engaged because I&amp;rsquo ; m very proud of this series , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki , who has become a household name over the course of his four decades of TV science . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m very proud to be part of it . And , you know , it&amp;rsquo ; s a joy . It keeps me learning . Every show is a learning experience for me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But , you know , I&amp;rsquo ; m not immortal . I&amp;rsquo ; m going to kick the bucket &amp;mdash ; and I hope the show goes on . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And he hopes it goes on with his daughters Severn and Sarika Cullis-Suzuki . For the record , Sarika has already co-hosted a few shows with her dad and hosted a couple of her own Nature of Things as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44514;TOOLONG ... title= " Nature of Things TV host and environmentalist David Suzuki with daughter , Sarika Cullis-Suzuki . Photo : Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun " alt= " Nature of Things TV host and environmentalist David Suzuki with daughter , Sarika Cullis-Suzuki . Photo : Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun " data-portal-copyright= " Ian Smith " **28;44550;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204321 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the show and his family keeps him motivated to stay healthy , he admits that it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to stay happy as he watches more pipelines getting green-lit and trolls attacking a teen activist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , this foreboding sense is not new for Suzuki . Sarika , in an earlier interview with Postmedia News , said her dad was often Dr. Doom and Gloom . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When told about that moniker he laughed , but then turned serious . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Periodically I go through depression , despair , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki . &amp;ldquo ; Fortunately , and my wife is the same , we don&amp;rsquo ; t go into despair at the same time , so we can pull each other out of that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the end , though , he says those feelings subside , for a bit , and he is reminded &amp;mdash ; and likes to remind others &amp;mdash ; that giving up isn&amp;rsquo ; t an option and that , by joining forces , change can happen . He sticks a pin in that point with this story : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Do you know the famous story of the hummingbird and the forest fire ? It&amp;rsquo ; s an Indigenous story . A hummingbird is flying through the woods and suddenly sees this huge forest fire . So , he whips over to a lake , picks up a beak full of water . It goes back and drops it on the fire , and he&amp;rsquo ; s whizzing back and forth this way , and all the other animals in the forest are laughing at him and saying : &amp;lsquo ; What the hell are you doing ? &amp;rsquo ; And the hummingbird looks at them and says : &amp;lsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m doing the best I can . &amp;rsquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re all those hummingbirds . If there are enough hummingbirds , damn it , we can put the fire out . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A good way to become a hummingbird is to just take time to be in and part of the natural world &amp;mdash ; a concept Suzuki has long since championed in his bid to get people interested in protecting our tenuous ecosystems . He says he is always surprised by how little people pay attention to the world around them . Whether they&amp;rsquo ; re riding a bus or running . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was with my grandson Ryo . We were on a path in Victoria and I spot an owl . It was a huge owl . Maybe people are used to seeing owls but I haven&amp;rsquo ; t seen many wild owls . I run over with the buggy and I&amp;rsquo ; m , &amp;lsquo ; Look , Ryo , look . &amp;rsquo ; I am taking pictures and not one person stopped to look where I was looking or said , &amp;lsquo ; What are you doing ? , &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki . &amp;ldquo ; So they are all doing their thing running and biking , but they&amp;rsquo ; re not interested in what&amp;rsquo ; s going on . And , you know , the brain is a novelty-seeking device . That bird is a really exciting part of my environment , but people are shut down . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;lsquo ; Shut down&amp;rsquo ; they must be . After all , who wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t want to stop when they see one of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s most recognizable figures standing on a path excitedly pointing at a tree ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Walking outside people don&amp;rsquo ; t notice who I am , &amp;rdquo ; said Suzuki . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s just an old man with a kid . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No , not really . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;44580;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;44607;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/danagee " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;44641;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; Dana GeeThu , 27 Feb 2020 18:11:17 **45;44672;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;46496;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1207185 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Alma Deutscher with the VSO&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;46526;TOOLONG : Feb. 28 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;46561;TOOLONG : Bell Performing Arts Centre , 6250 144 St. , Surrey &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;46597;TOOLONG : Feb. 29 , 30 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;46632;TOOLONG : Orpheum Theatre , 601 Smithe , Vancouver &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;46668;TOOLONG : March 1 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;46703;TOOLONG : Centennial Theatre , 2300 Lonsdale , North Vancouver &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and Info&lt;/strong&gt; : &lt;a href= " https : **33;46739;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;46774;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Composer Alma Deutscher premiered her Piano Concerto in E-flat major at the Carinthian Summer Music Festival in Austria in 2017 . She also performed her Violin Concerto No. 1 in G at the same event . Only a year earlier , conductor Zubin Mehta premiered her full-length opera , Cinderella , in Vienna . That&amp;rsquo ; s quite an impressive list of achievement for any classical musician . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deutscher was 12. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born in Basingstoke , England , in 2005 , the musical prodigy composed her first piano sonata at age six . At seven , she had penned a short opera based upon author Neil Gaiman&amp;rsquo ; s short story the Sweeper of dreams . Three years later , she produced Cinderella . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By that time , the world had taken notice of the confident young artist&amp;rsquo ; s prodigious talents , with many in the press dubbing her &amp;ldquo ; the next Mozart . &amp;rdquo ; Unwilling to wear that title , and noting that there already was a Mozart , the artist has gone on record stating she would prefer to be recognized for who she is : Alma. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Vienna is an incredibly inspiring place to grow up , it is really the city of music , &amp;rdquo ; said Deutscher , over the phone from her home in Austria . &amp;ldquo ; When I go to the vineyards with the amazing view of the city to skip around in the nature , or when I&amp;rsquo ; m sitting in the underground , I&amp;rsquo ; m constantly getting ideas . Also , having lived here awhile , I&amp;rsquo ; ve also composed a few Viennese waltzes. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These waltzes will almost certainly be imbued with the light and feathery touch that characterize the era when the House of Habsburg ruled the region . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critics writing about Deutscher&amp;rsquo ; s work have lit upon how it is very focused on melody , running counter to many of the atonal and arrhythmic facets of contemporary classical music . This somewhat tiresome argument bred in an academic circles that contemporary music must be ugly and dissonant to reflect these qualities in the world doesn&amp;rsquo ; t impress Alma. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her lush , symphonic music defies the critics . They certainly can&amp;rsquo ; t accuse her of failing to find inspiration in those same mechanics and technology of everyday life . Her recently composed Siren Sounds Waltz is informed by exactly what modernists say music should embrace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It just happens to be melodic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Viennese police siren is made in fourths&amp;nbsp ; and doesn&amp;rsquo ; t wail like most do in other places , so I decided to make it into a melody , &amp;rdquo ; Deutscher said . &amp;ldquo ; Then I also incorporated specific sounds such as local bus doors closing and other city noise and integrated them into a waltz . It begins very chaotically , with the orchestra playing like a street with horns and sirens , until it calms down and you enter into the imagination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;46806;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;46842;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; That imaginary realm is where the &amp;ldquo ; ugly sounds of the modern world become something that is beautiful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deutscher&amp;rsquo ; s imaginary realm is inseparable from her musical output . She has conceived a land she calls Transylvanian &amp;mdash ; never having been to Transylvania , she says she has no idea how that name entered her head &amp;mdash ; which is where she hears beautiful melodies that wind-up in finished works . These are often written by various uniquely-named composers in the land , such as Antonin Yellowsink. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All the composers in my imaginary country write a little bit differently , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Antonin is quite a melancholy character who writes sad melodies . Sometimes , when I&amp;rsquo ; m stuck in my compositions and don&amp;rsquo ; t know what to do , I show them to him and he often makes very good suggestions . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The strong female characters in her operas undergo adventures in Transylvanian too . Deutscher has always loved stories about girls who overcame difficulty through their talents and their determination . Due to this , she populates her works with them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s what I like , and it is also is a way for me to address how , in the past , there were talented female musicians who were denied the right to compose and have their works performed , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; That really made me rather quite angry . When I write a piece , working hard to develop the melodies into a something that makes senses , with a structure that makes sense ; I think of them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The more the interview continues , the more it becomes clear why Alma has enchanted everyone from Zubin Mehta to some of the classical music world&amp;rsquo ; s toughest critics and beloved British presenter Stephen Fry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her love of music is absolute , and completely impossible to separate from any other facet of her life . This artist was finding ways to note down the melodies that apparently come into her head constantly when she was six years-old and had no formal musical training to speak of . Her ongoing studying has , in large part , been about developing better techniques to transition what she hears to sheet music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deutscher went on the record at age 10 stating that she understood how it might be hard for some to take her music seriously because of her years . The 15 year-old on the other end of the line exudes a professional confidence coupled with youthful energy that begs the question : How far can it go ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m always composing , but it&amp;rsquo ; s a very hard and time-consuming process , taking those melodies that are constantly coming and organizing them , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; And for pieces such as the piano concerto I&amp;rsquo ; m doing in Vancouver , which I wrote when I was 12 , I am always doing little fixes and changes . I re-orchestrated almost the whole concerti to put in a big brass section , because I&amp;rsquo ; ve always wanted it to have a big crashing section that&amp;rsquo ; s really loud , and never felt that it worked quite right . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She says that the piano concerto holds a particular place in her heart , because she wrote a good deal of it on her grandmother&amp;rsquo ; s piano after she passed on . She says that it&amp;rsquo ; s one of the saddest things she has written , surprising to people who know what an incredibly happy person she is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what does she do besides music ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love ballroom dancing , and Vienna is a perfect place for that , and it&amp;rsquo ; s become a serious passion , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Twice a week , I get to go and learn the most amazing dances , and I&amp;rsquo ; m going to go to lots of balls this coming season with my dresses already picked out . And I also love the theatre . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alma Deutscher will play three performances with the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra under composer Stanley Dodds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " sderdeyn@postmedia.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;46878;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;46916;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;46945;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynFri , 21 Feb 2020 19:00:30 **45;46976;TOOLONG ... Each week celebrities hide their identities under elaborate costumes ( this upcoming season will include among the 18 contestants a llama , banana and astronaut ) while they sing ( apparently ) their hearts out in a bid to woo the judges and of course America . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Comedian &lt;a href= " http : //margaretcho.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Margaret Cho&lt;/a&gt; , who will be in Vancouver for a &lt;a href= " http : //jflnorthwest.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;JFL Northwest&lt;/a&gt; comedy festival show ( Feb. 15 , 7 p.m. at the Vogue , tickets $39 at &lt;a href= " https : **33;47954;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **27;47989;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt; ) &lt;/em&gt; , was the Poodle in Season 1 of the show . The current popularity of the show that started in Korea is no surprise to Cho . She agrees the wacky talent show is a kind of antidote to the emotional and politically polarizing heaviness that many are feeling these days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s something innocent about it , which I think is something that is needed , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho over the phone from her home in Los Angeles recently . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think we do need something we can kinda come together on that&amp;rsquo ; s very playful . It&amp;rsquo ; s unique , and at the same time it&amp;rsquo ; s something very important because we need a childlike wonder about things . I think it&amp;rsquo ; s really sweet . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s also free of labels and unconscious biases , as a singing egg and pineapple are equally nutty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Identity is put aside and right now there is so much caustic friction that people have about identity in particular , and so when you remove that sort of aspect of it and just look at the purity of somebody&amp;rsquo ; s voice , I think there is a tenderness there , and a humanity , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48018;TOOLONG ... title= " Margaret Cho. Sonically , it is very different , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Cho can throw down as a glamorous singing poodle , do successful sitcoms , host a podcast , design clothes , and act as a BDSM expert on the Netflix show Explained , the Grammy- and Emmy-nominated comic always manages to find her way back to the stand-up stage &amp;mdash ; a place she has called home since she was 16. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cho is part of a JFL Feb. 13-25 line-up that includes comedy headliners Hannah Gadsby , Bill Burr and Patton Oswalt as well as up-and-coming stand-ups , improv and sketch performances , hit podcasts and even short films . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48084;TOOLONG ... title= " Red-hot comedian Hannah Gadsby will be bringing her new show Douglas to the JFL Northwest comedy festival Feb. 24 and 25 . Photo : Jill Greenberg " data-portal-copyright= " Jill Greenberg " **28;48120;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206763 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; JFL is just one of about 100 stand-up gigs Cho does each year . &amp;nbsp ; While shows like this one make up the base of her three-decade-long career , she says she also needs variety for complete happiness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think they all kind of work together to make for a balanced life . I love acting . I love music , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To me it is really special to do all these different things , but comedy is a constant . It&amp;rsquo ; s something that is always happening so that is the most important part of my life . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cho grew up in San Francisco where her parents ran a gay bookstore . A self-identifying bisexual , Cho has always been a vocal supporter of LBGTQ communities and , in turn , those communities have supported her work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love that . To me that&amp;rsquo ; s still a big part of my identity and kind of my purpose . So , yeah , I love that , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho about her fan base . &amp;ldquo ; I love being queer . I love the queerness of my existence . It&amp;rsquo ; s the essence of who I am. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s also a big part of what she wants to talk about , but it by no means is her only topic when she takes to the stand-up stage . Like many comedians who call America home , the current state of their union is loaded with potential material . And really , isn&amp;rsquo ; t it better to laugh than cry ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What&amp;rsquo ; s good is there is a lot to say and there is a lot to deal with in all of these issues , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are things that I have talked about for a long time , whether it is racism , sexism , homophobia . All of these things have a big effect on our lives now , so there is a lot to say and that is what&amp;rsquo ; s great about comedy &amp;mdash ; that I can go out and do that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;48150;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;48192;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Check out our comprehensive event **29;48228;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;48259;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;48295;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Obviously at the eye of the liberal comedy storm is U.S. President Donald Trump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cho doesn&amp;rsquo ; t hesitate when asked about him . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Him getting elected , the whole thing has been upsetting from the minute it happened . I really didn&amp;rsquo ; t think it was possible , &amp;rdquo ; said Cho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is such a sickening situation . B.C. , with its high real-estate prices , is receiving an increasingly smaller fraction of migrants from other Canadian provinces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another thing that makes Prince Harry and Meghan like the largest cohort of new arrivals is the couple appear to be preparing to become temporary residents . They&amp;rsquo ; re planning on settling in Canada to a certain degree , but they&amp;rsquo ; re giving no indications they&amp;rsquo ; re here to obtain citizenship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though the world has been watching as Meghan and son Archie have spent much of the past two months on Vancouver Island and in Metro Vancouver &amp;mdash ; and Queen Elizabeth has acknowledged the family is going &amp;ldquo ; through a period of transition in which the Duke and Duchess will spend time in Canada and the United Kingdom&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; several things are unknown . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;50489;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;50531;TOOLONG ... Todd : Five things we learned about migration in **25;50567;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;50594;TOOLONG ... housing market pressed by temporary **30;50630;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;50662;TOOLONG ... Todd : A tale of two costly housing markets : Toronto and **30;50698;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The exact migration status of Meghan and Harry is up in the air , for instance . Still , the couple fit loosely into the category of &lt;a href= " http : **34;50730;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; " millionaire migrants . " &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s the title of the seminal book University of B.C. geographer David Ley wrote to describe the escalating movement of transnational wealthy people flocking to the world&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; gateway&amp;rdquo ; cities , such as Vancouver , in search of some sort of haven . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And should the moneyed royal couple buy a home in this country , they would be signing in on the current global fashion in real estate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada and B.C. &amp;mdash ; especially high-priced Metro Vancouver , Victoria and &lt;a href= " http : **34;50766;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Toronto&lt;/a&gt; ( where Markle has worked as an actress ) &amp;mdash ; are prime destinations for the world&amp;rsquo ; s wealthy to purchase properties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If Harry and Meghan put down money on a dwelling in Metro Vancouver , Victoria or in certain other urban centres on the West Coast , however , Vancouver immigration lawyer Sam Hyman says they would be subject to the B.C. government&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " http : **34;50802;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;foreign-buyers tax&lt;/a&gt; &amp;mdash ; and perhaps to its speculation and vacancy tax . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In that way , the famous couple would end up in the same boat as tens of thousands of other foreign national property owners in B.C. who do not spend more than six months a year in the country ( which normally means Ottawa does not tax their income ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NDP government is already beginning to take in hundreds of millions of dollars a year from targeting lightly- used , non-resident-owned B.C. properties with such taxes , which are similar to those in many sought-after global cities , including London , home to Buckingham Palace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since they are British and American citizens , Harry and Meghan are distinct in one way . They do not hail from the continent that is by far the largest source of new arrivals in Canada , Asia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As such they do not have to apply for a visitor&amp;rsquo ; s visa to make a home in Canada for up to six months a year . That distinguishes them from the more than three million people from countries such as China and India who have in recent years been &lt;a href= " http : **34;50838;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;snapping up Canada 's 10-year-multiple-entry visas&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;50874;TOOLONG ... title= " Queen Elizabeth II , Meghan , Duchess of Sussex , Prince Harry , Duke of Sussex at Buckingham Palace for an event to mark the centenary of the RAF , July 10 , 2018. " alt= " Queen Elizabeth II , Meghan , Duchess of Sussex , Prince Harry , Duke of Sussex at Buckingham Palace for an event to mark the centenary of the RAF , July 10 , 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " Chris Jackson/Getty Images " **28;50910;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1189257 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet long-term visitors such as Harry , Meghan and Archie add in a way to the country&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " http : **34;50940;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;exploding stock of non-permanent residents&lt;/a&gt; , a cohort made up mostly of international students and various types of guest workers . This group makes up two of three of the roughly one million new migrants to Canada each year , as well as of the more than 110,000 moving annually into B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regardless of the category of non-permanent resident to which t &lt;a href= " http : **34;50976;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;he royal family&lt;/a&gt; end up belonging , the consequences end up being similar in regards to lifestyle options &amp;mdash ; especially when it comes to Canada&amp;rsquo ; s housing market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though it&amp;rsquo ; s anybody&amp;rsquo ; s guess whether Prince Harry and Meghan will buy property in B.C. , it is common for non-permanent residents to do so . Such foreign nationals are free to come and go almost as they wish , whether to visit family or enjoy part-time living near evergreen forests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Without commenting directly on the royal couple , veteran &lt;a href= " http : **34;51012;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;B.C. real-estate analyst Steve Saretsky&lt;/a&gt; says the overall migration-fuelled growth in Canada&amp;rsquo ; s population that the arrival of the royal couple epitomizes has been &amp;ldquo ; nothing short of incredible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And the fact almost all of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s GDP expansion depends on such population growth &amp;ldquo ; should be of particular interest to Canadian home builders who are aggressively building homes to try and keep pace with the record number of people moving here . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s of specific concern , Saretsky says in his December report , when many new arrivals are non-permanent residents . &amp;ldquo ; We have become increasingly dependent on the growth of a cohort of people who could quickly vanish in the event of a weakened economy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although the details of the royal couple&amp;rsquo ; s future in Canada are understandably murky &amp;mdash ; including how they might engage in work or what they will do for housing &amp;mdash ; there is no doubt their expressed interest in setting up a part-time home in this country , particularly in B.C. , fits into several new and widespread migration narratives. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;MORE RELATED : &lt;/strong&gt; Asked whether the world was ready for another rock festival , the KISS bassist declared that the world wants anything that has quality and that is what Titans of Rock will deliver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Tens of millions of people in North America love a certain kind of music that revolves around guitars and being unapologetic about turning it up to 10 , or &amp;mdash ; yes &amp;mdash ; even 11 , &amp;rdquo ; said Simmons . &amp;ldquo ; The stadiums are filled with this kind of no-nonsense , kick-in-the-butt music that has ruled as long as most of us have been alive . " alt= " Aaron Chapman is an author and historian whose most recent title is Vancouver After Dark : The Wild History of a City 's Nightlife . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;57456;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1159000 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Vancouver After Dark&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Wild History of a City 's Nightlife&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **26;57486;TOOLONG Aaron Chapman ( Arsenal Pulp Press ) **26;57514;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $32.95 246 pages &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; In January 18 , 1971 , a page 2 ad in The Province announced a new entertainment at Club Zanzibar at 1129 Howe Street . &amp;ldquo ; Topless Wraslin&amp;rsquo ; . A Canadian First . See It to Believe It . Topless dancers trained to kick , maul , pinch , eye-gouge and hair-pull . Zany &amp;mdash ; Wacky &amp;mdash ; Hilarious &amp;mdash ; Violent . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;57542;TOOLONG &lt;img src= " https : **34;57569;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;57605;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; Hot baron of beef buffet rounded out the package . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was public outcry over this entertainment , as well as the want ads in The Vancouver Sun seeking 3 midgets to appear in a different &amp;ldquo ; wraslin ' &amp;rdquo ; event at the Gulf Club billed as &amp;ldquo ; one mad dog vs. five chicks. &amp;rdquo ; This was a far cry from bloody ground and pound MMA matches broadcast at most pubs today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It paled in comparison to far more zany , hilarious and &amp;mdash ; yes &amp;mdash ; violent stuff happening all over Vancouver at the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Vancouver After Dark , local historian Aaron Chapman shines a spotlight on &amp;ldquo ; the wild history of a city&amp;rsquo ; s nightlife . &amp;rdquo ; It took decades for the No Fun City designation to take hold . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is the third title in what the author describes as his trilogy , beginning with the story of the Penthouse in Liquor , Lust , and the Law ( 2012 ) and followed by Live at the Commodore ( 2014 ) . The Last Gang in Town ( 2017 ) , about the notorious Clark Park Gang , can be seen as a kind of &amp;ldquo ; adjunct title . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Responding to people&amp;rsquo ; s comments that Vancouver is too young to have any interesting history , Chapman frames his response academically : &amp;ldquo ; Crap . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For a long time , I think that the history of Vancouver that was presented was usually another story about the railroad arriving , the three greenhorns and real estate , or the standard Chamber of Commerce creation story , &amp;rdquo ; said Chapman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But just scratch the surface a little and there is so much to learn , and it&amp;rsquo ; s gritty . That&amp;rsquo ; s has been something of a thread line through all of my books , I suppose . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;57635;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;57677;TOOLONG ... about books and **28;57713;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;57743;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;57779;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Chapman notes in his introduction , Vancouver today &amp;ldquo ; sold to the outside world depicts bright bustling neighbourhoods full of boutique shops , set against a backdrop of photogenic beaches and mountains , both of which can be visited in the same afternoon . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As they do today , a century ago , pious city and provincial governments pursued teetotal agendas to put down opportunities to party . Persistent police raids , new noise legislation , and other machinery of the state couldn&amp;rsquo ; t keep the crowds from cramming into everything from bars and ballrooms to nightclubs and repurposed community halls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reading through Chapman&amp;rsquo ; s research , it&amp;rsquo ; s clear that access to entertainment spots in different neighbourhoods was far better in the past . But , he notes , there has always been a kind of entertainment district trend in town . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The whole club scene has moved around so much over the years , from Hornby , to Gastown to Granville , and each time people decry the loss of venues , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everyone I interviewed talked about how they saw the glory years of Vancouver , when it was the best time ever . But that changes with every generation , and there was a kid last night who went to the Commodore and saw a show which they will reflect back upon 20 years from now as the best time in the city . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While there is no question that the scene has changed , particularly when it comes to the amount of live music venues , a healthy and active club scene still exits . New spaces pop-up in surprising places , just as they did in the past , and Chapman acknowledges that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One thing that Vancouver After Dark makes abundantly clear is that places come and go with frequency . From such East Side cabarets as the New Delhi , where mixed-race rockers like the Hi-Fives filled the dance floor , to any number of comic legend Tommy Chong&amp;rsquo ; s clubs back in the Sixties , tear it down and sanitize has always been a dominant development theme in the Lower Mainland . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;57806;TOOLONG ... title= " The Hi-Fives perform at the New Delhi cabaret in Vancouver 's East End . " alt= " The Hi-Fives perform at the New Delhi cabaret in Vancouver 's East End . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;57842;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1158894 " /&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;57872;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;57914;TOOLONG ... about books and **28;57950;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;57980;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;58016;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; With every subsequent new luxury condo tower put up , more rules arrived . Add in skyrocketing licensing fees , rents , new noise bylaws , and more and it becomes hard to believe that anyone would choose to operate a business catering to nightlife . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But even so , there have always been people in Vancouver who have been managing clubs or putting on a party somewhere and dealing with all of the levels of red tape and challenge , &amp;rdquo ; said Chapman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In as much as I do try to be positive about the future , the one thing that can&amp;rsquo ; t be ignored is that guys like Danny Beceda and Frank Hook essentially opened Oil Can Harry&amp;rsquo ; s before they were 25 . I don&amp;rsquo ; t see anyone that age being able to do that now with costs what they are , and maybe if that can be fixed we will find ourselves in another golden era. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What most certainly has transpired with the homogenization of culture in the city is that people are far less likely to have regular hangouts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chapman fondly recalls how the front lounge at the Town Pump was a meeting point for the whole of the Vancouver music scene for years &amp;mdash ; a place where hard rockers rubbed elbows with rockabilly musicians , industrial growlers and pop stars , the &amp;lsquo ; Pump was a nexus for live music fans and players . The original Railway Club was another such hangout. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Such locations often had intergenerational memory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When these places go and disappear on us , a part of the DNA of the city changes a bit , but that is a theme that runs up and down the whole West Coast as cities have grown and gentrified. &amp;rdquo ; Chapman said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We were fortunate to have a situation dating back to the vaudeville days where tours would make it up here that never went over the mountains to Calgary or Edmonton . Major tours still kick off here or finish up here a lot of the time , and artists frequently will be here early to rehearse or stick around after the tour ends , which has added to the entertainment scene as well . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver After Dark delves into the way that the changing performance market paved the way for many of the older cabarets to shut down . As acts that used to grace their stages developed the ability to pack far larger venues , they no longer needed to do a few nights in a row to make the same amount of money that they could with one night . In the closing chapter , Last Call , Chapman notes how this reality has changed the Granville Strip , where more pubs have opened in place of live or even dance music venues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many of the buildings that once housed live music venues are still standing , potentially to be reopened . But the likelihood is that this won&amp;rsquo ; t happen . Chapman notes &amp;ldquo ; time and again , the threat to a Vancouver club hasn&amp;rsquo ; t been a fire or mismanagement but property development . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But there is still &amp;ldquo ; room for graveyard shift dreamers . &amp;rdquo ; &amp;nbsp ; Just don&amp;rsquo ; t try to revive topless wrasslin&amp;rsquo ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;58043;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;58085;TOOLONG ... about books and **28;58121;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;58151;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;58187;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;58214;TOOLONG ... title= " The Cave nightclub staff in Feb. 1949. " alt= " The Cave nightclub staff in Feb. 1949. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;58250;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1162004 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;The following is an excerpt from Vancouver After Dark . Images and text reprinted with permission from the publisher . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;The Cave&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; If there is one name on the list of all the nightclubs that have come and gone over the decades in Vancouver whose loss is perhaps most lamented , it&amp;rsquo ; s the Cave . There are even those who never went there who regret its demise , longing for the magic and excitement of a lost age . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Cave was the city&amp;rsquo ; s premier venue during the height of the nightclub show era &amp;mdash ; the early 1960s , when nightlife was stylish and sophisticated . Many Vancouverites even remember its kitschy faux-cavern interior of papier-m&amp;acirc ; ch&amp;eacute ; stalactites and stalagmites with fondness , wishing the club were still here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gordon King opened the Cave at 626 Hornby Street in 1938 . King had come to town from Winnipeg , where he&amp;rsquo ; d opened the first Cave nightclub in 1935 . He later opened another one in Edmonton . The Vancouver Cave lasted the longest , though , and was the most famous , attracting many big-name American acts that toured along the Pacific coast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition to its subterranean decor , the club featured a special sprung dance floor and a large forty-foot-wide stage . In the early years , the venue hosted performers from the vaudeville era and veteran stars who&amp;rsquo ; d made their names in radio and cinema . Local dancers and performers also appeared , along with comedian emcees and even the odd magician. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Cave changed management and ownership frequently during its history . After World War II , Gordon King&amp;rsquo ; s son Max returned from service in the Royal Canadian Air Force to run the club , until Isy Walters , who bought it in 1952 , sold it in 1958 and then opened Isy&amp;rsquo ; s Supper Club a year later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before they bought the Cave from Walters , Ken Stauffer and Bob Mitten had both worked at the Arctic Club , one of several members-only cocktail and supper clubs that were popular in Vancouver in the late 1940s and &amp;rsquo ; 50s . The two had the sort of good gamblers&amp;rsquo ; instincts that are crucial for being an effective nightclub owner . For instance , they often took chances on booking unknown acts , and most of the time , their intuition was proved right . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since vaudeville days , Vancouver had been known as Tune-Up City , where performers could rehearse a show in front of a live audience before taking the act down the Pacific coast , through Seattle , Portland , San Francisco , and on to Los Angeles . The same routes exist today in modern concert touring . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As far as club gigs went for local musicians , there were few better regular jobs than the Cave . The orchestra positions that paid union scale were coveted ones that most musicians in Vancouver did their best to keep . However , a few recent histories of the Cave suggest there was a colour barrier that kept black musicians from becoming orchestra members there . Harlem Nocturne proprietor and trombonist Ernie King stated , &amp;ldquo ; I was qualified enough to play in The Cave , but they didn&amp;rsquo ; t want a guy like me , they wanted an all-white band , not a coloured band with me sitting there . There were never any black musicians , unless it was a black band from the States . &amp;rdquo ; 1 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Veteran Vancouver saxophonist Gavin Walker agrees race was a factor for musicians seeking entry into some Vancouver nightclub orchestras at the time and notes that the Cave orchestra in particular presented other challenges . &amp;ldquo ; The guys that got the orchestra positions at the Cave&amp;mdash ; &amp;lsquo ; The Downtowners&amp;rsquo ; was their unofficial name&amp;mdash ; were very protective of their union scale work , and it was a bit of a closed circle . You had to have the ability to play but also be a top-notch sight-reader . The Downtowners also got a lot of CBC work , and when the jazz shows came up on the CBC , these were the guys the CBC hired , not the hard-core jazz players who were mostly white that played other venues like the Jazz Cellar . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One musician who did make the cut was Blaine Tringham , who began playing at the Cave as a junior orchestra member in his early twenties . &amp;ldquo ; A freelance horn player could make a pretty good living just by answering the phone and saying yes , &amp;rdquo ; Tringham says with a laugh . &amp;ldquo ; At the Cave , initially you&amp;rsquo ; d be the third or fourth call , but eventually you&amp;rsquo ; d work your way up to the first if you were any good . But in those days , the protocol was that whoever called you first got the gig , and I&amp;rsquo ; d take any gig I could . So sometimes you&amp;rsquo ; d take a gig at some other place like Isy&amp;rsquo ; s , then the Cave might call you and you&amp;rsquo ; d have to tell them you were already booked , even if you preferred to play there . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tringham recalls that pay at the Cave was $160 a week and $120 a week at Isy&amp;rsquo ; s , because the hours were shorter . &amp;ldquo ; That doesn&amp;rsquo ; t sound like a lot today of course , but you have to remember this was the early 1960s . The rent in my furnished apartment was $65 a month , so you could make a good living as a club musician then . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And with the number of nightclub acts that came through town at the Cave in the 1960s , Tringham stayed busy , but the schedule left little turnaround time to rehearse new acts . In the daytime , there were three-hour rehearsals to go over two ninety-minute shows . The constant flow of stars required a regular team of skilled musicians with seasoned chops on the Cave bandstand . In suits and ties , heads down in the charts on their music stands , Fraser MacPherson&amp;rsquo ; s band appeared completely focused and reserved from an audience perspective , but Tringham confesses things were not always what they seemed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The guys at the Cave could drink , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; They had a capacity you couldn&amp;rsquo ; t believe . I was just the kid and didn&amp;rsquo ; t drink at the shows because I was too nervous to screw up a part or miss a cue . But the regular Cave musicians bought Beefeater gin by the case and kept it backstage in these lockers that were supposed to be for clothes . They&amp;rsquo ; d always have a cup of it at their feet , sipping it , and gin just looked like water . Every night those guys got loaded . Sometimes they&amp;rsquo ; d send the busboy to the liquor store to get more . The amazing thing was they never screwed up . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tringham continues , &amp;ldquo ; There was a guy named Stew Barnett&amp;mdash ; he was the king of the trumpet at the Cave . As many drinks as he sipped away at , he never made a mistake through the whole show . It was only at the very end of the night he&amp;rsquo ; d run out of gas . The curtain would close and he couldn&amp;rsquo ; t get out of the chair . It was like a marathon runner who&amp;rsquo ; d hit the finish line . He was a great guy and a great musician . Everybody smoked and drank there while they played , taking a quick puff of a cigarette between parts . It was like that in the recording studios , too . That&amp;rsquo ; s just what you did then ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Cave orchestra had their favourite performers to work with . Mitzi Gaynor rehearsed her whole nightclub show in Vancouver before taking it to Las Vegas , and came back year after year . Tringham recalls that although Mel Torm&amp;eacute ; had a reputation for being difficult , the band enjoyed playing with him and he was a complete professional . Anthony Newley , meanwhile , &amp;ldquo ; confessed to us he was really nervous with this debut at the Cave because it was a new nightclub show he was trying out . But he was a lot of fun . Just one of the guys . &amp;rdquo ; Another favourite was singer and actress Jaye P. Morgan , who might be best remembered as a TV game show panellist during the 1970s. &amp;ldquo ; She was very outspoken about&amp;mdash ; how shall I put this ? &amp;mdash ; who she liked . There was a guy in the band she kept hitting on in front of us , saying that she was going to take him to bed . She was teasing him like crazy , even during the shows . It was very funny . One night his wife came down to see the show and he sweated through the whole night hoping Jaye wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t say anything . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , the Cave featured many touring nightclub acts : older acts like the Mills Brothers and Roy Orbison appeared along with more modern performers like Diana Ross and the Supremes , James Brown , the Righteous Brothers , Sonny &amp;amp ; Cher , and Bette Midler. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;58280;TOOLONG ... title= " Cave gig poster . " alt= " Cave gig poster . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;58316;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1162002 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Danny Baceda , who operated Oil Can Harry&amp;rsquo ; s jazz club , bought the Cave for $100,000 in 1971 . A month later , he bought Isy&amp;rsquo ; s Supper Club , making him the biggest nightclub owner in Vancouver at the time . But the expansion happened too quickly , and by 1972 , Baceda went into receivership . Ken Stauffer bought back the Cave in 1973 , running it briefly before selling it to Stan Grozina. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Originally from Slovenia , Grozina spent his early years in a series of German labour camps during World War II . He immigrated to Canada with twenty dollars in his pocket and soon became involved in the construction business in Winnipeg . He retired in Vancouver and bought the Cave , sinking $75,000 into renovations . But when the Cave reopened , Grozina&amp;rsquo ; s bookings were hit and miss . The club had success with rock bands like the Animals , Canned Heat , Trooper , and Doug and the Slugs , and Grozina occasionally booked some exciting emerging underground bands as well , like the local new wave band Pointed Sticks in 1979 . The musicals he booked weren&amp;rsquo ; t as successful , however , and with disco taking off in some downtown clubs , and punk rock emerging in others , the Cave was suddenly a horribly old-fashioned place to go . At that point , Grozina began booking wet T-shirt contests&amp;mdash ; things were going downhill fast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They had , in fact , been heading that way for a while . The golden era of nightclub acts was over . In many ways , the clubs had become victims of the performers&amp;rsquo ; success . The acts the nightclubs had nurtured had now become too successful to stay there , and the top performers who had once booked ten-day or two-week club engagements now came for one- or two-night stops at the Queen Elizabeth Theatre or , if they were big enough , the Pacific Coliseum . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Cave was unable to make the transition the Commodore Ballroom did . The Commodore had once seen an older generation of entertainment but had made the jump to a modern concert space , thanks to owner Drew Burns , whose policy of renting the room to outside promoters ultimately gave the club its future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Stan Grozina was no Drew Burns . He mistakenly hoped the old nightclub-style acts would live to see another day , and he could not imagine the Cave as any other kind of establishment . A disastrous booking in 1978 of an aged Ginger Rogers resulted in a $40,000 loss that doomed the club financially . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You could really feel that things were changing by the early 1970s , &amp;rdquo ; recalls Tringham . For him , and other musicians like him , the very music they were being called to play was changing . &amp;ldquo ; I feel lucky to have been at the Cave when I did . It was the right place at the right time , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Cave closed in 1981 , and aside from a few expressions of nostalgia , there seemed to be little public outcry that the iconic club would be no more . The Cave was demolished that summer . Some of the club&amp;rsquo ; s old stalactites and stalagmites were saved and auctioned off . The Hong Kong Bank of Canada Tower was built in its place , marking the end of an era when the Hornby Street strip of nightclubs thrived . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hornby is a different street now in a different city . There are no enticing neon signs or doormen on the street ushering you into the pleasures of the nightclubs inside . Only a few lonely taxi cabs glide by , heading to and from more exciting destinations . There is nothing to indicate this short stretch was were the city came to be entertained at the Cave and other thriving clubs . The sights and sounds of Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s nightlife have moved elsewhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;58346;TOOLONG ... title= " July 25 , 1981 . Demolition of The Cave nightclub . Deborah Cameron photo . " alt= " July 25 , 1981 . Demolition of The Cave nightclub . Deborah Cameron photo . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;65970;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1151829 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver comedian Graham Clark will be taking stand-up to the extreme next weekend when he attempts a marathon , &lt;a href= " https : **33;66000;TOOLONG ... set for charity&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Clark , a three-time Canadian Comedy Award winner and the co-host of the popular and long-running Stop Podcasting Yourself , will take the stage at East Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Havana Theatre on Friday , Nov. 29 at 8 p.m . He intends to leave the stage at 9 p.m &amp;mdash ; on Saturday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Inspired by fellow comedian Pat Thornton of Toronto , who has completed five such marathon shows to raise funds for the Stephen Lewis Foundation , Graham will soon become the first Vancouver comic to attempt the same . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We caught up with Clark to find out what possesses someone to do something like this , how he plans to pull it off , and if he&amp;rsquo ; s allowed bathroom breaks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;66035;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;66071;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q . What possesses a man to do 24 hours of stand-up ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A. The Stephen Lewis foundation encourages people to do dares to raise money for their charity . Pat Thornton has been doing this for years in Toronto , and Alistair Cook , the wonderful human who runs the Havana Theatre , dared me to do the same . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Your marathon is to raise funds for The Stephen Lewis Foundation , to fights HIV and AIDS in Africa . Why did you choose this charity ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a wonderful charity , and it&amp;rsquo ; s their dare campaign that lead to this , so it only makes sense that they should benefit from it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Do you actually plan to stay standing , or is this more likely to be 24 hours of sit-down comedy ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m going to stand as much as possible . I may lean some , and sure , if the occasion arises , I may sit . But I will be wearing my most comfortable shoes . I should get Dr. Scholl&amp;rsquo ; s on board next time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Do you even have that much material ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not even close . Luckily , I have some of Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s best and brightest comedians coming down to write material for me as it goes on . Hopefully people online will join in as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Havana is a pretty dimly-lit venue . Are you concerned at all about your audience , or your yourself , falling asleep , since that 's what normal people do when it gets late ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I am always concerned about this , not just at this show ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Forget holding people 's attention . Let 's talk about holding your bladder . What 's the plan for bathroom breaks ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m going to take the occasional bathroom break , but will be running an hour longer to compensate for those . As far as the plan for those bathroom breaks , that is privileged information . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;This has never been attempted in Vancouver . What makes you think you can pull of something no Vancouverite has ever done ? Do you think you 're special , Graham ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you ask my mother , yes , I&amp;rsquo ; m special . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;You recently served as the west coast correspondent for This Hour Has 22 Minutes . Does n't that seem like a more reasonable amount of time to be consistently funny ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ha ! Actually that would be a great name for this event : This Hour Has 24 Hours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Did you ever consider just running an actual marathon instead ? It would only take you , like , four or five hours . You 'd be home for dinner . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It might only take you five hours . I think this will be a much shorter time span than it would take me to finish an actual marathon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Finally , are there any other local comics you 'd like to see attempt a full day of stand-up ? Name names . Call them out . Throw down the gauntlet . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s so many talented comedians in this city , I&amp;rsquo ; m sure we could take on a whole month ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Graham Clark 's 24 Hours of Standup For Charity begins Friday , Nov. 29 in Vancouver 's tiny Havana Theatre at 1212 Commercial Drive .
