Afghani-Canadian broadcaster and singer and subject of the book Voice of Rebellion . 2019 PNG Merlin Archive " alt= " Mozhdah Jamalzadah . Afghani-Canadian broadcaster and singer and subject of the book Voice of Rebellion . 2019 PNG Merlin Archive " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;67334;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1137228 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Voice of Rebellion&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How Mozhdah Jamalzadah Brought Hope to **26;67364;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By Roberta Staley ( Greystone Books , Vancouver ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; $32.95 280 pp. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; In this rags-to-righteousness story , author Roberta Staley charts how Mozhdah Jamalzadah went from being a child refugee arriving in Canada to hosting the barrier-breaking Mozhdah Show for two years and earning the moniker , &amp;ldquo ; the Oprah of Afghanistan&amp;rdquo ; in her 20s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tackling such taboo subjects as divorce and domestic violence earned the dynamic young broadcaster a fierce fan base matched only by an even-fiercer opposition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the book documents , there came a time when it was no longer safe to continue working in Kabul . But by the time that occurred , her reputation was such that she sang at the White House , met her idol Oprah Winfrey and accomplished much more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With her career in her ancestral homeland cut short , Jamalzadah continues her activism from abroad , pursuing a musical and acting career from her Vancouver home . The cover image of her wearing the blue burqa turned up to reveal her face is loaded with defiance and contradictions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When her family &amp;mdash ; educated and modern &amp;mdash ; took a midnight bus from Afghanistan to Pakistan , her mother , Nasrin , wore the full burqa to pass as an obedient , passive peasant wife through the many checkpoints along the way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mozhdah discusses how a symbol of female subjugation had become a means to freedom impacted upon her later choices from everything to how she appeared on TV to how she lives her life today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;67392;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;67428;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Voice of Rebellion . Book about Mozhadeh Jamalzah by author Roberta Staley . Greystone. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; During the Civil War , the whole country changed and a whole Soviet-style surveillance culture developed that had everyone looking over their shoulder , &amp;rdquo ; said Jamalzadah. &amp;ldquo ; Then during the Taliban era , there was this element of fear added to it . Even afterwards , there would be moments when rumours or news would go around that would get everyone in a state of heightened tension again . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Coming to Canada from that unsettled war zone was an impulsive decision when her father was warned the police were coming for him . The family made it to Pakistan as refugees , where life was basically hand to mouth . Permitted to immigrate to Canada , the family landed in Oshawa , Ont. , where everything from snow piled high to rampant classroom racism took its toll on the impressionable young Mozhdah. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Moving to Vancouver proved a much different experience in the more multicultural classroom and population mix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The passages about bullying and the hardships of the immigrant experience in Voice of Rebellion prove to be a potent antidote to the bigoted masses making up their own headlines in social media that the mainstream press often proliferates. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; How the family rebuilt itself through diligent work , smart business decisions and dedication out of nothing is inspirational enough . But where Mozhdah takes it is exceptional . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Setting her father&amp;rsquo ; s protest poem , titled &lt;em&gt;Dukhtare Afghan&lt;/em&gt; , about acid attacks on girls walking to school , to music , Mohzdah became a chart-topping singer and was invited to perform the song in front of the Obamas at the White House . The status she attained from the song and other musical appearances lead to the offer to host a show on the new 1TV station in Kabul . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Heading back to her ancestral homeland , she found herself directionless again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;67458;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;67494;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the story of my life . This complete cultural shock of being somewhere completely different all over again , trying to define my space there all over again and again , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Here , I&amp;rsquo ; m seen as ethnic , as an immigrant , and English as a second language-speaker. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In Afghanistan , I&amp;rsquo ; m this Westerner in their eyes trying to speak Farsi for an entire one-hour show . That was one of the hardest things I&amp;rsquo ; ve ever had to do . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But she did it , and the show was a game-changer in Afghanistan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Inspired by the Oprah Winfrey Show , the Mozhdah Show was unlike anything on the air . Topics ranged from domestic violence to the lives of spandis &amp;mdash ; young people who begged on the street waving burning cans of herbs at motorists to ward off evil . The programs hit a nerve in a war-torn country emerging from a tumultuous few decades . Not everyone loved it , but she kept at it . Then an assault by a co-worker and mounting serious death threats made it impossible to continue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All of that changes you as a person , and the strength you gain coming out on the other end of it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t come without a cost , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I went there really optimistic , naively thinking that I could help and make things possible and , perhaps because of that , it actually did for a time . When it didn&amp;rsquo ; t , it set me back and I almost fell into a very dark hole where I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t see the light , or get myself back up and be where I was before . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She stresses the experience gained from her time in Kabul reinforces her convictions that there are good people everywhere being taken advantage of by people in power manipulating situations to their benefits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If anything , the experience has opened her eyes to the fact that issues such as the subjugation of women are global in nature , that bad apples fall from all trees regardless of their cultural or religious practices and the main thing is to keep standing up to the negative and work toward the positive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Of all the things that me and my 19-year-old producer brought in as subjects for the show , nothing was as rewarding as introducing the concept of positive thinking , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Decades of war has instilled a very negative mindset in everyone , and everything is negative and in denial . So for a couple of episodes , I talked about how positive thinking could change your day , you life , your way of thinking and even that met with serious opposition . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But she says people still comment how important raising the topic was . She thinks there is a platform for spreading the word to future generations of young people &amp;ldquo ; messed up , depressed and bullied by social media , &amp;rdquo ; as well as hearing the immigrant voice around all manner of issues in the news . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jamalzadah hopes that &lt;em&gt;Voice of Rebellion&lt;/em&gt; will inspire other young women to pursue the difficult , but rewarding , path of breaking down barriers and developing dialogue around difficult issues . The way her story reads , it&amp;rsquo ; s not difficult to imagine a scriptwriter phoning to option it for a new series on one of the many streaming services out there . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given that she posts regular videos on her label &lt;a href= " https : **32;67530;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Ethnobeast&lt;/a&gt; &amp;lsquo ; s YouTube channel , it&amp;rsquo ; s obvious we haven&amp;rsquo ; t heard the last from this rebellious voice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;67564;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;67600;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;67636;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;67667;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;67705;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;67734;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;&lt;a href= " **27;67765;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK **35;67794;TOOLONG class= " s2 " &gt; to report a typo. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span class= " s2 " &gt;Is there more to this story ? Chelsea Handler can . Her latest read , titled Life Will Be the Death of Me , explores a year of self-discovery undertaken by the author to exorcise some personal demons such as the death of her brother , and come out on the other end all the better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a change of direction for the writer best known for blunt dissections of sex , drinking and other assorted activities in books such as Are You There , Vodka ? It&amp;rsquo ; s Me , Chelsea ( 2008 ) , or Lies that Chelsea Handler Told Me ( 2011 ) , and Netflix series such as Chelsea Does or last month&amp;rsquo ; s Hello , Privilege , It&amp;rsquo ; s Me , Chelsea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The book also heralds Handler&amp;rsquo ; s return to standup &amp;mdash ; actually , sit-down &amp;mdash ; comedy as she embarks on a massive tour in support of the text . Digging deeply into the pain of her childhood loss put the comedian in a very different frame of mind . She remains the self-deprecating New Jersey-ite fans adore , but there is a renewed passion for activism around personal and political issues , as well as everyone&amp;rsquo ; s favourite herb . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We begin our discussion around the line of marijuana products that Handler is launching in 2020 , and how one launches a line of cannabis products . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You have to do a lot of research , into tinctures , oils , lotions , bath salts , weed and edibles , and I made it my priority for the past 2 1/2 years to do that , &amp;rdquo ; said Handler . &amp;ldquo ; It was a surprising pivot from alcohol and one I far prefer , but it makes international travel challenging . I&amp;rsquo ; m back on the sauce here in the U.K. , so I&amp;rsquo ; m looking forward to coming to Canada . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Advised of the continuing supply shortages , slow pace of introducing full product lines into the marketplace and the vibrant black market , she zeros in on the irony that the legal marijuana business is being run by the same people that used to jail people for minor offences and they&amp;rsquo ; re doing it poorly . Handler says that she and her partners at NorCal Cannabis are looking at organizations representing people who are in jail for minor possession charges . The plan is to donate a portion of the proceeds to getting people out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She also wants women to expand the cannabis category to include products specifically developed for women , who she feels have been ignored for the most part . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve discovered with micro-dosing that it&amp;rsquo ; s a whole different ball game and I want women and first-time users to know that it&amp;rsquo ; s a safe place , where you can get high and be emboldened and empowered instead of having negative experiences , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I want to look into developing the THCV strain , which is an appetite suppressant , and has been completely ignored by the guys who have been in charge of marketing weed for the past 100 years . Handler says to wait and see in the new year , which is when the product line should be launching . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Until then , she has plenty on the go . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hello , Privilege , It&amp;rsquo ; s Me , Chelsea , found her trying to dive into the issue of what white privilege is and how blind , or antagonistic to it , white people are to the subject . Beginning with Chandler herself , who has admitted in interviews that she likes to &amp;ldquo ; get her opinion changed . &amp;rdquo ; The show has drawn mixed reviews , with many media outlets noting Chandler&amp;rsquo ; s controversial past jokes and actions as problematic . The comic doesn&amp;rsquo ; t deny it , but says that her humour is sharper now that she is more educated around the issues around racism , sexism and so on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The election of Donald Trump to the office of U.S. president proved to be a major catalyst for her creative energy , and bringing the contents of her new book to the stage on this tour has been rewarding . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t planning on doing the book , or on doing standup , but then the book just vomited out of me and I had something that I could take on the road as a standup show , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve taken the subject matter from the book , made it side-splitting and that&amp;rsquo ; s always been something that I really wanted . She&amp;rsquo ; s not sure that anyone but her could play her at this stage in her life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This tour , and this book has been more personal than anything else I&amp;rsquo ; ve ever done before and that authenticity shows , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; People respond to that in different ways , and it&amp;rsquo ; s nicer to be out there not being a loud-mouthed b&amp;mdash ; h and spreading something more positive instead . " alt= " Chris Buck directed the Walt Disney animated movie Tarzan , which won an Oscar in 1999. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;71132;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1121605 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;SPARK Animation&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;71162;TOOLONG : Oct. 24- 27 , various times &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;71197;TOOLONG : Emily Carr University , 520 E. 1st Ave . and other venues &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info&lt;/strong&gt; : &lt;a href= " http : **32;71233;TOOLONG ? f ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;71267;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1934 , Walt Disney decided that the studio bearing his name would move into making feature-length animated films and work started on Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs . The first full-length animated movie took years to make and industry insiders were so convinced it would bankrupt the studio , they dubbed the project &amp;ldquo ; Disney&amp;rsquo ; s Folly . &amp;rdquo ; How wrong they were . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a brief period , the 1937 film was the highest-grossing sound film of all time . It remains in the top-earning animated films to this day , and it&amp;rsquo ; s impossible to separate the Disney brand from the animated feature genre . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In subsequent decades , full-length animated movies saw their popularity decline . Then the Disney Renaissance ( 1989 to 1999 ) restored Walt Disney Animation Studios into a global animation powerhouse . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chris Buck was around for that rise , co-directing 1999s Academy Award-winning Tarzan . The Oscar-winning director of 2013s Frozen and the coming sequel Frozen 2 will appear at the 2019 SPARK Animation conference for a 20th anniversary screening of Tarzan on Saturday , preceded by a question and answer with Buck and co-director Kevin Lima . Buck is also a keynote speaker at the conference . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the things the session is certain to touch upon is the way in which the film managed to skirt both young and old audiences alike . This was the source material from author Edgar Rice Burroughs&amp;rsquo ; 1912 novel Tarzan of the Apes writ large in eye-catching animation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; While we always had the kids in mind , we never talked down to them or deliberately did anything that would mess with the well-known original source material , &amp;rdquo ; said Buck . &amp;ldquo ; We had these incredible action sequences that we didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to dilute or lessen the intensity of and that kept it enjoyable for all-ages and really got audiences thrilled with the viewing experience . Of course , we also had the incredible music from Phil Collins . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;71300;TOOLONG ... title= " Oscar-winning Director Chris Buck attends the Frozen Fan Fest Product Showcase at Casita Hollywood this October 02 , 2019 in Los Angeles , California . " alt= " Oscar-winning Director Chris Buck attends the Frozen Fan Fest Product Showcase at Casita Hollywood this October 02 , 2019 in Los Angeles , California . " data-portal-copyright= " Andrew Toth " **28;71336;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1121543 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , it was Collins&amp;rsquo ; soundtrack and song , You&amp;rsquo ; ll Be In My Heart , which won the movie an Oscar , a Golden Globe and a Grammy . The winning Disney formula dating back to classics like Dumbo and the Jungle Book , where a fast-paced classic storyline is paired with show-stopping musical numbers had been upgraded to the modern pop era . Subsequent hits such as Frozen and the Lion King remake have ridden this to massive appeal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There were so many elements of Tarzan that made it so special , especially to have it be my first feature , &amp;rdquo ; said Buck . &amp;ldquo ; It started over in the TV studio under Kevin Lima&amp;rsquo ; s direction , as he had done a Goofy movie for them . Features got hold of it and took it over , but owing to the size and scope of the project , they wanted Kevin to bring in a second . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buck was reticent to become involved with the movie , viewing animation as a particularly time-consuming arena of the film biz . He had seen colleagues get bogged down in full-length cartoons and wasn&amp;rsquo ; t sure that the work was for him . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Then I was on weekend vacation at a ski hill in a rented condo and they had an old copy of Reader&amp;rsquo ; s Digest in the room that I picked up to thumb through before we hit the slopes , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; And in the margins , someone had written &amp;lsquo ; people regret more of what they haven&amp;rsquo ; t done than what they have done . &amp;rsquo ; There was my answer to my struggle over the decision whether to do Tarzan or not . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;71366;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;71402;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Made for a budget of US$130-plus million , Tarzan was one of the most expensive animated features of the time . To date , worldwide box office proceeds are $450-plus million-and-counting with the 20th anniversary possibly driving sales up again . The Buck-directed Frozen was moderately more expensive ( $150 million ) and took in a staggering $1.2 billion-plus . Frozen held the top-grossing animated box office record until August 2019 when the reboot of the Lion King passed $1.3 billion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eighty two years on , &amp;ldquo ; Disney&amp;rsquo ; s Folly , &amp;rdquo ; appears to paid off plenty . Frozen 2 lands on Nov. 22. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Like Tarzan being somewhat more mature , in the world of Frozen 2 , we are letting our characters grow up some , &amp;rdquo ; said Buck . &amp;ldquo ; We found the emotion in the adoption story , and being able to give life , emotion and voice to the animals that Tarzan is raised by and lives and communicates with was a beautiful way to go . Animation , particularly Disney , does that type of tale beautifully and , unlike any previous Tarzan film , we could make him move like Burroughs had written it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , working with source material as familiar as Tarzan enables the creative team a great deal more depth of background to work on the film&amp;rsquo ; s narrative line . There are a total of 24 Tarzan books , the majority of them were written before Burroughs died in 1950 , with subsequent novels being co-written from the author&amp;rsquo ; s ideas or other writers officially authorized by the estate to keep the story going . Buck and the team knew that to keep their cinematic story going , they needed to embrace the latest technology for maximum impact . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;71438;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;71474;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We were able to use this new technique called Deep Canvas , which enabled us to move through the jungle in a way that wasn&amp;rsquo ; t just flat , but instead enabled you to be immersed in the environments you were moving through , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; It was created by some of our incredible artists and technicians and that&amp;rsquo ; s how you get those magic scenes of Tarzan practically surfing through the trees and the animals moving through so fluidly . I still think it looks amazing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides the panel discussion to follow the screening of Tarzan , Buck will also be presenting a lifetime achievement award on opening night ( Oct. 24 ) to Hollywood animation production legend Bonnie Arnold . The producer of the How to Train Your Dragon franchise , as well as Toy Story and Tarzan , she has worked with Disney , Pixar and DreamWorks Animation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;71510;TOOLONG " **36;71541;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;71579;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;71608;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynTue , 22 Oct 2019 17:39:06 **45;71639;TOOLONG ... Gladwell 's latest book looks at how we talk to strangershttp : **31;71686;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;71719;TOOLONG ... title= " Author Malcolm Gladwell looks at how we talk and deal with people we do n't know in his new book Talking to Strangers Photo credit : Celeste Sloman " alt= " Author Malcolm Gladwell looks at how we talk and deal with people we do n't know in his new book Talking to Strangers Photo credit : Celeste Sloman " data-portal-copyright= " Celeste Sloman " **28;71755;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1112455 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thanks to the circus-like atmosphere of American politics , best-selling author &lt;a href= " https : //www.gladwellbooks.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Malcolm Gladwell&lt;/a&gt; admits he pines a little for his old job as a Washington Post reporter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gladwell was at the newspaper from 1987 to 1996 , first as a business and science writer , and then the Post&amp;rsquo ; s New York bureau chief . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I miss it . To be at the Washington Post right now is the best moment to be a journalist in 50 years . It&amp;rsquo ; s fantastic , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell , reflecting on the constant mayhem of Donald Trump&amp;rsquo ; s administration . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It must be so thrilling . They must be working 60 hours a week &amp;mdash ; if not more . I am sure they are killing themselves , but this is what journalists live for , this kind of stuff . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You see the value . This is a really , really powerful reminder of how valuable a free press is . Democracy can not function without that , &amp;rdquo ; he added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The topic of American politics came up ( as it often does these days ) in advance of the five-time best-selling author&amp;rsquo ; s event at the &lt;a href= " https : //writersfest.bc.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Vancouver Writers Festival&lt;/a&gt; &amp;nbsp ; to discuss his new book , &lt;a href= " https : **33;71785;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Talking to Strangers : What We Should Know about the People We Do n't Know&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;71820;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;71856;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the book , Gladwell reminds us of the polarized world we live in , how we have stopped listening to each other , and how we often make the wrong assumptions about others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the more impactful points in the new book is the idea that we don&amp;rsquo ; t have to meet a person to understand them . In fact , it might be better , at first , if we went on hard facts over handshakes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A classic example of that theory , Gladwell says , is former British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain&amp;rsquo ; s huge hoodwinking at the hands of Adolf Hitler before Second World War . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The people who were wrong about Hitler were the ones who had talked with him for hours , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell , who outlines Chamberlain&amp;rsquo ; s trips to meet with Hitler in the book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those who were right about him never met him , he says , but they read the writing on the wall and the writing in Mein Kampf ( the 1925 manifesto where Hitler laid out his anti-Semitic political ideology and future plans ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gladwell&amp;rsquo ; s course toward his latest book began with an interest in spies , and how many of them were inept bumblers who somehow went go undetected in the high-stakes world of international espionage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t understand why it was so hard to catch spies . So I did all that spy stuff that&amp;rsquo ; s in the book first , but I didn&amp;rsquo ; t think it was a book . I just thought it was interesting . I did all those interviews and I went down and met ( psychologist ) Tim Levine , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( Levine ) has thought as much about the problem of why we are deceived by strangers as anyone in social science , &amp;rdquo ; added Gladwell about the professor and chair of Communication Studies at the University of Alabama Birmingham . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of Levine&amp;rsquo ; s ideas is that we &amp;ldquo ; default to truth&amp;rdquo ; as basically a way of just getting on with things . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Levine&amp;rsquo ; s big argument is trusting strangers makes for a very efficient communication and social transaction &amp;mdash ; default to truth . The reason why we have evolved to default to truth is that it just works better . It allows us to do all kinds of things , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell , who was raised in rural Ontario but has called New York City home for years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With his spy research completed , Gladwell decided to move forward on a book after the story of Sandra Bland broke . Bland was in Texas when she was pulled over for failing to signal a lane change . The cop demanded she get out of the car . She questioned why , and they argued . He eventually said : &amp;ldquo ; I will light you up ! Get out ! Now ! &amp;rdquo ; He drew his gun . She got out and went to jail where she took her own life three days later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t know where I was going with it and then Sandra Bland happened and I realized that was a kind of really , really useful way of coming to grips with this problem of these sort of tragic encounters between law enforcement and African-Americans . And so Sandra Bland was the catalyst for the book , but I had been kind of thinking about this problem of strangers before that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thanks to the internet , we interact with strangers all the time . Modernity has moved us outside of what Gladwell calls our &amp;ldquo ; kinship circle , &amp;rdquo ; and forced us to confront people who are different . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If you think about things like Airbnb and Uber , they&amp;rsquo ; re two exercises in institutionalized stranger transactions , where you&amp;rsquo ; re taking an extraordinary leap of faith entrusting your home and your transportation to someone you have never met . Someone you basically know nothing about and who supposedly was kind of vetted by some third party &amp;mdash ; but who even knows if that is the case ? &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We weren&amp;rsquo ; t doing that in the 1960s , were we ? We weren&amp;rsquo ; t even doing that in 1985 . So , there is something weird about that going on right now . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Doing research for the book and talking to strangers Gladwell says reminded him to take a beat before forming a definitive opinion about another person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It has powerfully reinforced something that I might have had already &amp;mdash ; a kind of caution about&amp;nbsp ; drawing conclusions about people I don&amp;rsquo ; t know well . It is something I have always done , but it is something I feel more strongly about , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have lost all my sense of certainty about my ability to make sense of someone . Now I am just trying to reserve judgment as much as possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That outlook comes in handy when you are out on the road promoting a book , meeting new people every day and having your work critiqued and criticized by those who aren&amp;rsquo ; t buying what you&amp;rsquo ; re selling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have done it before , I know what to expect . It is always exhausting but it is exhilarating , as well , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell about the launch of a new book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; With book one , I was , predictably , much more sensitive to criticism than I am now . Now , not really . I&amp;rsquo ; ve been doing this for 20 years , and I have built an audience . I have painstakingly cultivated a group of people who like what I do and want to participate in my ( work ) &amp;mdash ; whether it is my podcast or my books , my articles or whatever . Those are the people I am writing books for . So that is more than enough for me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t need 100 per cent approval . I don&amp;rsquo ; t think anybody gets a 100 per cent approval , do they ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With the book already launched , Gladwell is looking forward to focusing on the fourth season of his podcast &lt;a href= " http : **25;71886;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Revisionist History&lt;/a&gt; . While he enjoys the format of podcasts , he admits it makes for a lot more creative anxiety than writing a book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I need 10 ideas , not one , for the podcast . It&amp;rsquo ; s a huge difference . It is actually a little more hair-raising than writing a book , &amp;rdquo ; said Gladwell. &amp;ldquo ; I am having a good time , but I am losing sleep . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " dgee@postmedia.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;71913;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/danagee " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;71947;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;71978;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;72020;TOOLONG ... more about books and **28;72056;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;72086;TOOLONG ... the latest in local , national and international books **25;72122;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;72149;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? NewsAudible.ca releases hip-hop industry insider Sophia Chang 's The Baddest Bitch in the Roomhttp : **36;74890;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;74928;TOOLONG ... title= " Sophia Chang attends Bustle 's 2019 Rule Breakers Festival at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside on Sept. 21 in Brooklyn , N.Y . " alt= " Sophia Chang attends Bustle 's 2019 Rule Breakers Festival at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside on Sept. 21 in Brooklyn , N.Y . " data-portal-copyright= " Bryan Bedder " **28;74964;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1101816 " /&gt; **27;74994;TOOLONG Baddest Bitch in the **30;75023;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Sept. 26 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Online &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; $14.95 a month . First month free at &lt;a href= " https : **33;75055;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;audible.ca&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s hardly news that the music industry is still white-male dominated and minorities , particularly female , are barely represented in its ranks . When she moved from her hometown of Vancouver to New York in 1988 to pursue a career in music , Sophia Chang didn&amp;rsquo ; t give that a single thought . The city was the heartbeat of hip-hop . The 23-year-old Korean-Canadian was enchanted by the genre ever since a classmate at Prince of Wales mini-school spun Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five&amp;rsquo ; s breakout release , The Message . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chang planned on taking a big bite out of Big Apple rap . She did that and a whole lot more , becoming a major music-biz player privately as well as producing runway shows for Vivienne Tam and the Project Runway All Stars , and writing a screenplay for HBO . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In her audible.ca memoir titled The Baddest Bitch in the Room , Chang tells the tale of how someone who grew up in super-safe , suburban , white Vancouver became an A&amp;amp ; R ( artist and repertoire , talent scout ) for the enormously influential label Jive and moved in the grittier circles of Staten Island backroom recording studios hanging out with Wu-Tang Clan founder RZA and opening up her Manhattan apartment to a who&amp;rsquo ; s who of hip-hop legends to crash in . While she may not be a household name , Chang&amp;rsquo ; s name is familiar to any in the music industry during rap&amp;rsquo ; s golden age , and the journey she details in her audiobook comes across like a script for a biopic that is coming to a streaming service near you . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her memories of life in Manhattan&amp;rsquo ; s Lower East Side in the heyday of hip-hop , new wave , the loft scene and more is loaded with sharp insights into what life was like in the days before gentrification and development turned the Bowery into a boutique . No , it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t always wonderful , but it certainly was real . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t know that The Message was what I wanted to hear more than anything else until I heard it . I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t identify that missing thing until I heard it and it was so real , &amp;rdquo ; said Chang. &amp;ldquo ; We were listening to The Jam , The Clash and the Pistols a little bit , with this urgency and **26;75090;TOOLONG . Then there was this hip-hop with all of that and this phenomenal storytelling like nothing I had ever heard before , plus that incredible beat . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , her guitar-playing boyfriend at the time said it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t real music . This tired-out line is still trotted out by unoriginal musicians everywhere who resent talented turntablists and MCs making music that matters rather than trying to reformat Foghat for commercial rock radio . Tied into this whole attitude , which goes back to such loathsome acts as Disco Demolition Night at Comiskey Park , Chicago , on July 12 , 1979 , are elements of racism , homophobia and class bias . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;75118;TOOLONG ... title= " Sophia Chang attends Bustle 's 2019 Rule Breakers Festival at LeFrak Center in Brooklyn on Sept. 21. " alt= " Sophia Chang attends Bustle 's 2019 Rule Breakers Festival at LeFrak Center in Brooklyn on Sept. 21. " data-portal-copyright= " Bryan Bedder " **28;75154;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1109001 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I worked closely with Nile Rodgers ( Chic ) who was huge in the disco era . And in his phenomenal biography , The Freak , he talks about how the music came right out of the black-and-brown queer scene in the New York underground in the &amp;rsquo ; 70s , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; And a lot of that opposition to disco came from racism and homophobia , and a lot of the resistance to hip-hop , for sure , had to do with race . I absolutely think that if rap had been coming from white men , there wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have been that pushback. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As she notes in the book , there was a point where that opposition to hip-hop as a musical force became tilting at windmills . Soundscan&amp;rsquo ; s sales chart couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be denied . The genre was exploding on vinyl , on select radio stations , on MTV and in concert . Sales figures for albums like the first NWA or Wu-Tang Clan&amp;rsquo ; s Enter the Wu-Tang ( 36 Chambers ) mirrored those of breakout rock bands . Working with artists finding a way to describe their culture in a powerful voice led Chang back to her own issues of cultural identity and belonging . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My mother and father literally risked their lives to get out of Korea and I was raised with a serious amount of , what I&amp;rsquo ; ll call , their intrepidity , and I knew that I was smart , that my opinion mattered , and I didn&amp;rsquo ; t take it much further than that , &amp;rdquo ; said Chang. &amp;ldquo ; Coming into a genre that was so clearly defined by gender and by race was daunting for me , but hip-hop embraced me so completely . I came to proclaim that , &amp;lsquo ; My name is Sophia Chang and I was raised by Wu-Tang , &amp;rsquo ; because it was so . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She spent decades working with Wu-Tang Clan&amp;rsquo ; s RZA , GZA and ODB and was involved with A Tribe Called Quest , Raphael Saadiq and D&amp;rsquo ; Angelo as well . Through this continuing connection , she had what is described as a &amp;ldquo ; transformational odyssey , &amp;rdquo ; coming to a point where she took what she learned from her dear friends and applied it to her own life . Along the way , she would take up Shaolin martial arts and have children with an actual practising monk , move up the ranks of record-label boardrooms and come to define her role as an Asian woman in the entertainment business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the best things about this job has been that I&amp;rsquo ; ve been able to not only work with these artists , but also to come to experience their humanity and learned from them , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; For years , people have been saying that I should write a book about my &amp;lsquo ; crazy life , &amp;rsquo ; and I bristled at the idea because it would be me writing about hanging out and working with famous people , and who gives a shit . But when I started working at Universal Music Group in 2014 and was mentoring a bunch of really young women , I realized that telling my story and relating my experiences could be in service of others trying to make it in this business . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chang said working with Paul Simon made her acutely aware of the price people pay for fame . Her late mentor Sonya Chang told her to fiercely protect her anonymity for both longevity and sanity . By bringing her life out of the boardroom and into a book , Chang bares it all , warts and everything , proclaiming , &amp;ldquo ; I am the fearsome empress on the throne , to whom you bend the knee and whose bling you kiss . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Baddest Bitch in the Room is 54 now . She says releasing an Audible Original was an obvious choice in storytelling for someone who has held onto microphones for decades . Chang is currently developing film and TV properties , raising her children and trains kung fu seven days a week . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;75184;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;75220;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;75256;TOOLONG " **36;75287;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;75325;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;75354;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynSun , 29 Sep 2019 18:00:01 **45;75385;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;75505;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1100616 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s just get it out of the way , former justice minister and attorney general &lt;a href= " https : **33;75535;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Jody **25;75570;TOOLONG will be writing a memoir . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But no , she won&amp;rsquo ; t be releasing it a few days before the Oct. 21 federal election . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m not going to throw a bomb unless a bomb is to work really hard and work on behalf of your constituents , then maybe , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould when asked if she would use the &lt;a href= " https : //www.snclavalin.com/en " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; SNC-Lavalin&lt;/a&gt; affair to deliver a blow to her former boss , Justin Trudeau , and the Liberal party . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;75597;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;75633;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; While there is no timeline yet for the impending memoir , Wilson-Raybould admits she has had it on her mind for a while now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have lots of notebooks and I have been writing about my experiences , &amp;rdquo ; added the former Liberal cabinet member and We Wai Kai Nation member . &amp;ldquo ; From what I can tell , people are interested in it , so I will write a memoir at some point . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Oh yes , people are interested . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the meantime , Wilson-Raybould has released &lt;a href= " https : **33;75663;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;From Where I Stand : Rebuilding Indigenous Nations for a Stronger Canada . &lt;/a&gt; It doesn&amp;rsquo ; t include any deep dives , it&amp;rsquo ; s more a matter of Wilson-Raybould dipping a toe into the SNC-Lavalin affair that saw her resign on principle from cabinet in February . Two months later she , along with MP Jane Philpott , was ejected from the Liberal caucus . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The book instead is made up of an extensive introduction followed by a series of speeches she has given over the years . The opening speech is a keynote to the Western Canada Aboriginal Law Forum in May of 2010 . The book closes with her speaking at a Feminists Deliver event in June of 2019. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Driving those speeches is the theme of reconciliation , including the understanding of how we got to where we are on Indigenous issues as well as ideas on structured , sensitive and , most importantly , viable paths forward to ensure true reconciliation . She says the Liberal government could have done more to advance reconciliation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilson-Raybould , who was the first Indigenous person to be attorney general , asks the citizenry ( including government , Indigenous leaders and the public ) to help continue to move reconciliation forward . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I envision 10 years from now we will have taken bold leadership and created the mechanisms to transform Indigenous nations or to create the space for Indigenous nations to be self-determining , including self-governing , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilson-Raybould grew up in Port Hardy and Comox . Her Kwak&amp;rsquo ; wala name is Puglaas , which roughly translates to &amp;ldquo ; woman born to noble people . &amp;rdquo ; Her father is Bill Wilson , a First Nations hereditary chief , politician , and lawyer . Wilson-Raybould is a former crown prosecutor and she was Regional Chief of the Assembly of First Nations for B.C. ( 2009-2015 ) before entering federal politics and becoming a star candidate for the Liberals in 2015. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , that all changed when news broke that the PMO had allegedly attempted to influence Wilson-Raybould in regards to the ongoing prosecution of SNC-Lavalin . After appearing in front of the House Judiciary Committee , Wilson-Raybould became a household name &amp;mdash ; and a major thorn in the side of the prime minister . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;75698;TOOLONG ... title= " Vancouver Granville independent candidate Jody Wilson-Raybould. " alt= " Vancouver Granville independent candidate Jody Wilson-Raybould. " data-portal-copyright= " Mike Bell " **28;75734;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1101274 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , here we are month away from a federal election and Wilson-Raybould &amp;mdash ; who was stripped of her Liberal party nomination for the 2019 federal election &amp;mdash ; is promoting a book and running to retain her Vancouver-Granville riding . The Liberals have thrown their weight and money behind candidate Taleeb Noormohamed. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was a difficult period of time for almost a year now . I think though through life , and this reality I have lived through , you learn lessons , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould , who was also briefly the veterans affairs minister . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; People don&amp;rsquo ; t bring up the specific facts of that company in Quebec ( SNC Lavalin ) but they bring it up to me and are having discussions of the very nature of our democracy . It is so surprising , but so welcoming , to have people talk about the importance of the rule of law and why we are so fortunate to live in a country like this because we have the rule of law and we uphold it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think that everything happens for a reason . Now I am running as an independent and I&amp;rsquo ; m in the place that I should be , &amp;rdquo ; added Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; The fact that people have learned similar lessons and have that greater awareness of what they want from politics , or that they want to have politicians make decisions on what&amp;rsquo ; s important in terms of the issues versus what&amp;rsquo ; s important in terms of political expediency or power is why I got involved in politics in the first place to actually &amp;mdash ; and it&amp;rsquo ; s an over used phrase &amp;mdash ; do politics differently . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It really has emboldened me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver Granville is easily going to be one of the most-watched races in B.C. And maybe even the country . Wilson-Raybould says she is feeling good and more importantly feeling the support . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The idea of Wilson-Raybould running as an independent raises some red flags for people , most importantly will her voice be heard over a chorus of party-backed and party-line towing MPs ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m in the right place at this time , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; I have always advocated my own views , beliefs and principals . I&amp;rsquo ; m not tied to or told what to say which I think is the extremely positive element of being an independent . Less partisanship is what I hear all the time . People actually just want to talk about issues . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilson-Raybould wants to , and hopes her constituents and the rest of the country can take a minute and look at her and her campaign as a way forward , a way to begin to loosen up the partisan political party lines that many believe have tied up our democratic system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What we need politicians in Ottawa , actually anywhere for that matter , to do says Wilson-Raybould is to take a page from the Indigenous people&amp;rsquo ; s playbook. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I found and learned that Ottawa could take some lessons in terms of decision-making from the culture that I come from , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; All voices are important . That&amp;rsquo ; s the culture I come from . You have to raise people up to fulfil their roles and if you don&amp;rsquo ; t do that there is something taken away from the strength of the community . People might roll their eyes when I say something like that and it might sound airy-fairy or naive but in my view it&amp;rsquo ; s not . My culture has survived for millennia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am not saying parliament is going to change overnight and we&amp;rsquo ; re all going to function by way of consensus , but at least moving in that direction or recognizing that we are never going to resolve issues like climate change or Indigenous reconciliation unless we come together and have bold plans and understand in having bold plans they have to live beyond the life of one government in order to be sustainable in order to actual address the issue . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the first line of the intro for the new book , Wilson-Raybould says : &amp;ldquo ; A central lesson instilled in me from a very young age was to be careful with words because you can not take them back &amp;mdash ; you must always speak the truth . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When you bring up the idea that , for many people , trusting the words of a politician has gone the way of straw boaters hats and stages covered in bunting , Wilson-Raybould pauses for a second and let&amp;rsquo ; s out a bit of a sigh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It makes me kind of sad but I understand the reality we live in . This cynicism about politics and politicians is something that is hugely problematic for our democracy , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; We need to change the culture or the nature of our politics to know that when we say something &amp;mdash ; that it has to mean something . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For me it comes from my culture being an oral culture . And if we don&amp;rsquo ; t speak the truth , the culture dies , &amp;rdquo ; added Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; People should be more careful with what they say . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Speaking of what people are going to say , one has to wonder whether the Liberals will go after Wilson-Raybould in October or keep their heads down in hopes of keeping talk of SNC-Lavalin out of the campaign . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I can&amp;rsquo ; t put myself in the position of other candidates or parties , &amp;rdquo ; Wilson-Raybould said . &amp;ldquo ; I am hopeful that we can look at issues that are issues we all have to address like Indigenous issues and focus on them as opposed to focusing on individuals or trying to undermine the credibility of individuals . I&amp;rsquo ; ve faced that now for over eight months and I think that is very unfair and very debilitating and focusing energy where it shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though eight months or so have passed since the country was glued to the SNC-Lavalin story , Wilson-Raybould reluctantly &amp;mdash ; she doesn&amp;rsquo ; t want to seem &amp;ldquo ; self-serving&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; admits she draws a lot of attention when she is out pounding the pavement in her riding . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Sometimes people just burst into tears . It&amp;rsquo ; s not about me . It&amp;rsquo ; s what I represented in that , if you believe in something , then you stick to it . You speak your truth without any fear of repercussions , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However repercussions are a very real thing and politics is a dirty business . But rather than waiting and worrying about what may get lobbed her way , she is looking ahead and trying to be a good example to those who may follow her into the political arena . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I can inspire people to understand what my grandmother taught me , which was if you have a dream , if you are passionate about something and you work hard you can accomplish anything , &amp;rdquo ; said Wilson-Raybould. &amp;ldquo ; If there&amp;rsquo ; s a message to any little Indian girl in any corner of this great country or beyond , it is to know you can accomplish whatever you set your mind to if you work hard . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;75764;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;75791;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/danagee " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;75825;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; Dana GeeFri , 27 Sep 2019 18:18:22 **45;75856;TOOLONG ... announcement : Celine Dion Courage World Tour comes to Rogers Arenahttp : **35;75903;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;75940;TOOLONG ... title= " C ? line Dion performs in 2016 at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas . Email &lt;a href= " **28;78491;TOOLONG " **46;78521;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; David CarriggThu , 19 Sep 2019 16:45:41 **45;78569;TOOLONG ... NewsTelevisionElton John says Farewell Yellow Brick Road on final tourhttp : **36;78616;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;78654;TOOLONG ... title= " Sir Elton John will perform three shows at Rogers Arena this month as part of his Farewell Yellow Brick Road Tour . " alt= " Sir Elton John will perform three shows at Rogers Arena this month as part of his Farewell Yellow Brick Road Tour . " data-portal-copyright= " FERDY DAMMAN " **28;78690;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1091606 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Elton John Farewell Yellow Brick Road Tour&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;78720;TOOLONG : Sept. 21 to 24 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;78755;TOOLONG : Rogers Arena &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info&lt;/strong&gt; : &lt;a href= " https : **33;78791;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;78826;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; After 57 years performing , Sir Elton Hercules John ( CBE ) is saying goodbye to global fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour was announced on Jan. 24 , 2018 . With 300-plus dates , the piano-playing pop star&amp;rsquo ; s last road trip is scheduled to end in a two-night stand at The O2 in London in December . The musician born Reginald Kenneth Dwight on March 25 , 1947 , wants to spend more time with his husband David Furnish and their two sons , Zachary and Elijah . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He&amp;rsquo ; ll be home in time for Christmas . Still standing , but probably ready for a well-earned retirement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Along the way , John makes multiple stops across Canada . It&amp;rsquo ; s testament to his popularity that none of these dates are single night shows . Vancouver actually has a three night-run . That&amp;rsquo ; s nearly 57,000 fans entertained at one stop and the other venues are of a similar size . Sir Elton is doing his best to not bow out breaking fan&amp;rsquo ; s hearts . The setlists on the tour are averaging 25 songs a night and almost all of those were hit singles , from the heights of his gaudy , glam-rock phase to the soundtrack successes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;78857;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;78893;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Such is the career of the artist who began making pocket change playing in pubs and local rock bands before first gaining attention in 1962 backing UK blues singer Long John Baldry in Bluesology . Changing his stage name to Elton John in 1972 , he and his lifelong lyricist Bernie Taupin , set about writing the first album . Titled Empty Sky ( 1969 ) , it didn&amp;rsquo ; t do much . The followup , 1970s Elton John , included the single You Song which went top 10 in both the U.K. and U.S. and remains in regular rotation on classic rock and adult contemporary radio to this very day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From there , it&amp;rsquo ; s a whirlwind of creative and commercial successes . By the time Honky Chateau became John&amp;rsquo ; s first U.S. No. 1 record in 1972 , his catalogue was already getting packed with the sort of singles most artists&amp;rsquo ; dream about achieving just once or twice . The John/Taupin songwriting machine made it look easy , and one year later , Goodbye Yellow Brick Road dropped including the title track , Bennie an the Jets ( U.S. No. 1 ) , Candle in the Wind , Saturday Night&amp;rsquo ; s Alright For Fighting and Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding . And the songs just kept coming . By 2013 , Billboard hailed the artist as the most successful male solo artist on the trade magazine&amp;rsquo ; s Hot 100 Top All-Time Artists . He was just behind the Beatles and Madonna . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As fans prepare for the 72-year-old singer&amp;rsquo ; s arrival , here are five things to know about someone once referred to as &amp;ldquo ; Reggie . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;1 . The Top Tune&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given the depth of the John/Taupin back catalogue , trying to get fans to agree on their top 10 tracks taken from the 30 albums the two have collaborated on is very difficult . Given there are over 58 Billboard top 40 hits included in the list over a 50 year period , there are generational shifts to take into account too . In a Sept. , 2018 piece in the Guardian , critic Dave Simpson compiled a top 50 songs list . Top spot went to Tiny Dancer , a six minute-long tune from Madman Across the Water which bombed upon release . Revitalized by its inclusion in director Cameron Crowe&amp;rsquo ; s film Almost Famous , the song has held the top spot in numerous lists published over the years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;78929;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;78965;TOOLONG &lt;h3&gt;2 . The Voice&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sure , the wild costumes and accessories such as the US$5,000 spectacles that spelled his name in lights were great for gaining attention in the powder-happy hedonism of the glam rock era . Being a piano player in an era rife with showy guitar heroes was pretty different . But what really has been John&amp;rsquo ; s most potent tool throughout his career is his spectacular voice . He can croon , he can soar , he can scream and he almost lost it . In 1987 , John had surgery on his vocal cords to deal with a non-malignant lesion which resulted in his voice taking on whole new levels of deeper timbre and a noticeably rounder and fuller quality . He first showcased this on his 21st studio LP , Reg Strikes Back which included yet another Adult Contemporary chart No. 1 tune in I Don&amp;rsquo ; t Wan na Go on with You Like That . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;3 . The Osbourne Effect&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Bernie Taupin may be one of the only lyricists ever to wind up a household name , he isn&amp;rsquo ; t the only writer that John has turned to for words . Award-winning UK writer Gary Osbourne has been a frequent collaborator , coming up with Part Time Love , Little Jeannie and global hit Blue Eyes , amongst others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;4 . The Bitch is Back&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hands down , the best backstories of any John hit is the one for this snarky rocker from 1974 . As reported in the Guardian , the musician was very well-known for throwing mega-tantrums at the time . Following one such outburst , Bernie Taupin&amp;rsquo ; s ex-wife , Maxine Feibelman , exclaimed &amp;ldquo ; Uh-oh , the bitch is back . &amp;rdquo ; Taupin loved it and turned it into the lyric for this celebrated rocker , which featured John&amp;rsquo ; s good friend John Lennon on tambourine . John has joked that it is &amp;ldquo ; my theme song . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;5 . Retirement ; not Retirement&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Easily one of the most prolific artists to come out of the classic rock era , Sir Elton has been busy in the soundtrack scene since the 1970s , hitting a career high with The Lion King in 1994 . And , yes , Gnomeo &amp;amp ; Juliet could be a career low as far as these projects go . OK , the biopic Rocketman didn&amp;rsquo ; t perform as hoped either , but it&amp;rsquo ; s all so much water off of John&amp;rsquo ; s Donald Duck costume&amp;rsquo ; s back . He has inked a deal with Universal Music Group to represent both his five decade-long catalogue as well as new music . There will doubtless be new music . Who knows , maybe there could be a tour with Taron Egerton playing John performing only music from his 1970s records . The music is certain to have a life of its own after Elton hangs up his concert platforms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;79001;TOOLONG " **36;79032;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;79070;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;79099;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynMon , 16 Sep 2019 18:05:00 **45;79130;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Picasa " **28;80025;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1087074 " /&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Scott Thompson 's Apres le De'luge&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;h3&gt;The Buddy Cole Monologues&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;80055;TOOLONG : Sept. 19 to 21 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;80090;TOOLONG : The Cultch Historic Theatre &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info&lt;/strong&gt; : From $26 , at &lt;a href= " https : **33;80126;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **27;80161;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; The character Charles Budderick &amp;ldquo ; Buddy&amp;rdquo ; Cole first turned up on screen in the groundbreaking CBC series The Kids in the Hall . The jaded , sharp-tongued , openly gay role created by Scott Thompson became one of the show&amp;rsquo ; s most celebrated characters during its 1989 to 1995 run . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From romps with Queen Elizabeth ( also played by Thompson ) and other rich and famous friends to increasingly outrageous adventures , Cole&amp;rsquo ; s monologues were unlike anything else on TV. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Buddy declared in a classic sketch : &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m an actor , singer , dancer , model , Canadian . I can make the word Canadian sound sexy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After the series , the character continued to make appearances , including recurring segments on The Colbert Report reporting from the Sochi Olympics and other locales . Thirty years on , Thompson is dusting off the Ascots and lam&amp;eacute ; smoking jackets and bringing the Buddy Cole Monologues to theatres across Canada in a show titled Apres le De'luge. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson , 60 , says it&amp;rsquo ; s particularly appropriate being Buddy now because he always envisioned the character to be around his age . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When I first started doing Buddy , it was a very different world where homophobia was so prevalent and so obvious and encouraged by society , &amp;rdquo ; said Thompson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Comedies normally had a moment where the male characters had to prove they weren&amp;rsquo ; t gay and show revulsion about it for laughs &amp;mdash ; such as Steve Martin and John Candy waking up together in Planes , Trains and Automobiles &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; and it&amp;rsquo ; s still happening . So there was this enormous hostility towards Buddy from the mainstream but also from the gay community , because he represents a kind of mirror . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;80190;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;80232;TOOLONG ... more about Vancouver **28;80267;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;80297;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Check out our comprehensive event **29;80333;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;80364;TOOLONG ... North : The latest from the B.C. TV and film **29;80400;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Modelled after a real life &amp;ldquo ; brief date , &amp;rdquo ; Buddy was bound to be controversial . The character is crass , effeminate , relentlessly critical , and full of opinions that certainly wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t pass muster at most social gatherings . Yes , Buddy is a stereotype . But Thompson says the character is also genuine , and that rubbed a lot of people the wrong way back in the day &amp;mdash ; and in the present . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Being Buddy , behaving like that , talking like that , dressing like that was , in many ways , already a joke , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A guy being like that was pretty hilarious , and you could laugh at him from a point of superiority . For all of the advances we have made against homophobia , the effeminate , older gay male is still pretty low down in the pecking order , and I made sure that Buddy reflected that awareness and threw it right back . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A fine example of this would be the Cole monologue from his gay bar called Buddy&amp;rsquo ; s , which the character says he paid for with money saved from not smoking . Addressing the breaking stories of the day about outing Hollywood stars , Buddy observes that he really hopes that Liberace isn&amp;rsquo ; t gay because he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t want him to be , and also name drops former Donald Trump and Rupert Murdoch legal counsel Roy Cohn . Disbarred for unethical conduct in 1986 , Cohn had been involved in outing homosexuals during the McCarthy era , costing people their jobs and more during the &amp;ldquo ; Lavender Scare . &amp;rdquo ; He died of AIDS on Aug. 2 , 1986. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Liberace and Roy Cohn &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s like being told Satan&amp;rsquo ; s a fag , &amp;rdquo ; says Buddy . &amp;ldquo ; Maybe that&amp;rsquo ; s why God is such a homophobe and Satan&amp;rsquo ; s so sexy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By the end of the 5-min piece , Cole has taken on gay-bashing comics like Andrew Dice Clay , declared himself the new Lenny Bruce , and announced that Buddy&amp;rsquo ; s will have no standup comedy : &amp;ldquo ; just family entertainment for the Queer Nation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson says lines like that led to people being antagonistic when he first began to play the character &amp;mdash ; and they remain so today , but for different reasons . From the political committee groupthink of the &amp;rsquo ; 80s to the &amp;ldquo ; modern puritanism&amp;rdquo ; of the present day , the world just doesn&amp;rsquo ; t seem a place to embrace Buddy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Now , young people are so conditioned to be angry at the character behaving like that because it&amp;rsquo ; s apparently insulting , as if being effeminate is wrong in itself , &amp;rdquo ; says Thompson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is an enormous amount of delusion and denial going on with people , and Buddy&amp;rsquo ; s just not part of that . Plus he&amp;rsquo ; s very sexual , and that was never something that was allowed and there has been a kind of subconscious reaction to forget what that meant in the AIDS years . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;80431;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;80473;TOOLONG ... more about Vancouver **28;80508;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;80538;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? TV and film **29;80641;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; This last point has been addressed in numerous programs lately , particularly in a powerful scene in the 2019 Netflix Tales of the City miniseries . At a dinner party , &amp;nbsp ; generational conflict flares up between a group of older men and a younger one over the fact that the impact of the AIDS epidemic doesn&amp;rsquo ; t seem to resonate with him . It&amp;rsquo ; s powerful stuff , and Thompson says that the scene brought him to tears . Buddy was born of that era. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Back then , it was such a terrible time , that there was no guarantee that I&amp;rsquo ; d make it , it was quite likely I would get it , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I practised safe sex very early on , but for the first few years after I came out no one knew . People have no memory of how it affected people , and I look around at gay men in my age group and we are so broken . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;80672;TOOLONG ... title= " Scott Thompson as Buddy Cole . " alt= " Scott Thompson as Buddy Cole . " data-portal-copyright= " Picasa " **28;80708;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1091252 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson says that he&amp;rsquo ; s waited 30 years to deal with the psychic fallout of the era , which is where the Apres le De'luge title comes from . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Likening his generation to &amp;ldquo ; Vietnam vets that no one wants to look at or acknowledge , &amp;rdquo ; he says he thinks a lot of the contemporary gay community wants the AIDS years forgotten because it somehow &amp;ldquo ; reflects badly . &amp;rdquo ; Among those who Thompson knew who didn&amp;rsquo ; t make it was the man that Buddy was modelled upon . He says that , in an ironic way , he&amp;rsquo ; s keeping him alive carrying on the character . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He was a very flamboyant , very sexual , powerful , effeminate gay man and I was so full of self-loathing at the time over my own non-classically masculine behaviour , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It meant a lot to me , even though it was a really fleeting moment in time . You reflect on those sorts of things as time goes by . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; None of the 11 monologues featured in the show have ever been seen on TV , as they were all penned after The Kids in the Hall ended , and cover the period from 1995 to the present day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The idea is that as everything around him is changing , Buddy doesn&amp;rsquo ; t because he&amp;rsquo ; s perfect , &amp;rdquo ; Thompson said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s like a rock in the middle of a river , it just has to flow around it . A kind of poignancy builds as you go on the journey , because he&amp;rsquo ; s not afraid at getting to the truth , even if it makes him look bad . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thompson says that Buddy gets away with saying things that he never would in his own standup act . From crews to directors and screenwriters , programs are in place to produce some of the most talented employees in these growing global industries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The demand for new content to populate streaming services is generating more entertainment industry jobs than ever in an already bustling business . The demand for workers with a wide-ranging skill set is stronger than ever . But is &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; the next generation of workers in Hollywood North feeding an American machine with the stories it wants at the expense of telling Canadian stories ? &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s definitely a period of changing models right now as the streamers don&amp;rsquo ; t do production deals in the same way broadcasters or major studios did , and the whole idea of what rights and global licensing is are changing the traditional models , &amp;rdquo ; said Creative B.C.
