Animation Career Review rated the Vancouver Film School the No. 1 Global Animation School and the No. 1 Canadian Animation School this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On a tour of the downtown campus with VFS executive producer and head of marketing Christopher Ian Bennett , the scope of training being offered to the next generation of Hollywood North employees is clear . Student productions are shooting on sound stages , including a room kitted out to resemble a &amp;ldquo ; Beautiful B.C.&amp;rdquo ; landscape complete with trees , shrubs and a solid rock face to climb . In another room are carefully detailed set models . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;82284;TOOLONG ... title= " A landscape sound stage inside the Vancouver Film School . Photo : Arlen Redekop/Postmedia " alt= " A landscape sound stage inside the Vancouver Film School . Photo : Arlen Redekop/Postmedia " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop " **28;82320;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1079146 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Hit the lights and see how much work goes into these models , &amp;rdquo ; said Bennett . &amp;ldquo ; You use a light source to study how it plays in the room to determine film shots . What happens when a car drives up , when someone walks outside ? It&amp;rsquo ; s better to figure it out here than when you are rolling on a crewed-up set . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The facility is preparing workers for the local and international market , said VFS managing director Jon Bell . Students come from Canada , Mexico , Korea , China , India and other locales to learn a wide range of industry-related skills . Film is still the most in-demand program , but the bottom line is different . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In terms of industry demands , the global video game industry is three times the size of film and television combined , &amp;rdquo ; said Bell . &amp;ldquo ; The skill set and employability in visual effects is one of the best , and Vancouver has one of the biggest industries in the world now . We have revised programs to reflect the industry . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Local crews operating in every capacity of production are regularly rated some of the best in the business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our talent is in global demand and there is certainly a desired trickle-down effect that comes back to domestic productions fully owned and created here , &amp;rdquo ; said Gil. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Last year , the provincial government enhanced the film incentive B.C. tax credit to include writers , which hadn&amp;rsquo ; t existed before . As that happened , Creative B.C. , Netflix and the Producers Association were able to create the new Pacific Screenwriters Program focused on building writing rooms here and supporting our writing talent to be able to work on both their own content and in service writing rooms . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;82350;TOOLONG ... title= " Christopher Bennett , the executive producer and head of marketing at the Vancouver Film School . Photo : Arlen Redekop/Postmedia " alt= " Christopher Bennett , the executive producer and head of marketing at the Vancouver Film School . Photo : Arlen Redekop/Postmedia " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop " **28;82386;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1085777 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Kim&amp;rsquo ; s Convenience and Schitt&amp;rsquo ; s Creek &amp;mdash ; both CBC programs &amp;mdash ; recently proved , there are global audiences for good stories with universal appeal . Raila Gutman at the Pacific Screenwriting Program says generating local intellectual property ( IP ) is often overshadowed by service bureau work . Writers wanting to develop their own projects usually have to go to Los Angeles or Toronto to get things moving . The program aims to change that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re training writers , not the emerging ones but mid-level and senior ones too , to develop their own IP in B.C. , &amp;rdquo ; said Gutman. &amp;ldquo ; Historically , there wasn&amp;rsquo ; t a workforce here to give the industry the impression we could have writers&amp;rsquo ; rooms based here , so they set them up in L.A. Last year , we hosted a summit where we invited Netflix , CBC , Canadian and American broadcasters and major studios out to B.C. to get them engaged with the writing community . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the same time that the industry is being introduced , writers are being taught the ins and outs of working in a writers&amp;rsquo ; room . Gutman says the program aims to provide the tools required to work in writers&amp;rsquo ; rooms . Proof of its success will be seen in an increase in locally developed and produced intellectual property . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kendrie Upton , the executive director at the Directors Guild of Canada , B.C. District Council , says the same situation of underutilized talent has applied in the past to locals helming productions . Programs such as the Directors Initiative provide vital training . The DGC B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s Director Showcase ( Sept. 6 to 8 at the Vancity Theatre and Playhouse ) showcases B.C. directed work in film and TV to provide exposure and advocate to get more Canadians in the director&amp;rsquo ; s chair . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not that it&amp;rsquo ; s not happening , Upton explains , shouting out to companies such as Nomadic Productions and programs such as Netflix&amp;rsquo ; s Travellers who employed local talent . It&amp;rsquo ; s just that the DGC B.C. recognizes challenges in getting its members noticed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our market share has traditionally clung around the 30 per cent mark , &amp;rdquo ; said Upton , a 30 year industry veteran . &amp;ldquo ; That would be not be good enough anyways , but with production so much higher now it hasn&amp;rsquo ; t increased with it . We did some market research recently where we reached out to our L.A. clients to say we&amp;rsquo ; ve got some really talented B.C. directors you could be using on your locally shot shows and the standard return was &amp;lsquo ; we don&amp;rsquo ; t know who they are . ' &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;82416;TOOLONG ... title= " Vancouver 's first film commissioner David Shepheard with executive director of the Vancouver Film &amp; Media Centre , Nancy Mott . Photo : Nick Procaylo/Postmedia " alt= " Vancouver 's first film commissioner David Shepheard with executive director of the Vancouver Film &amp; Media Centre , Nancy Mott . Photo : Nick Procaylo/Postmedia " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;82452;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1085784 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps the art of the pitch should be added to industry training manuals . Done right , you get results . Vancouver film commissioner David Shepheard notes that a recent tour of Hollywood North by various members of the U.K. entertainment industries produced exciting results . From industry organizations to government bodies , establishing relationships is key to driving local IP and employment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A lot of good business relationships were established out of us bringing over people on that tour , including a financing deal to establish a new range of kid&amp;rsquo ; s animated films using the Bear Grylls brand between Platinum Films and Burnaby-based Bron Studios animation wing , &amp;rdquo ; said Shepheard. &amp;ldquo ; This kind of content creation reflects the changing market where the globe becomes increasingly smaller and content reaches markets that wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have been reached in the past . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver born-and-raised Shawn Williamson started Brightlight Pictures in 2001 . In its 18 year-long history , the company has cultivated an impressive combination of local intellectual property and service work ranging from TV&amp;rsquo ; s The Good Doctor to Disney&amp;rsquo ; s hit Descendants properties . He echoes the sentiment on the importance of building relationships to recognize the talent base in the local industry . And he supports the proposition that the combination of service work and local intellectual property is key to keeping the industry vital and providing continuing opportunities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have multiple examples of how we were able to leverage relationships developed from service work we&amp;rsquo ; ve done on shows we didn&amp;rsquo ; t own into creative work on ones we did , &amp;rdquo ; said Williamson . &amp;ldquo ; An example is an international film we did a few years ago called Horns , starring Daniel Radcliffe and directed by a French director named Alex Aja , which lead to a developing a project called the 9th Life of Louis Drax , developed within the Canadian content system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the joys with the bulk of production of shows being produced here and internationally with the demand for new content is that those who were otherwise having challenges breaking down the doors of Hollywood are being given a shot and we have a deep talent pool . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Williamson says that they are presently crewing up something in the realm of a &amp;ldquo ; thousand technicians , actors , background people , writers and so forth&amp;rdquo ; on their shows . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Phil Klapwyk , the business representative at IATSE local 891 knows all about those jobs . While producers , writers , directors and actors may get the glory , but it&amp;rsquo ; s often the hard-working crews that make the movie getting more work . His local represents 19 departments with 135 job titles that all work in film and television production careers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For every one director that lands a job , there are usually about 120 talented technicians and artists working behind them to make their vision come to fruition , and a lot of these are people are those with correlative skills in the real world , from electricians to carpenters to make up artists . &amp;rdquo ; said Klapwyk. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is a labour market information project due to be released by the government very soon that suggests a five-per cent attrition rate throughout the industry per year up against a three to four per cent annual growth which means we need at least an eight to nine per cent workforce increase to keep up with that pace . For my 9,000 members , that means 720 jobs a year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hollywood North&amp;rsquo ; s future looks bright , although not without challenges keeping pace with predicted growth . Expect to see more and more outreach and educational efforts to entice young people to consider careers in the existing creative industries as well as those to come . As Christopher Hobbs of Vancouver custom software development firm TTT Studios notes , the city is well-positioned for new businesses in emerging entertainment technologies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because of its proven past in film , TV , gaming and digital entertainment and the infrastructure around it , there are continuing great opportunities , &amp;rdquo ; said Hobbs . &amp;ldquo ; VR ( virtual reality ) and AR ( augmented reality ) are natural fits in terms of tech development , and we can become a global leader there beyond the entertainment infrastructure . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;82482;TOOLONG " **36;82513;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;82551;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;82580;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;82611;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? No surprise the legendary Cuban vocalist Omara Portuondo ( Buena Vista Social Club ) and rising star Silvana Estrada make appearances on the John ( Beetle ) Bailey-engineered record . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They are the only other performers on the album recorded in Canada , Mexico , Cuba and Spain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alex handles every other instrumental duty on the disc and he&amp;rsquo ; s never sounded better . As he readies for an extensive round of touring across North America and elsewhere , the musician discussed the realities of breaking into markets where his music is more readily consumed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As an almost entirely Spanish language artist , his fame is far greater outside of this country than in it . He&amp;rsquo ; s fine with that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Mexico has emerged as quite the place for me in the past few years , &amp;rdquo ; said Cuba . &amp;ldquo ; According to streams on Spotify and other sites , it is the place that listens to me the most and we are , obviously , paying attention to that . It&amp;rsquo ; s the kind of place you can find any kind of music really and where they are quite open to a lot of variety in the music . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s a good fit for the artist whose work can best be described as pop/rock . Owing to his understanding of Latin American genres ranging from bolero and bachata to rancheros to son , Cuba has always worked elements of these forms into his hook-laden material . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But there are considerable influences drawn from classic pop tunesmiths like the Beatles or funk masters like Stevie Wonder turning up in gems such as his hit Directo . On Sublime , he opens with a complex rhythmic romp titled Yo No S&amp;eacute ; that could have been on an early Brazilian Tropicalismo release by Caetano Veloso or Gilberto Gil. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The artist loves the comparison , noting he still listens to a lot of recordings from that era because they are &amp;ldquo ; so real , so honest , the music is pure and it keeps it sounding alive . &amp;rdquo ; That he can write something which hearkens back to that creative hubbub is impressive . That the opening song on Sublime was an instant recording is amazing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Yo No S&amp;eacute ; was the last song on the album , written on the spot on the last day in the studio , which came from a bass line I was jamming and loved and knew I had to use , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So I was writing the lyrics while I was playing all the different parts , shouting them out and we were both rolling on the floor by the end of it blown away by the results . Essentially , the concept of the song became was Alex Cuba rehearsing with Alex Cuba , so I made this video for it that has me , in colour , and a bunch of black and white Alex Cubas playing the song . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;84011;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;84047;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The track sets the vibe for Sublime and it&amp;rsquo ; s spot on for the collection of a dozen songs ranging from the tender lead single Voz De Corazones to the easy flowing duet Solo M&amp;iacute ; a with Mexican star Leonel Garcia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dominican star Alex Ferreira and Cuban musicians Kelvis Ochoa and Pablo Milan&amp;eacute ; s also appear on the album . For those in the know , this lineup along with Portuondo and Estrada demonstrates the kind of pull that Cuba has in the upper levels of Spanish language stars . People want to perform his songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I grew up listening to people like Pablo Milan&amp;eacute ; s , who is the Cuban Bob Dylan , and Omara and others and really wrote the songs that they appear on with their spirit in mind , because their work really shaped my writing , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And when I decided to go to the next level and see if they would honour me by appearing , I was really taken about that they knew who I was and knew my work and said yes . Canada may not be the best place for putting my music forward , but the reason that my music is fresh and different is because it comes from Canada . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sublime holds a special spot in Cuba&amp;rsquo ; s heart as it is the record , he believes , that took him back home to his birth country of Cuba and reflects the journey he&amp;rsquo ; s taken to where he is today . The musician originally hails from Artemesia , Cuba , and both he and his brother , Adonis , were schooled in music by their guitar-playing music teacher father from a young age . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alex and Adonis settled in Victoria in 1989 after Alex married a Canadian he met in Cuba . The Puentes Brothers duo released a Juno-nominated debut , eventually deciding on solo careers around the early 2000s . Alex moved to his wife&amp;rsquo ; s hometown of Smithers in 2003 and has run his career from the central B.C. town since . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He says he can make music anywhere and finds the natural beauty and chill vibe completely suited to crafting his , frankly , more tropical material . He is constantly jotting down ideas , melodies and more on his phone wherever he is and that process was used on Sublime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I recorded this album in Gibsons with Garth Richardson , because Beetle Bailey said he had a great sounding room there , &amp;rdquo ; said Cuba . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So I packed up all my toys &amp;mdash ; seven guitars , congas , a standup bass , bongos , shakers , triangles and more &amp;mdash ; into my car and drove down . It took two days and I had my computer connected to the stereo and the phone on voice memos. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I had a lot of time to myself to think about things like &amp;ldquo ; oh , we need a handclap there and this would be a good place for more backing vocals. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The ultimate goal is to give each song the right vibe and Cuba feels Sublime has it in large amounts . All the technological tricks in the world can fake it . If it&amp;rsquo ; s there , you can make it happen anywhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;84083;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;84114;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **26;84152;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;84180;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span class= " s2 " &gt;&lt;a href= " **27;84211;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK **35;84240;TOOLONG class= " s1 " &gt; to report a typo. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Is there more to this story ? " data-portal-copyright= " Graham MacIndoe " **28;84487;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1076150 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;The National&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;84517;TOOLONG : Aug. 28 , 5:30 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;84552;TOOLONG : Festival Lawn at Deer Lake Park , Burnaby &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and inf&lt;/strong&gt; o : $65 at &lt;a href= " https : //www.livenation.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **28;84588;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; I Am Easy to Find is the title of the eighth album by the critically acclaimed and commercially successful American indie rock band The National . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A short 27-minute film of the same name directed by indie feature director and graphic designer Mike Mills , starring Academy Award-winning actor Alicia Vikander , arrived with the record . Using rearrangements of songs from the album as the soundtrack , the black-and-white work tells a woman&amp;rsquo ; s story from childhood to passing , touching on those moments in a life that define it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anyone familiar with the band&amp;rsquo ; s sound and , particularly , singer Matt Berninger&amp;rsquo ; s imagistic and emotional lyricism , won&amp;rsquo ; t find it surprising that they are making movies . The group&amp;rsquo ; s music is immediately cinematic and increasingly artsy . Its expansive orchestrations and Berninger&amp;rsquo ; s rounded baritone provide the soundtrack to the film , which includes subtitles . It&amp;rsquo ; s a beautifully moving work from a band with two decades of documenting human frailty and subdued rage in increasingly complex albums. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I Am Easy to Find takes all the group&amp;rsquo ; s past achievements and ups the ante considerably . Where past records put Berninger&amp;rsquo ; s voice at the centre of everything , he is matched equally by a different featured female vocalist on most of the songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cast includes heavyweights such as Ireland&amp;rsquo ; s Lisa Hannigan , French folky Mina Tindle ( Pauline de Lassus ) , This Is the Kit&amp;rsquo ; s Kate Stables , Sharon Van Etten and the Brooklyn Youth Chorus on the show-stopping Dust Swirls in Strange Light . One of the standout performances in an album loaded with them is longtime David Bowie bassist and backing singer Gail Ann Dorsey , who slays on the opening track You Had Your Soul With You . It begins what winds up being something of a 16-song conversation that comes to you from some very abstract starting points . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bassist , multi-instrumentalist Scott Devendorf said the members haven&amp;rsquo ; t forgotten how to write straight-ahead songs or being able to define them . He vehemently disagrees with any suggestion that the more experimental side projects he , Berninger , guitarist Aaron Dessner , guitarist Bryce David Dessner and drummer Bryan Devendorf are involved in have bled into The National&amp;rsquo ; s music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;84618;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;84654;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re pretty aware of what a straight-ahead song is . We write a lot of them , &amp;rdquo ; said Devendorf. &amp;ldquo ; Songs with words being pushed along with choruses , verses , poetry and structure or a piano ballad or two . But this time , working with Mike Mills on the album , he was very encouraging about us working outside of our comfort levels , and that&amp;rsquo ; s where we went . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No , this in no way means that I Am Easy to Find is a &amp;ldquo ; difficult&amp;rdquo ; record or bound to be filed further back in the future listening pile than something like 2010&amp;rsquo ; s breakout High Violet . It&amp;rsquo ; s the sound of a band going where they wanted with confidence and hitting the marks . Plus , for all its lush orchestration , it&amp;rsquo ; s not so complicated that it can&amp;rsquo ; t be delivered live . Developing the new tour strategy did involve some &amp;ldquo ; market research . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Starting back in April , we did five preview shows where we would show the film , have a short Q&amp;amp ; A and then play as much of the record as we could in the time frame , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; We only did it from start to end in New York because that was when we had the Brooklyn Youth Chorus , who don&amp;rsquo ; t tour . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From there , the band worked out ideas for the coming tour and Devendorf said it&amp;rsquo ; s been great . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Yes , the songs were constructed in such a way as to be playable , but are very vocal , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; Fortunately , our friends who joined us in the recording have been able to join us for the additional instrumentation . And we have been able to have two or three of our friends who recorded with us &amp;mdash ; Lisa Hannigan , Pauline De Lassus , Kate Stable , Gail Ann Dorsey &amp;mdash ; present for one or more of the shows and scheduling so that everyone is always overlapping . It&amp;rsquo ; s mainly been Kate and Pauline , but everyone has their own projects going too , so it needs to be flexible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The bassist admits it would be impossible to present the music on the new album without at least one additional singer and additional musicians . But that has been the case going back a few albums now , and The National can certainly work with it . The band also manages to keep making music and touring with two pairs of siblings in the same band . One need only look back at The Kinks , Oasis and others to know that family can sometimes be the worst combination for group longevity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;84690;TOOLONG ... title= " The National play Deer Lake Park in Burnaby on Aug. 28. " alt= " The National play Deer Lake Park in Burnaby on Aug. 28. " data-portal-copyright= " Graham MacIndoe " **28;84726;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1080216 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Do the many side projects &amp;mdash ; from Bryce Dessner&amp;rsquo ; s classical composing to Berninger&amp;rsquo ; s EL VY , Aaron Dessner&amp;rsquo ; s Big Red Machine , Bryan Devendorf&amp;rsquo ; s Pfarmers and the brothers Devendorf&amp;rsquo ; s LNZNDRF &amp;mdash ; help keep the peace and keep everyone feeling fresh ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Definitely , the influence of all of those side projects is always there when we get together , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; We will all be finding new things through those experiments and bringing them into the room when we are working again , and it keeps it fresh and interesting and launches new ideas . Even if some of them don&amp;rsquo ; t work out , sometimes the exercise can be really important and liberating , too . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As to whether the Dessners or the Devendorfs are the Gallagher Brothers in the band , Scott laughs heartily . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Oh , I really have to say neither . NewsNewsDaphne Bramham : After decades of promises , has Canada finally reached a tipping point ? http : **34;85274;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;85310;TOOLONG ... title= " Supporters gather in Victoria to support Wet'suwet'en chiefs who oppose the Coastal GasLink pipeline . " alt= " Supporters gather in Victoria to support Wet'suwet'en chiefs who oppose the Coastal GasLink pipeline . " data-portal-copyright= " KEVIN LIGHT " **28;85346;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1219348 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;85376;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Countless words have been written in voluminous reports with hundreds of recommendations regarding the promise that Canada&amp;rsquo ; s relationship with Indigenous people will be transformed . Often years in the making and costing millions of dollars , the reports are encyclopedic , in both the good and the dull sense . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Warmly welcomed by politicians , the full reports with their many volumes are rarely read by them or by anyone else , including journalists and experts offering sage commentary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The excuses are easy : The reports are too long . We are too busy to read more than the executive summaries . And how much easier it is to reduce it all to a simple debate over whether using the word genocide is appropriate to describe the murders and disappearances of so many Aboriginal women . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For every recommendation , promises are made to give due consideration . But after public attention has inevitably and quickly pivoted to the latest Instagram-able issues , it has been easy for politicians to decide the recommendations are too costly in dollar terms , political capital , or both . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has wasted so many opportunities . Why is anyone surprised by the disruption to national rail service , or by protests that have kept legislators and others from their work ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only surprise is that the tipping point finally forcing a resolution to generations of talks seems to be the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary chiefs&amp;rsquo ; refusal to allow a natural gas pipeline to run through their traditional territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every little thing that makes a difference &amp;mdash ; to paraphrase the subtitle of Malcolm Gladwell&amp;rsquo ; s book The Tipping Point . He argues that there are three essential requirements to tip the balance and force change : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There must be strong leaders with influential and charismatic friends , which is a good description of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en chiefs and climate activist Greta Thunberg , who has accused Canada of violating children&amp;rsquo ; s rights because of its continued support for oil and gas development . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There has to be a &amp;ldquo ; stickiness factor&amp;rdquo ; that compels an idea or phenomenon to stick in people&amp;rsquo ; s minds and influence their future behaviour . That might , in this case , include small things such as the now-ubiquitous acknowledgements at every gathering of whose unceded territory people are meeting on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The final element is context , and for this , I&amp;rsquo ; ll stick to only the most recent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eight years ago , Idle No More shut down multiple border crossings , blocked railway lines , disrupted traffic with flash mobs and garnered international attention . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It petered out when then-Prime Minister Stephen Harper promised high-level dialogue , not with Idle No More&amp;rsquo ; s female founders and leaders , but with then-Assembly of First Nations Chief Shawn Atleo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Five years ago , the Truth and Reconciliation Commission&amp;rsquo ; s 11 pages of recommendations provided a roadmap for overcoming the legacy of residential schools . &amp;nbsp ; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau committed to implementing all 94 recommendations in December 2015 . The government&amp;rsquo ; s progress is tracked online at &lt;a href= " http : **34;85412;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That raised Indigenous peoples&amp;rsquo ; expectations , as did the appointment of Jody Wilson-Raybould as justice minister . But many hopes were dashed with the government&amp;rsquo ; s purchase of the Trans Mountain Pipeline and its subsequent re-approval , as did **25;85448;TOOLONG ; s demotion and eventual ouster from the Liberal caucus following her testimony about how Trudeau tried to convince her not to prosecute SNC-Lavalin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Which brings us to the gas pipeline going through Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en territory that is backed by John Horgan&amp;rsquo ; s NDP government &amp;mdash ; the same government that less than a year ago promised to bring B.C. laws in line with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Adding to the frustrations are 1,200 murdered and missing women , health outcomes that lag other Canadians by a wide margin , and 27 years of B.C. treaty negotiations that have yielded only eight finalized agreements , involving only 38 per cent of the province&amp;rsquo ; s Indian Act bands . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And , yes , there&amp;rsquo ; s climate change that also disproportionately affects Indigenous people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Senator Murray Sinclair , who chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission , wrote in a recent blogpost that what is needed to resolve the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en pipeline dispute are &amp;ldquo ; positive acts . &amp;rdquo ; But he is not optimistic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Frankly , given Canada&amp;rsquo ; s intransigence , and the rising sense of injustice felt by Indigenous leadership throughout the country , I do not like where this is heading . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is a rich irony that among the strongest voices deriding protesters as radical activists and urging police to take action against them are themselves using the spectre of western separatism to get their way on pipeline approvals. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada is in the midst of an existential crisis with the intersection of Indigenous rights , climate change and the economy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is no simple solution . Certainly , it can&amp;rsquo ; t be solved by company-sought court injunctions enforced by police , or by any other court rulings . It hasn&amp;rsquo ; t worked before in Canada and it hasn&amp;rsquo ; t worked in other democratic societies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s future depends on federal , provincial , Indigenous , business and community leaders as well as its citizens talking in good faith and with respect about what Canada should be and could be , not only a decade from now , but a century from now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;85475;TOOLONG " **36;85506;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamThu , 20 Feb 2020 17:33:57 **45;85544;TOOLONG ... **34;85591;TOOLONG investments needed in climate-friendly infrastructure , says resources ministerhttp : **32;85627;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;85661;TOOLONG ... title= " Recognizing the importance of oil and gas " does not mean we hide from the reality of climate change , " Natural Resources Minister Seamus O'Reagan. " alt= " Recognizing the importance of oil and gas " does not mean we hide from the reality of climate change , " Natural Resources Minister Seamus O'Reagan. Court of Appeal ruling last May which said the province couldn&amp;rsquo ; t impose restrictions on the pipeline&amp;rsquo ; s contents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are all of the view to dismiss the appeal for the unanimous reasons of the Court of Appeal for British Columbia , &amp;rdquo ; Chief Justice Richard Wagner said after several hours of hearings Thursday in Ottawa . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Federal lawyers argued B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s attempt to require provincial permits for heavy oil to flow through pipelines was a clear imposition on the constitutional authority given to Ottawa over interprovincial pipelines. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Several of the judges on the Supreme Court agreed in their statements and questions throughout Thursday&amp;rsquo ; s hearings , before issuing their quick dismissal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Attorney General David Eby also called their decision &amp;ldquo ; disappointing&amp;rdquo ; and echoed Horgan&amp;rsquo ; s pledge to fight to protect the environment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " It 's &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;important to remember this was one of a suite of regulations the province put in place around toxic substances that can be brought into our province by train or pipeline or truck , " Eby said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Of that suite , there was one regulation in particular the province of Alberta &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;was concerned about so we referred that to the court . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Shahin Dashtgard , a professor in the department of earth sciences at Simon Fraser University , said Horgan has run out of options . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;87302;TOOLONG ... title= " Pipes at a Trans Mountain facility in Hope , B.C. " alt= " Pipes at a Trans Mountain facility in Hope , B.C. " data-portal-copyright= " Jonathan Hayward/The Canadian Press files " **28;87338;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1191080 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think it was a political decision that he went with , an attempt to satisfy the Green party , something that he promised them from the get-go , &amp;rdquo ; said Dashtgard , referring to the NDP and Greens&amp;rsquo ; confidence and supply agreement , in which the three Green MLAs promised to support the NDP minority government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t think there was really a leg to stand on from the beginning , &amp;rdquo ; Dashtgard said . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s an interprovincial thing that&amp;rsquo ; s always been under federal jurisdiction and now that he&amp;rsquo ; s taken it all the way to the Supreme Court , that&amp;rsquo ; s the end of it , I think . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although construction has begun , there remain other barriers to the expansion&amp;rsquo ; s completion , including a legal challenge by Indigenous communities affected by the construction . They argue they were not properly consulted by Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eby said the province is not participating in those cases and &amp;ldquo ; &lt;span class= " s1 " style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;we do n't anticipate at this stage participating &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;in those . " &lt;br&gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;George Heyman , the B.C. environment minister , said in a statement that the province is &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;reviewing conditions attached to a provincial environmental certificate for the project as directed by last year 's B.C. Court of Appeal decision . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Today 's decision provides some further context for that work , " Heyman said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;B.C . Liberal Leader Andrew Wilkinson on Thursday called for the NDP government to now throw its support behind the pipeline project . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " John Horgan knew the federal government held clear jurisdiction over the pipeline but he spent millions of dollars just in political posturing , " Wilkinson said in a statement . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " When will the NDP stop the political games and let British Columbians get to work on a project supported by a majority of people in our province ? " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Wilkinson called the government 's work to stop against the project a " total waste of B.C. taxpayer money " and demanded that Eby explain how much was spent . E&lt;/span&gt; xternal legal fees alone had reached nearly $1 million by last March 31 , Wilkinson said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eby said the government hasn&amp;rsquo ; t yet determined the final cost . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; " But I can tell you in terms of costs versus a catastrophic oil spill , bitumen spill or another toxic substance that 's brought into the province this has been a fraction of that kind of cost and our efforts to protect our environment , " Eby said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The federal Liberals argue the pipeline is needed to get more Canadian oil to foreign markets beyond the United States and bought the existing pipeline with a view to completing the expansion once the legal and political challenges were out of the way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It intends to sell it back to the private sector after the expansion is complete . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alberta Premier Jason Kenney took immediately to Twitter to express gratitude for the court decision Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Today , the Supreme Court of Canada dismissed B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s attempt to regulate the heavy oil content in a pipeline , &amp;rdquo ; he wrote . &amp;ldquo ; We are very pleased with this outcome and look forward to construction continuing on the Trans Mountain Pipeline . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s Natural Resources Minister Seamus O&amp;rsquo ; Regan said he welcomed the ruling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is a core responsibility of the federal government to help get Canada&amp;rsquo ; s resources to market and support good , middle-class jobs , &amp;rdquo ; he said in a statement Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We know this is only possible when we earn public trust and work to address environmental , Indigenous peoples&amp;rsquo ; and local concerns , which we are doing every step of the way on TMX. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the B.C. NDP government was elected in 2017 partly on a promise to oppose the expansion , it had limited options because of the Constitution . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , B.C. argued it has jurisdiction to protect the environment in its borders and since that province would bear the brunt of any damage from a spill if the pipeline ruptured , it should get a say in what can flow through it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In April 2018 , it filed a reference case with the B.C. Court of Appeal asking it to rule on whether the province could change its environment laws so that it could require permits for any heavy oil that was to flow through pipelines. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The B.C. Court of Appeal ruled in May 2019 that it could not , noting that would overstep the constitutional authority given to Ottawa . The court also noted while B.C. was trying to portray the legislation as a general change to its environment laws , it was clearly targeting the Trans Mountain expansion , since that was the only project to which the changes would apply . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The case was the catalyst that led to the federal government&amp;rsquo ; s decision to buy the existing pipeline in May 2018 for $4.5 billion . NewsPoliticsBear necessities cause havoc for B.C. Hydro customers more than once in 2019http : **36;87544;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;87582;TOOLONG ... title= " File photo of a black bear . " alt= " File photo of a black bear . " data-portal-copyright= " Postmedia Archives " **28;87618;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1082961 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;87648;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; As 2019 winds to a close , B.C. Hydro is shining a light on some of the incidents that left British Columbians in the dark , many of them caused by animals behaving badly , such as an itchy bear in Williams Lake and a clumsy eagle in Clinton . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bears exercising their ursine impulses knocked power out to B.C. Hydro customers not once but twice in 2019 , among the more unusual of some 50,000 trouble reports submitted to the utility , a spokesperson said Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And a bald eagle caused a failure northwest of Cache Creek when it dropped its lunch &amp;mdash ; a goose &amp;mdash ; directly onto a power line . The eagle&amp;rsquo ; s goose was cooked , and the same was true for the unfortunate Clinton customers who had to resort to candlelight until the power was restored . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wildlife incursions are not out of the ordinary for B.C. Hydro , but the more usual interruptions come from birds landing on exposed switches or critters gnawing on wires among the 25 to 30 power outages crews respond to every year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Beavers falling trees onto power lines is also not unheard of . That happened twice in 2019 , according to a list of unusual outages distributed by B.C. Hydro &amp;mdash ; once near Dawson Creek and once near Hazelton. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The largest animal-caused outage happened on Nov. 25 , &amp;rdquo ; said B.C. Hydro spokesperson Susie Rieder , &amp;ldquo ; when a rodent managed to shut off power to 10,850 B.C. Hydro customers in large areas of central and east Richmond . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rodent , presumably a squirrel , contacted a transformer and caused a converter fault at Cambie substation . Fortunately , power was restored within 90 minutes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t just animals knocking out the lights in B.C. in 2019 . Humans were also behind several of the utility&amp;rsquo ; s most memorable service calls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A customer in Surrey flew his drone into power lines , resulting in an outage at their home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A customer on Vancouver Island looking to surreptitiously spy on his neighbours climbed a power pole to install a security camera atop the structure . B.C. Hydro crews were alerted and the camera was swiftly removed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And this past summer , hunters near Stewart used a transmission tower for target practice , resulting in an outage for 170 customers and over $60,000 in damages . Two similar incidents also occurred near Coombs and near Qualicum Beach , as hunters literally shot the lights out on Vancouver Island . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Balloons were particularly problematic for B.C. Hydro as well in 2019 &amp;mdash ; a trouble that began as soon as the new year got underway . On New Year&amp;rsquo ; s Day in Richmond , a bundle of rogue balloons contacted power lines in Richmond , resulting in a power interruption to 20 customers . That was one of 52 outages caused by balloons this year , according to the utility &amp;mdash ; 53 if you count the big hot air balloon that struck power lines on descent in Vernon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; None of these incidents , however , affected as many people as the Northern Interior blackout in September , which was the single largest interruption of the year in terms of total number of customers in the dark at one time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The cause was a transmission circuit failure caused by a suspected lightning strike that left 124,000 customers without power in the Northern Interior , including Prince George , &amp;rdquo ; said Susie Rieder. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And let us not forget the February windstorm , in which 150,000 customers lost power in the Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island over the course of a very blustery day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Hydro reminds customers to exercise caution , not just before outages but after . Anyone who happens upon a downed or damaged power line is urged to stay back at least 10 metres and report it by calling 911. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; -- with files from Derrick Penner &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **28;87684;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **35;87714;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **28;87751;TOOLONG " class= " twitter-follow-button " data-show-count= " false " &gt;Follow **25;87781;TOOLONG &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;87808;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? The standing-offer program was indefinitely suspended in February . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among other First Nations interested in solar power , the Upper Nicola Indian Band is pursuing a proposal for a more substantial 15 megawatt solar farm on its Quilchena reserve near Merritt with Fortis B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For now , the Tsilhqot&amp;rsquo ; in project is just the second utility-sized solar plant that B.C. Hydro&amp;rsquo ; s net metering program , which allows customers to generate power that offsets their own power needs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the program allows customers to feed electricity back into B.C Hydro&amp;rsquo ; s system , and earn credits for doing so when their solar panels generate more power than they are using , Fish said the utility doesn&amp;rsquo ; t intend for net metering to become a source of provincial grid supply . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In total , Fish said some 2,400 Hydro customers have enlisted with its net metering program , mostly with small solar-power systems , generating about 17 megawatt-hours of power a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. , with some particularly sun-scorched Interior locations , has great potential for large solar projects , according to Martin Mullany , the interim executive director at Clean Energy B.C. , the main industry organization that represents private-power producers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The first lesson is that solar works in B.C. , &amp;rdquo ; Mullany said of the Tsilhqot&amp;rsquo ; in project , which serves an example for other communities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the Tsilhqot&amp;rsquo ; in , Mullany said that besides providing a business opportunity to the First Nation , having a source of electric power close to their communities helps stabilize the power grid for the entire region . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The cost of ( solar ) technology has dropped 90 per cent in the last 10 years , Mullany added . ' s most recent public accounts report&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These are revenues that are being foregone , &amp;rdquo ; said Parfitt , who obtained credit figures with a Freedom of Information request . &amp;ldquo ; Down the line , those credits are reimbursed in the form of lower royalty payments . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program was initiated as an incentive to take on more expensive extraction projects , which Parfitt argues have now become mainstream . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deep well and horizontal drilling is used extensively in hydraulic fracturing , which was used to extract natural gas from 98 per cent of wells brought into production in 2017 , according to the B.C. " data-portal-copyright= " Francis Georgian " **28;91071;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1120806 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;The utilities commission concluded in its supplementary report Tuesday that oil and gas companies provided inconclusive or conflicting data&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; to explain the &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;13-cent-a-litre margin customers pay at retail stations &lt;/span&gt;that were first identified in &lt;a href= " https : **33;91101;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;an August report&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It also noted B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s gas supply and retail outlets are owned by a small number of companies , creating an oligopoly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The commission reviewed new submissions from five major B.C. companies : Parkland Fuel Corporation , the owner of Metro Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s only refinery , located in Burnaby ; Imperial Oil Limited ; Suncor Energy ; 7-Eleven Canada and Advanced Biofuels Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The commission concluded that the price of all gas in B.C. is set by the most expensive five per cent of the province&amp;rsquo ; s supply , from Seattle , called the Pacific Northwest Spot Price . That creates a profit margin for companies that get cheaper gas from Alberta , or elsewhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The second margin is the difference between Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s price and Seattle&amp;rsquo ; s price , which has grown to 20 cents a litre since 2015. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gas companies cited increased costs for transportation , B.C. and federal fuel standards , overhead , U.S. credits , exchange rates , inflation and other factors , but the commission said that still left 10 to 13 cents per litre unexplained . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s 13 cents more that they are charging for something , presumably , they don&amp;rsquo ; t have to pay for , &amp;rdquo ; said commission chair David Morton . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The unexplained margin costs B.C. motorists approximately $490 million annually at the pumps , according to the commission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 13-cent price difference can be better explained if you consider B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s scarcity premium due to a limit in refining and pipeline capacity , as well as the profit margin built in for oil companies due to B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; oligopolistic market structure , &amp;rdquo ; said Werner Antwiler , associate professor of the University of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s Sauder School of Business , who researches gas prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " https : **34;91136;TOOLONG ... &lt;div style= " width:100% ! ; margin-top:4px ! important ; text-align:right ! important ; " &gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;91172;TOOLONG ... target= " top " class= " flourish-credit " &gt;&lt;img style= " width:105px ! important ; height:16px ! important ; border:none ! important ; margin:0 ! important ; " src= " https : **34;91207;TOOLONG ... alt= " Made with Flourish " **26;91243;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The oil and gas companies had at first fought the commission to avoid handing over sensitive data on profit margins and supply . Eventually , after subsequent security assurances , they did provide some of that information . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Morton said during the supplementary phase of the report , released Tuesday , that the companies provided only hypothetical data to explain why the 13 cent price gap was incorrect , and not actual invoices and costs the companies incurred in the province . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " The oil companies that made those arguments were not able to provide any single piece of evidence that would persuade us that was the case , " said Morton . " All they did was send us a spreadsheet , this is what a hypothetical gas company would look like . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " They did n't send us an invoice and say this is what it costs to provide a shipment in . There was no concrete evidence provided . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " At the end of the day we said we really do n't have anything definitive , so we 're not going to back off this 13-cent number . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;91271;TOOLONG ... title= " PetroCan fuelling station at East Broadway and Clark " alt= " PetroCan fuelling station at East Broadway and Clark " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop " **28;91307;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1061507 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The commission reports were less clear in breaking down the cost structure at the retail level of gas stations , which are mostly owned and operated by the major companies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Morton said retail gas pricing , which starts at a daily high around 10 a.m. and lowers to a 6 p.m. price , was impossible to break down with the data provided . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We don&amp;rsquo ; t really know what the full story is on retail sales , &amp;rdquo ; he said . Morton cited protests in Squamish and Powell River over higher gas prices than elsewhere in the province , and was unable to explain why . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The retail side warrants more investigation , he said . But the NDP government&amp;rsquo ; s cabinet order giving the commission jurisdiction to investigate gasoline pricing expired on the weekend , and it can do no further work without provincial approval . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Morton said he would be pleased if government did pass legislation that gave his commission more routine data from the oil and gas companies on supply and pricing , but it would need to come with a mandate from government to do something with that information . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Certainly if we were asked to participate further in trying to unravel this mystery , so to speak , yes it would be very helpful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;91337;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **33;91365;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;91400;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;91429;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;91460;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;91502;TOOLONG ... preps ' fuel transparency ' bill to track gas price **28;91537;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;91567;TOOLONG ... inquiry finds B.C. motorists paying at least 13 cents a litre too **25;91602;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;91629;TOOLONG ... &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is a legal basis for recovering costs in your own courts even against international parties , &amp;rdquo ; said Gage. &amp;ldquo ; The letters are a first step to establishing the moral and legal responsibility for those harms. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The &amp;ldquo ; strict liability&amp;rdquo ; approach to litigation &amp;mdash ; in which there is no proof of fault &amp;mdash ; has not been tested in Canada , according to a report to Burnaby council obtained in a Freedom of Information request by the resource sector advocate Resource Works . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pursuing legal action &amp;ldquo ; is a contentious and uncertain undertaking , with high costs , long time frame , and high uncertainty of success , &amp;rdquo ; Burnaby staff wrote . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The difference is about six cents in northern B.C. , according to the inquiry&amp;rsquo ; s findings released Friday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The commission estimated that discrepancy costs B.C. motorists $490 million annually . &lt;/p&gt; Hydro set up the customer-crisis fund in 2018 as a three-year pilot project as part of its last rate-setting application to the B.C. Utilities Commission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In its first year , however , B.C. Hydro collected $4.5 million through a 25-cents-per-month rate rider on customer bills , but only spent $1.7 million on the program , according to an interim report filed with the Utilities Commission at the end of July . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We found our program costs to be lower than we had anticipated . Hydro spokeswoman Tanya Fish said in an email response to questions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Participation during the first year of the pilot was also lower than estimated , largely due to us not having have a comparable program to base participation on . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The crisis fund paid out just $847,518 in direct grants to 2,282 customers unable to pay their bills , at an average of $371 per customer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In its initial estimate , B.C. Hydro estimated it would pay out $4.1 million to some 10,250 customers when it launched the fund in 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 6,416 applications for help from the fund that the utility received in the first year of operation was less than half the 15,000 it anticipated , according to the interim report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So the utility wants to cut the rate rider , the special charge to customers , to 13 cents per month from 25 cents , effective Oct. 1 . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Based on the ( crisis fund ) rate rider , the current ( fund ) costs and the forecast costs of operating the ( program ) for the remainder of the three-year pilot to April 30 , 2021 , B.C. Hydro expects that the revenue collected will continue to be greater than the forecast costs , &amp;rdquo ; said Fred James , Hydro&amp;rsquo ; s chief regulatory officer in a letter to the Utilities Commission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If Hydro kept collecting the rate rider at the 25-cent level , James wrote that the surplus in the account could reach as high as $7.9 million by the end of the three years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cutting it to 13 cents could still leave a $3.8-million surplus at the end , but would provide Hydro with leeway to accommodate increased participation as more customers become aware of it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The idea for the crisis fund came from the B.C. ' s federally regulated Nova Gas Transmission system , by extension of being another TransCanada subsidiary , sharing common management and having the potential for physical connections with the Nova Gas infrastructure . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NEB panel heard that Coastal GasLink&amp;rsquo ; s design included a three-km right of way between its line and Nova Gas&amp;rsquo ; infrastructure that extends into Alberta . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;That question was the subject of an NEB hearing in May . On Friday , the board ruled against Sawyer 's arguments . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Based on the totality of the record before it , the board does not find a basis to conclude that the project is properly within federal jurisdiction , &amp;rdquo ; presiding NEB member Philip Davies wrote in the decision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Put another way , the board does not find that the ( Coastal GasLink ) pipeline forms part of a single indivisible undertaking with the ( Nova Gas ) system or any other federal undertaking , &amp;rdquo ; the decision continued , and therefore did not fit under the precedent arguments that Sawyer&amp;rsquo ; s counsel relied on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the Coastal GasLink design allowed for the prospect of future linkages with the Nova Gas system , the project was being built for the sole purpose of delivering natural gas to the LNG Canada facility in Kitimat. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Rather , the ( Coastal GasLink ) project is a local work and undertaking properly regulated by the province of B.C. , &amp;rdquo ; the NEB decision concluded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The Coastal GasLink project , a 48-inch diameter , 670-km natural-gas pipeline , is a crucial link in the $40-billion LNG Canada liquefied natural gas development being led by Shell Canada that has been approved by regulators and received a final investment decision by investors last fall . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The NEB hearing involved 13 participants and included the filing of evidence by relevant parties and included written and oral arguments on the question whether the Coastal GasLink project forms part of a federal undertaking as contemplated by Section 92 of the Constitution Act . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;In its decision , the NEB found that , based on the evidence it heard , the Coastal GasLink project " is properly regulated by the province of British Columbia . And those prices changed at least three times that day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the morning of Canada Day &amp;mdash ; notorious for price jumps at the pump &amp;mdash ; the Super Save was selling for 26 cents a litre less than the Petro-Canada on Broadway in Kitsilano six kilometres away . One , John Sliziak , said he knew he was paying more than across the road but was getting a five-cent-a-litre discount and found Super Save gas to be &amp;ldquo ; sluggish . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Super Save , Dan Sims and Edna David said they were driving past when they noticed the gas was cheaper than anywhere else , while Brant Dorman found out the price from a gas-pricing website . None knew how gasoline was priced , though Sims &amp;mdash ; originally from New Zealand &amp;mdash ; said the price fluctuations &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;were very noticeable&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; here compared to back home . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a major city that pays more for regular gas than any other in North America &amp;mdash ; peaking in late April at an average 172.9 cents a litre &amp;mdash ; these wild and localized price fluctuations get noticed . The provincial government&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;96004;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Gasoline and Diesel Price Inquiry&lt;/a&gt; is set for release in late August against a backdrop of growing consumer concern and increasing retail margins . Coast Capital Savings last month released a phone survey that found gas prices in Metro Vancouver were affecting the ability of half the respondents to save , while a report released Wednesday shows the &lt;a href= " https : **33;96039;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;retail margin for Vancouver gas stations&lt;/a&gt; is 8.4 cents a litre higher than the average in other western Canadian cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;96074;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " **39;96116;TOOLONG ... prices rose with land costs but full differentials unexplained : **27;96157;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " **39;96186;TOOLONG ... gas price inquiry boosts confidential status , but firms still **30;96227;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " **39;96259;TOOLONG ... companies refuse to cough up profit margins to B.C. **28;96300;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;96330;TOOLONG ...
