" data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;96496;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1047860 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Arco Fuels opened salvo in late ' 90s gas war&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gas-price wars first came to Vancouver in the summer of 1998 when U.S.-based Arco Fuels bought a string of Lower Mainland gas stations and began selling discounted gas that it barged in from a refinery in Washington state . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before that , gas stations would change their price infrequently , usually when there was a significant change in the price of crude oil or a tax change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Arco began offering cheaper gas , the big players &amp;mdash ; Petro-Canada , Shell , Esso , Chevron and Husky &amp;mdash ; fought back hard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This led to the gas war , with prices at one time dipping below 30 cents a litre . Some of the independent gas stations couldn&amp;rsquo ; t compete and closed , but the big companies hung in and Arco left the market in 2001 . From that point on , local gas stations began monitoring each other&amp;rsquo ; s prices more closely , changing them accordingly , and the price wars never really went away . And the cut-price retailers still exist in the form of Super Save , Costco and Safeway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96526;TOOLONG ... title= " Dec. 16 , 1998 -- Arco gas stations in Langley ( 208th Ave ) had customers lining up for 35 cent a litre gas . " alt= " Dec. 16 , 1998 -- Arco gas stations in Langley ( 208th Ave ) had customers lining up for 35 cent a litre gas . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;96562;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1047985 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to the Kent Group&amp;rsquo ; s 2018 National Retail Petroleum Site Census , the number of gas stations in the Lower Mainland is relatively stable at 582 &amp;mdash ; 432 in Metro Vancouver and 150 in the Fraser Valley . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the Kent report said the ownership landscape was changing , with traditional pit-to-pump operators &amp;mdash ; those responsible for extraction , refining , transportation and retailing &amp;mdash ; getting out of retail . In 2016 , Esso sold the bulk of its Metro Vancouver stations to 7-Eleven and Parkland Fuels . In 2017 , Chevron sold its B.C. retail assets to Parkland , including Metro Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s only refinery , and at the start of 2019 Husky announced it was considering selling its retail operations and its refinery in Prince George , the second of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s two refineries. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Werner Antweiler , an economics professor at UBC&amp;rsquo ; s Sauder School of Business , said profit margins are higher in refining than in retail and refiners are less interested in controlling the process from extraction to sales at the pump , preferring to allow companies or individuals with expertise in storefront retail to take over . This is because gas stations are more and more reliant on food and drink sales and car washes to make more profit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the 1980s , most gas stations were owned and operated by one of the big players . Now , across B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;1,368 gas stations , &lt;/span&gt; the decision on what to charge at the pump depends on the relationship between the station operator and the supplier of fuel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More gas stations are independently owned , with owners selling fuel under the banner of a recognized brand and deciding themselves what price to charge . Generally speaking , in B.C. about half the gas stations set their own prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dhillon said part of his job is to check the prices at nearby gas stations three times a day and report the information to Super Save&amp;rsquo ; s Surrey head office . He is then told what price to set and makes the change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Parkland Fuel Corporation &amp;mdash ; with 180 Chevron stations , 46 Esso stations and 27 Fas Gas stations in B.C. &amp;mdash ; has a price-control centre for its directly controlled stations where staff &lt;strong&gt; &lt;/strong&gt; gather price information from retailers across the province and set prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Antweiler said a lot of &amp;ldquo ; time-of-day pricing&amp;rdquo ; goes on . For example , prices will be higher during peak driving hours and lower in the evening , as retailers try to maintain their sales volumes , hoping to draw in people who might also buy a litre of milk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96592;TOOLONG ... title= " Gas on sale for 139.9 at the Super Save gas station at 12th Ave . and Clark Drive in Vancouver , B.C .. , July 3 , 2019. " alt= " Gas on sale for 139.9 at the Super Save gas station at 12th Ave . and Clark Drive in Vancouver , B.C .. , July 3 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;96628;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048035 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Retail margin easier to calculate than refining margin&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The smell of gasoline fills the night air at Petro-Canada&amp;rsquo ; s Fourth and Cypress station as a delivery driver pours 40,000 litres of fuel into three below-ground tanks &amp;mdash ; one for each of the three grades of fuel for sale . Generally , regular gas makes up 90 per cent of sales ; however , in some areas , like Richmond , that percentage is less . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a Denwill Enterprises truck , though if you look closely at the tank you can just make out an old Chevron sign , likely painted over when Chevron sold its Metro Vancouver assets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The operator , in blue coveralls with a high-visibility vest and wearing thick black gloves , measures the depth of each tank with a simple long rod , then signs off on the order . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96658;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;96694;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; He says one load filled one station and the delivery took around an hour to complete . The company&amp;rsquo ; s trucks run around the clock servicing Petro-Canada , Shell , Chevron and Costco in the Lower Mainland . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cost to deliver this load is one small part of the complicated set of commodity prices , refining and transportation costs and profit used to calculate what you pay at the pump on any given day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It starts with the crude oil used by refineries in Alberta , Burnaby and Washington state to meet British Columbia&amp;rsquo ; s roughly 5.2-billion-litre yearly demand for refined gasoline &amp;mdash ; enough to fill over 2,000 Olympic-sized pools . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The refiners add their refining cost , including their profit , to the cost of the oil , and then add the cost of transportation to a storage terminal where refiners charge their &amp;ldquo ; rack price&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; or wholesale price &amp;mdash ; to gas stations . The rack is simply the physical location where delivery trucks get filled . In Burnaby , there are 10 racks at three locations ( Parkland , Shell and Imperial ) that supply all the Lower Mainland , with Imperial being the largest provider . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When coming up with the rack price , the refiners also take into account supply &amp;mdash ; for example , if a refinery is running at reduced capacity , the price will be higher &amp;mdash ; and what the spot price for gasoline is on the Pacific Northwest commodity market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rack price minus the spot price of a barrel of oil reveals the refiner&amp;rsquo ; s margin , while the pump price minus the rack price and taxes reveals the retailer&amp;rsquo ; s margin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Within that refiner&amp;rsquo ; s margin is a complex set of production components that the big refiners are reluctant to share . The gasoline price inquiry is currently dealing with B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s major refiners , assuring them those details would be kept secret once they are handed over to the inquiry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the retailer&amp;rsquo ; s margin is simpler to understand , since it involves just the cost of operating the gas station and getting the gas from the terminal rack to the pump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96724;TOOLONG ... title= " Gas trucks fill up at a rack at Imperial Oil 's facility in Burnaby , July 3 , 2019. " alt= " Gas trucks fill up at a rack at Imperial Oil 's facility in Burnaby , July 3 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;96760;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048037 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rack prices are not secret &amp;mdash ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;96790;TOOLONG ... and &lt;a href= " https : **32;96825;TOOLONG ... posting them daily on their websites &amp;mdash ; and can vary as much as 10 cents on any given day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The amount the retail gas station pays at the rack can vary a bit , with some receiving a few cents discount if they buy a lot of gas , and others paying a few cents more for the cost of injecting additives for branded gasoline like Shell , Chevron , Petro-Canada and Husky . Super Save and Costco don&amp;rsquo ; t inject additives , which is one reason they can generally sell for less at the pump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96859;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;96895;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; For example , on July 5 , the rack price in Vancouver was 89.5 cents a litre and the average retail price of the day was 154.9 cents a litre . In Vancouver , you pay taxes of 44.39 cents a litre , plus five per cent sales tax . So the average gas retailer was making a margin on the day of 13.26 cents a litre , give or take a few cents for volume or additives. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Antweiler said the profit in retail is all about volume , and what one charges over the course of the day is a balancing act that factors in that a lower price brings more people into the station to buy other things and maybe get a car wash . The average Metro Vancouver gas station sells about four million litres of fuel a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Last month , the B.C. Utilities Commission inquiry commissioned Vancouver-based Deetken Group to provide &lt;a href= " https : **33;96925;TOOLONG ... primer&lt;/a&gt; on B.C. 's market for refined petroleum&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to the report , Vancouver gas stations pay a higher rack price than stations in any other city in Western Canada . They also set a higher margin on their sales of gas than in those cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A comparison of B.C. to other parts of Western Canada reveals that wholesale gasoline prices ( the rack price ) in B.C. have risen above historical price differentials , and prices in Vancouver have experienced a more significant increase when compared to average prices in other western Canadian cities , &amp;rdquo ; said the report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The report states that since 2015 , the rack price difference between Vancouver and the rest of Western Canada has risen as much as 15 cents a litre . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The report said retail margins fluctuate frequently on a month-to-month basis , making it hard to discern systemic changes . However , the report looked at a six-month rolling average and found &amp;ldquo ; that retail margins in Vancouver specifically have risen above the average in the Western region and those observed in Kamloops . Vancouver appears to have outpaced the growth in retail margin compared to the rest of Western Canada since 2015 , a year after crude prices plunged . Victoria and Abbotsford have followed suit . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A report filed to the inquiry by Parkland Fuels states that retail margin is not the same as a profit margin and must take into account B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s higher land values and property taxes , its higher minimum wage and high credit-card processing costs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Antweiler adds that the loss of several gas stations in Vancouver &amp;mdash ; particularly on the westside &amp;mdash ; over the past few years has had an effect on margins . There is less competition , so prices can be higher . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , he said , the bigger reason for the higher margins was simply the &amp;ldquo ; spillover from the housing market&amp;rdquo ; because land , leasing and property taxes are now so much higher here than elsewhere in Western Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Deetken Group&amp;rsquo ; s latest report , released Wednesday , &lt;a href= " https : **33;96960;TOOLONG ... the increased retail margins&lt;/a&gt; were due almost entirely to higher land and credit-card costs . So far this year , the retail margin for Vancouver gas stations is 8.4 cents a litre higher than the average in other western Canadian cities . It was 5.9 cents a litre higher in 2018 . The Deetken Group found that 1.4 cents a litre of that 8.4-cents-a-litre difference could not be attributed to land or other costs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;96995;TOOLONG ... title= " Gas being pumped into a Rover TC 2000 at the Super Save station at 12th and Clark Drive on July 3. " alt= " Gas being pumped into a Rover TC 2000 at the Super Save station at 12th and Clark Drive on July 3. " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;97031;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048112 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the inquiry is not expected to offer any price predictions , Antweiler expects prices to increase over time because of the growing population and car use in the Lower Mainland , coupled with continuing supply problems . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;h3&gt;GAS BY THE NUMBERS&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; &lt;strong&gt;46 billion : &lt;/strong&gt; The National Energy Board says Canadians burned through 46 billion litres of gasoline in 2018 &amp;mdash ; four billion litres more than in 2013. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; &lt;strong&gt;24.6 million : &lt;/strong&gt; According to Statistics Canada , there were 24.6 million &amp;ldquo ; road motor vehicles&amp;rdquo ; registered in 2017 . So , an average Canadian driver in a car with a 70-litre tank burned through 26 tanks a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; &lt;strong&gt;2.4 million : &lt;/strong&gt; &amp;nbsp ; In 2017 there were 2.4 million passenger vehicles registered in B.C. , which is 330,000 more than four years earlier . The average British Columbian driver in a car with a 70-litre tank burned through 30 tankloads a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; &lt;strong&gt;$3,150 : &lt;/strong&gt; At an average price of 150 cents a litre , that&amp;rsquo ; s $3,150 a year . The same person living in Edmonton paying $1 a litre would be spending $2,100 a year on gas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;97061;TOOLONG ... title= " The first gas station in Canada , at Cambie and Smithe streets in Vancouver . It opened in June 1907. " alt= " The first gas station in Canada , at Cambie and Smithe streets in Vancouver . It opened in June 1907. " data-portal-copyright= " Imperial Oil " **28;97097;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048034 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;FIRST GAS STATION&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first gas station in Vancouver , as described by the late city archivist James Matthews , opened in June 1907 at the southeast corner of Cambie and Smithe alongside an Imperial Oil office . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Until that time , the few gasoline-powered vehicles in the city had been fuelled with a pail out of a tub of gasoline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That first pump dispensed gas from an old 60-litre kitchen hot-water tank , via a &amp;ldquo ; length of rubber garden hose , &amp;rdquo ; and was bought for 20 cents a gallon and sold for 40 cents a gallon &amp;mdash ; just under 10 cents a litre , which would have been very expensive at the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;97127;TOOLONG " **36;97158;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;97196;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/i&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;i&gt;Is there more to this story ? " data-portal-copyright= " Amber Bracken " **28;97408;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1048023 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is &amp;ldquo ; substantial evidence&amp;rdquo ; that vulnerable women face increased violence in boomtowns full of transient labourers building big resource projects . It&amp;rsquo ; s a concern raised by the Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls report and one that could intensify with the approval of the Trans Mountain pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Work camps , or &amp;lsquo ; man camps , &amp;rsquo ; associated with the resource extraction industry are implicated in higher rates of violence against Indigenous women at the camps and in the neighbouring communities , &amp;rdquo ; says the report , released in June after the national commission gathered testimony from 1,500 people , including survivors and relatives of murdered and missing women . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Increased crime levels , including drug- and alcohol-related offences , sexual offences , and domestic and &amp;lsquo ; gang&amp;rsquo ; violence , have been linked to &amp;lsquo ; boom town&amp;rsquo ; and other resource development contexts . &amp;hellip ; There is an urgent need to consider the safety of Indigenous women consistently in all stages of project planning . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The vast majority of resource workers are law-abiding and the large projects they work on are important for the economy , but now that the &lt;a href= " https : **33;97438;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Trans Mountain pipeline has been approved&lt;/a&gt; , towns along its route need to take precautions to protect women , experts say . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Much research has been done on the negative impacts of suddenly bringing in a large group of people to a new place when they don&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily have a clear connection to the local community . It&amp;rsquo ; s been highlighted by the MMIWG Commission , which pointed out the negative consequences can disproportionately hurt Indigenous women and girls , &amp;rdquo ; Premier John Horgan told Postmedia. &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the responsibility of governments in all jurisdictions to ensure public safety and to prevent violence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although he provided no specifics , Horgan said his NDP government would work with local communities to prevent violence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Horgan is among those opposed to Trans Mountain , which Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said would &amp;ldquo ; have shovels in the ground&amp;rdquo ; this year after the federal government gave its second approval in mid-June to twin the pipeline from Alberta to Burnaby. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some B.C. First Nations , including the Cheam and Whispering Pines , have signed benefit agreements that will provide money and jobs from the project , while other Indigenous groups adamantly oppose the pipeline , largely over environmental concerns . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;97473;TOOLONG ... title= " Grand Chief Stewart Phillip , president of the Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs , &lt;a href= " https : **32;97539;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;said in June&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The MMIWG report calls on industries to consider the safety of Indigenous women during the planning and construction phases of resource projects . It encourages companies , governments and service providers to work together to expand social infrastructure in communities , which includes &amp;ldquo ; ensuring that policing , social services and health services are adequately staffed and resourced. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trans Mountain has &amp;ldquo ; met extensively with communities&amp;rdquo ; where construction will occur along the pipeline , and has a worker code of conduct for its employees , spokeswoman Ali Hounsell said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Community safety is a top priority for Trans Mountain , &amp;rdquo ; she said , adding the company understands the importance of ensuring the presence of temporary workers and worker accommodation is managed and that related social effects are minimized . That includes any potential impacts on Indigenous groups , Indigenous women and girls and other vulnerable groups , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The issues of harassment , respectful behaviour , lawfulness , drugs and alcohol , violence and possession of weapons are directly and overtly covered in the code of conduct . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trans Mountain said it provided information to key organizations , including Indigenous groups , about the number of employees and where they would live in each community . It has also held meetings with local governments and service agencies , and noted it is a National Energy Board condition that the company monitor the socioeconomic effects of the pipeline construction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Trans Mountain will gather information about Indigenous social experiences during construction , including those relating to worker accommodation , worker conduct , as well as Indigenous social and cultural well-being , &amp;rdquo ; Hounsell said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;97573;TOOLONG ... title= " Tanks at the Trans Mountain Westridge Marine Terminal , Burnaby , in 2016. " data-portal-copyright= " Gerry Kahrmann " **28;97609;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1038234 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indigenous advocate Connie Greyeyes said she is not against pipelines and knows many honourable resource workers where she lives in Fort St. John , the home of several big projects . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But she has also &amp;ldquo ; had so many interactions with women who are assaulted by people who they didn&amp;rsquo ; t know , who were here as workers . &amp;rdquo ; This could be curtailed , she argued , if industry , government and communities provided more resources to vulnerable women . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; While I understand that progress happens , there has to be solutions to lessen the impacts on women and girls , &amp;rdquo ; Greyeyes said . &amp;ldquo ; This was never an attack on people or an industry , but it&amp;rsquo ; s about raising awareness that there are things that need to change . Provincial Health Services Authority . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This has largely been attributed to the influx of hundreds to thousands of temporary workers who are often young , male and single , have high disposable incomes , and spend long stretches of time in isolated camp settings , &amp;rdquo ; says the report , The Social Determinants of Health Impacts of Resource Extraction and Development in Rural and Northern Communities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Family violence and economic and housing insecurity are reported impacts of resource development , which are factors that are known to contribute to the entry of individuals into the sex trade . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Women are made vulnerable by the combination of exclusion from high-paying resource jobs and having to make ends meet in a town where the cost of living is rising , Greyeyes added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The majority of work in the resource industry is for men . And you try to live as a single mom in Fort St. John waitressing , then you are living in poverty , &amp;rdquo ; said Greyeyes , a case manager with the Indian Residential School Survivors Society . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The non-profit Women&amp;rsquo ; s Resource Society spends thousands running a small food bank in Fort St. John , and could use some financial help . She encouraged large companies doing temporary work in small towns to help fund organizations that assist with housing , addictions , counselling and job training . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There has been progress on this front . Shell , which runs a large gas project outside Fort St. John , hired Greyeyes and another woman in 2018 to speak to its workers about sexual harassment and other abuse in the workplace . And Black Swan , an energy company with an operation near Fort St. John , has &amp;ldquo ; invested heavily&amp;rdquo ; in the community , she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;97639;TOOLONG ... title= " Aluminum stacked on the wharf at Kitimat B.C. , ready to be shipped to market from Rio Tinto 's aluminum smelter . " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop " **28;98050;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1045236 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;98080;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; VICTORIA &amp;mdash ; The companies behind most of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s major gas stations are refusing to provide details about their profit margins to a government-ordered inquiry into retail gasoline prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Husky Energy , Suncor Energy and Shell Canada &amp;mdash ; with a combined almost 500 gas stations under retail brand names that include Petro-Canada and Esso &amp;mdash ; declined to give the independent B.C. Utilities Commission information about their retailing margins , which would show how much money they make per litre of gasoline at the pump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Husky called the information &amp;ldquo ; commercially sensitive and confidential , &amp;rdquo ; while Suncor replied that it &amp;ldquo ; is not prepared to provide its retailing margins at controlled sites as this information is competitively sensitive . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Due to the confidential and commercially sensitive nature of such information , Shell is not in a position to provide specific information regarding its retail and wholesale gasoline and diesel retail margins , &amp;rdquo ; Shell Canada said in its written submission to the commission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The three companies are among the largest players in B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s retail gas market . Their refusal to volunteer key data may prove problematic for the commission inquiry , which was ordered in May by the provincial government to examine the factors behind record high gas prices in the Lower Mainland . Premier John Horgan has said he wanted to know if price gouging was at play . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;We will continue to cooperate and to provide information to the BCUC that is not competitively sensitive , " Suncor spokesperson Paul Newmarch said in a statement Tuesday . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Husky spokesperson Kim Guttormson said the commission is unable to safeguard the information to the company&amp;rsquo ; s satisfaction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Under its governing legislation and the inquiry mandate from the B.C. government , the BCUC was unable to provide an appropriate level of confidentiality for the information , " he wrote . " We continue to discuss the issue with the BCUC. " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Commission hearings begin next week in Vancouver . The government &lt;a href= " https : **33;98116;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;forbid the commission&lt;/a&gt; from examining the role of provincial taxes on the price of gasoline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gas prices spiked to more than $1.70 per litre in the Lower Mainland in May , but have since declined to the $1.40 to $1.50 range . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;98151;TOOLONG ... title= " The Husky at 7389 River Rd. in Delta was selling as at 178.9 on April 23. " alt= " The Husky at 7389 River Rd. in Delta was selling as at 178.9 on April 23. " data-portal-copyright= " Francis Georgian " **28;98187;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1003691 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; 7-Eleven Canada , which operates 124 retail gas stations in B.C. , was the only international retailer to provide profit margin data on gasoline and diesel . It asked the utilities commission to keep the information confidential , and redacted the figures from its publicly posted written reply . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Release of such information to the public , including suppliers and competitors of 7-Eleven , would harm 7-Eleven&amp;rsquo ; s economic interests , compromise its relationships with suppliers , harm its competitive position , and/or provide an undue advantage to its competitors and suppliers , &amp;rdquo ; the company wrote . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is also in the interests of the administration of justice that the commission receive commercially sensitive information in confidence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Super Save Gas , a smaller player with 40 gas stations in B.C , also handed over financial data confidentially . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The National Energy Board , in its submission , said the refining margin on regular gasoline in Vancouver in April averaged 52.1 cents per litre , roughly double the Canadian average refining margin . The retail margin was a further 10.5 cents a litre , roughly 54 per cent higher than the Canadian average , according to the NEB . Transit , provincial and federal taxes add another 52 cents per litre in Metro Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The BCUC could compel testimony and documents from companies as part of its review . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The inquiry panel is currently reviewing these submissions and will determine if further information is required once the review has been completed , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;chair and CEO David Mortin said in a statement . &lt;/span&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If part of a submission has been identified as &amp;lsquo ; commercially sensitive&amp;rsquo ; , the BCUC is required to safeguard the confidential information . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The oil and gas companies offered various explanations for the price of gas and diesel at the pumps in their written submissions , with many citing U.S. benchmarks , limited capacity on the existing Trans Mountain Pipeline , the increased cost of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s low-carbon gasoline standards , a rising minimum wage , and other operational cost pressures . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suncor was one of several companies that blamed the federally owned Trans Mountain Pipeline for changes that have limited both the flow of crude and refined oil and gas for use in B.C. markets . Premier John Horgan has said he has talked to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau about trying to get more refined gas to B.C. through the existing pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;98217;TOOLONG ... title= " Tanks at the Trans Mountain Westridge Marine Terminal , Burnaby , November 29 2016. s terminals in British Columbia by approximately 30-36 ( million litres ) per month , which resulted in an increase in the more costly transportation of these products by rail and truck , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;98283;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;wrote Suncor&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The transportation of gasoline and diesel via truck and rail has increased significantly since 2015 &amp;hellip ; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As a result of pipeline apportionment on the Trans Mountain Pipeline , Imperial has : increased the amount of refined products it ships to British Columbia by rail and marine vessel , which are typically more expensive means of transportation than transportation by pipeline ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Parkland Fuel Corp. , which operates B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s largest refinery in Burnaby , said Trans Mountain is the only viable way to get the light crude it needs to refine into gasoline , but it can not get enough product . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because of capacity constraints on the Trans Mountain Pipeline and the method used to allocate capacity on the pipeline , the refinery is often forced to purchase space ( if possible ) from other shippers , which comes at a significant premium over tariff rates , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You wonder why Canadians are cynical about the way this government is dealing with the climate crisis , &amp;rdquo ; Weaver said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Government , however , is betting on being able to earn credit for helping countries displace more carbon-intensive energy with lower greenhouse-gas-emission LNG. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; LNG Canada&amp;rsquo ; s facility will help bring a cleaner Canadian energy source to replace coal in some of the world&amp;rsquo ; s fastest-growing economies , &amp;rdquo ; said Navdeep Bains , the federal minister of innovation , science and economic development , whose Strategic Innovation Fund will put up the $220 million for the high-efficiency turbines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; LNG Canada CEO Andy Calitz said the payment will enable the company to develop &amp;ldquo ; the lowest carbon content LNG for export in the world today . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To Weaver , however , the spending is still a subsidy to what will become B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s single-largest source for carbon dioxide emissions and one of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s biggest , in addition to other tax breaks and support that the industry has received . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Renewable energy proponents have leaned on the LNG sector to electrify its process as much as possible to reduce the industry&amp;rsquo ; s greenhouse-gas impacts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last fall , when LNG Canada announced its final investment decision , Clean Energy B.C. called on the province to &amp;ldquo ; seize the opportunity to extensively electrify the existing fossil fuel infrastructure as much as possible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a white paper , the organization , which represents B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s private-power producers , argued that&amp;nbsp ; electrifying LNG , from drilling natural gas in the northeast to transporting it by pipeline for processing in Kitimat , could reduce total emissions of conventional LNG production by up to 65 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Monday , Clean Energy B.C. executive director Martin Mullany said they understand that LNG Canada&amp;rsquo ; s timelines are too short to electrify the process to compress and freeze natural gas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Hydro wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have enough time to plan for , submit to an environmental review , then build an additional power transmission line to deliver the amount of electricity such a plant would need , Mullany said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , he argued there is still time to make sure the upstream natural gas drilling , processing and pipeline are powered by electricity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If the federal government wants to spend funds subsidizing a project where a final investment decision has been made , that is their choice , &amp;rdquo ; Mullany said in an emailed response to questions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We think it would have been better spend on electrifying the upstream value chain , but perhaps it is not an either/or decision , &amp;rdquo ; Mullany said . &amp;ldquo ; Perhaps they intend to fund electrification as well . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;98905;TOOLONG " **36;98936;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;98974;TOOLONG " &gt;tw ... &lt;/p&gt; Derrick PennerTue , 25 Jun 2019 15:15:40 **45;99003;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " THE CANADIAN PRESS/Jonathan Hayward " **28;101640;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 996055 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; VICTORIA &amp;mdash ; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s fisheries minister says he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know about the &amp;ldquo ; gaps&amp;rdquo ; B.C. keeps saying exist in Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s oil spill response plan , though the province insists it has been highlighting them for more than a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fisheries and Oceans Minister Jonathan Wilkinson said his government doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know why Premier John Horgan again cited &amp;ldquo ; gaps in the ocean protection plan&amp;rdquo ; at a news conference Tuesday . Horgan was responding to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s re-approval for the expansion of the Trans Mountain pipeline expansion from Alberta to B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To be honest with you , I&amp;rsquo ; m not sure we fully understand what gaps the province is referring to , &amp;rdquo ; Wilkinson said Wednesday . &amp;ldquo ; But we have said to them repeatedly we are more than open to have a conversation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilkinson said he has a good relationship with the B.C. government , monthly discussions with Horgan and talked to provincial officials on Wednesday . Yet , the &amp;ldquo ; gaps&amp;rdquo ; remain ill-defined , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If B.C. can more clearly articulate to us the specific issues they are concerned about and some of the ideas they &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa just finished a third phase of consultations with First Nations communities , in which 60 officials from 13 federal departments held 402 meetings with Aboriginal groups with the goal to amend the Trans Mountain plans where possible to address their concerns . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When asked how it&amp;rsquo ; s possible the federal government could still be unclear about B.C. concerns regarding oil spill response after a year of intense B.C. community consultations , Wilkinson pointed to Premier Horgan&amp;rsquo ; s longtime political opposition to the pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think the B.C. government has made no secret of the fact that it has opposed this project , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; As they said during the election campaign , they were intending to use all the tools in the tool box . I think there is an increasing recognition on the part of the premier and his government that the pipeline rests in federal jurisdiction . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;101670;TOOLONG ... title= " The Coast Guard on the scene of a spill in English Bay April 15 , 2016. " alt= " The Coast Guard on the scene of a spill in English Bay April 15 , 2016. " data-portal-copyright= " Photo by Bryce Westlund , SKY Helicopters " **28;101706;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 449138 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Environment Minister George Heyman said he&amp;rsquo ; s surprised Ottawa refuses to acknowledge B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s concerns about marine response after almost two years of meetings among ministers , deputy minsters and provincial officials , as well concerns put into letters to federal departments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I honestly can&amp;rsquo ; t explain why Minister Wilkinson would say they don&amp;rsquo ; t know or are not clear , &amp;rdquo ; said Heyman. &amp;ldquo ; We were pretty clear in our written submissions . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. has identified five gaps . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They include wanting a &amp;ldquo ; transparent and comprehensive emergency towing strategy that has a clear requirement regarding response times to ensure that towing capacity is available , &amp;rdquo ; said Heyman. &amp;ldquo ; We think that should be completed and it hasn&amp;rsquo ; t been and it&amp;rsquo ; s not a condition of the recent decision . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The province also &amp;ldquo ; needs some clarity on enhanced cost recovery provisions in the event of a spill&amp;rdquo ; so that First Nations , local communities and the provincial government get &amp;ldquo ; guaranteed fair and timely access to funds&amp;rdquo ; and don&amp;rsquo ; t have to wait for lengthy federal reimbursement procedures , said Heyman . He pointed to the Heiltsuk Nation&amp;rsquo ; s frustrations getting compensation from Ottawa after helping to contain the Nathan E. Stewart diesel spill near Bella Bella in 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;101736;TOOLONG ... title= " An aerial view of the Nathan E. Stewart tug , which went aground spilling diesel fuel into waters claimed by the Heiltsuk Nation territory . " alt= " An aerial view of the Nathan E. Stewart tug , which went aground spilling diesel fuel into waters claimed by the Heiltsuk Nation territory . " data-portal-copyright= " Marilyn Slett " **28;101772;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 755123 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two other B.C. concerns were partly addressed by Ottawa as part of its approval announcement &amp;mdash ; support for co-developing community response plans to a spill in specific areas , and funding to train and purchase marine spill equipment for local communities and First Nations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Heyman said that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t go far enough and B.C. wants specific geographic response plans instead of regional plans , and a long-term commitment to Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s equipment funding instead of the current five-year promise . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. also wants more transparent information from Ottawa on the types and volumes of substances being transported by rail , pipeline and marine vessels . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The federal government has promised a $1.6 billion oceans protection plan that includes new Canadian Coast Guard ships to respond to oil spills faster and with more on-scene environmental cleanup tools . It also reopened the Kitsilano Coast Guard base , installed six new radar stations , is mapping of high-traffic commercial waterways , and will spend more than $220 million to protect endangered killer whales by reducing vessel noises , expand buffer zones and restricting chinook salmon fishing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New measures announced Tuesday with the pipeline approval include real-time marine information for First Nations communities , fish habitat restoration and long-term monitoring of the Salish Sea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s continued concerns are echoed by environmental groups . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;101802;TOOLONG ... title= " Minister of Environment and Climate Change Strategy George Heyman at a February 2018 news conference in Victoria . " alt= " Minister of Environment and Climate Change Strategy George Heyman at a February 2018 news conference in Victoria . " data-portal-copyright= " CHAD HIPOLITO " **28;101838;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 779707 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critics of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; world class&amp;rdquo ; spill response often point to the International Tanker Owners Pollution Federation&amp;rsquo ; s estimate that even in ideal conditions in oceans around the world , only 10 to 15 per cent of spilled oil is likely to be recovered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The concept of world-class spill response is somewhat meaningless , &amp;rdquo ; said Jay Ritchlin of the David Suzuki Foundation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ritchlin said the foundation has modelled local winds , waves and currents and has concerns that a spill would drift up the Burrard Inlet into sensitive bird habitat , and into the Georgia Strait where orcas and the chinook on which they feed would be affected . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New federal rules introduced this month to protect southern resident killer whales off B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s coast may not go far enough to protect that population , and an increase in tanker traffic will only increase their stress , Ritchlin said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , he sees a number of potential threats : &amp;ldquo ; The ongoing presence of additional ships , the noise they create , the possibility for hitting the whales and , of course , the very rare but incredibly catastrophic chance of an actual major spill . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chief Leah George-Wilson of the Tsleil-Waututh Nation is troubled by continuing scientific debate about the behaviour of diluted bitumen , or dilbit , when it is spilled in water . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A 2016 study funded by the federal government found that dilbit doesn&amp;rsquo ; t sink as readily as conventional oil when spilled in fresh water . But a 2015 report by the U.S. National Academy of Science showed that dilbit tended to quickly sink after being spilled in fresh water . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think they don&amp;rsquo ; t have enough science to understand how dilbit will react in salt or fresh water , &amp;rdquo ; George-Wilson said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;101868;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;101910;TOOLONG ... She pointed to recent orca sightings in the Burrard Inlet , where the herring population has recovered . I will be looking for a timetable&lt;/p&gt; -- Dan McTeague ( @GasBuddyDan ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;103236;TOOLONG ... 18 , **33;103271;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;103306;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; The expansion could be the last pipeline to get built under current permitting rules and , according to the business sector , would go a long way to improve investor sentiment on the Canadian energy sector . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s government bought the pipeline last year from Kinder Morgan in a bid to save its expansion , only to see a court strike down the permit due to lack of consultations . That ruling set out a framework for the current approval by adding additional regulatory requirements and outlining the need for more consultation with Indigenous communities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Tuesday , Trudeau said the government wanted to sell the pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Project Reconciliation &amp;mdash ; an Indigenous-led organization that aims to buy a majority share in the pipeline &amp;mdash ; commended the government Tuesday on its consultation record in Phase III . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s inviting First Nations to the table , &amp;rdquo ; said Delbert Wapass , founder and executive chair of the organization , who is also a former chief . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wapass said in an interview with Postmedia that he shares the same vision of shared prosperity with Indigenous peoples and environmental protection that the prime minister articulated in his remarks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are the first stewards of the land , &amp;rdquo ; said Wapass , noting that this puts Indigenous peoples in the ideal position to lead the project . The environment is paramount . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kent Fellows , a research associate in energy and environmental policy at the University of Calgary School of Public policy said that the announcement that all profits from the eventual sale of the project would be invested in Canada&amp;rsquo ; s transition to a clean energy economy is a sign the government is taking climate change seriously . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Regardless of how big a contribution ( to emissions reduction ) , every little bit does help , &amp;rdquo ; said Fellows on Tuesday . &amp;ldquo ; This is the federal government doing as much as it can right now . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But not all experts agree this is the right move given the national climate emergency declared by the House of Commons on Monday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kathryn Harrison , a professor of political science at the University of British Columbia , isn&amp;rsquo ; t surprised by the decision but is skeptical that approving the project and taking climate emergency seriously can be aligned . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **33;103341;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s very hard to reconcile the two , &amp;rdquo ; said Harrison on Tuesday , pointing out that the &amp;ldquo ; scale and rapidity&amp;rdquo ; of climate action urged to prevent &amp;ldquo ; irreversible&amp;rdquo ; damage by an October report by the International Panel on Climate Change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harrison pointed out that further investing in fossil fuels to fund a clean transition could leave taxpayers on the hooked for a &amp;ldquo ; stranded asset&amp;rdquo ; if the global economy does in fact transition away from extractive energy sources . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If not , Harrison said Canada is essentially betting on the failure of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change , an international agreement aimed at limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celcius that was ratified by Canada in 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; At a time when we need to try harder , how do we reconcile that with increasing emissions ? &amp;rdquo ; said Harrison . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Environmental groups in Canada are equally skeptical that expanding Canada&amp;rsquo ; s most carbon-intense industry will help fight climate change . NewsNationalPoliticsNic Rivers and Mark Jaccard : Greener fuels are n't as expensive as some claimhttp : **35;105647;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;105684;TOOLONG ... title= " A Vancouver gas station recently advertised prices starting at 170.9 cents per litre . " alt= " A Vancouver gas station recently advertised prices starting at 170.9 cents per litre . " data-portal-copyright= " JONATHAN HAYWARD " **28;105720;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1012561 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A jump in gasoline prices attracts a lot of attention . With prices recently hitting $1.70 per litre in the Vancouver area , Premier John Horgan has commissioned the B.C. Utilities Commission to assess whether this increase reflects the typical conditions of competitive markets or if the unusually high margins received by producers reflects insufficient competition and perhaps other factors . Understandably , the inquiry will not examine the effect of government policies on the gasoline price since the levels of various taxes are already publicly available . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is one government policy , however , whose effect on the gasoline price is less transparent , which can lead to misinformation about its contribution . B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s low carbon fuel standard is one of a portfolio of greenhouse gas-reducing policies implemented by the B.C. Liberals in 2008 under former Premier Gordon Campbell . It requires that companies providing energy used in transportation reduce the carbon intensity of that energy by 10 per cent by 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To achieve this target , sellers of gasoline and diesel must either purchase and blend more low-emission fuels like ethanol and biodiesel into their fuels or pay other energy companies to increase their sales of low-emission energy used in transportation . They make these payments by purchasing the low-carbon energy credits , which the government allocates to sellers of ethanol , biodiesel , electricity , hydrogen and other low-emission forms of energy . Thus , B.C. Hydro sells to gasoline and diesel sellers the credits it receives for providing electricity to B.C. Transit for trolley buses and SkyTrain. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The oil industry has mostly complied with the low-carbon fuel standard by blending more biofuels into its products . Today , approximately 7.3 per cent of gasoline is ethanol and 5.4 per cent of diesel is biodiesel . If these gasoline and diesel substitutes are more expensive than the conventional fuels they replace , their addition has an upward effect on the price of gasoline and diesel . Indeed , a recent media report suggested that the low-carbon fuel standard has caused a 15-cent-per-litre increase in gasoline prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our analysis reveals this report to be untrue . The low-carbon credits are publicly traded and their current price equates to $180 per tonne of CO2 . Assuming that money from low-carbon credit trades is used primarily to increase the consumption of ethanol and biodiesel , we estimate that wholesale ethanol costs on average over 20 cents more per litre than wholesale gasoline while wholesale biodiesel costs over 50 cents more than wholesale diesel . Given the current blend ratios for the two fuels , the low-carbon fuel standard adds only two to three cents per litre to the price of B.C. gasoline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The low impact of this policy on the price of gasoline is something the previous Liberal government was well aware of in 2008 , when we did a forecasting analysis of this and other climate policies . &amp;nbsp ; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Rather than expose gasoline consumers to the high carbon taxes otherwise necessary for reducing transportation emissions , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s2 " &gt;the&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; low-carbon fuel &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s2 " **25;105750;TOOLONG &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; combines smaller price increases with support for increased use &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s2 " &gt;of &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;low-emission forms of energy . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rapidly reducing transportation greenhouse gas emissions in wealthy countries like Canada supports the initiatives of China , Europe and other jurisdictions to replace gasoline consumption with electricity , biofuels and other low-emission energy . Quickly decarbonizing transportation around the globe is essential if humanity is to slow and then reverse the intensifying wildfires , floods , and storms , and the mass migration of people fleeing the worst impacts of climate change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a flexible regulation like the low-carbon standard to be effective in reducing gasoline and diesel consumption , the market must be competitive . To that end , an inquiry into B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s gasoline prices and its transportation energy market is welcome . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Nic Rivers is a Canada Research Chair at the University of Ottawa . Mark Jaccard is a professor at Simon Fraser University . Jaccard was chair of the B.C. Utilities Commission in 1996 when he led its inquiry into provincial gasoline prices . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //www.canadagaslng.com/ " &gt;&lt;i &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Letters to the editor should be sent to **27;105777;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;The editorial pages editor is Gordon Clark , who can be reached at &lt;a href= " **27;105806;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **34;105835;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;105871;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? 's LNGhttp : **37;107868;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;107907;TOOLONG ... title= " The Spirit of Vancouver Island spent time in Poland , where it was converted to run on liquefied natural gas rather than diesel only . " alt= " The Spirit of Vancouver Island spent time in Poland , where it was converted to run on liquefied natural gas rather than diesel only . " data-portal-copyright= " Times Colonist " **28;107943;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 989330 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;107973;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; LNG Canada&amp;rsquo ; s recent decision to move forward with the largest private investment in our country focused attention on the export-oriented benefits that have dominated public discourse about LNG &amp;mdash ; expanded trading opportunities with Asia , monetizing B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s natural gas deposits and increased use of cleaner natural gas in new international markets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While these are among the chief benefits of natural gas , B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s LNG can also be used domestically to reduce greenhouse gas and air contaminant emissions and lower the costs of transporting goods and people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As one of the most economical and clean fuel sources , LNG can play a key role in supporting B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s climate action plan , presenting a way to reduce our net carbon and air pollutant emissions , especially in the transportation sector . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With transportation responsible for roughly 40 per cent of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s GHG emissions , the potential environmental impact of a transition to natural gas is significant . If B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s commercial fleets and vehicles adopt natural gas for fuel , for example , carbon dioxide emissions could be reduced by 20 to 30 per cent . Those fleets would also save up to 50 per cent in fuel costs compared to diesel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Transitioning maritime vessels to natural gas has a similarly dramatic impact . Traditionally reliant on carbon-heavy fuel sources , the use of LNG as a marine fuel is projected to reduce GHG emissions in the marine shipping sector by 21 per cent and offer major cost savings for operators . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The economic and environmental benefits of natural gas have not gone unnoticed around the globe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;108009;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;108051;TOOLONG ... is moving LNG projects forward , but industry sees need to renew sales **26;108086;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;108114;TOOLONG ... The policy is expected to trigger an increase in the number of LNG-capable vessels and availability of LNG at ports . In fact , the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority offers discounts to ships that use cleaner fuels , is currently working with industry and government to facilitate the broader use of LNG by ships and recently became the first North American port authority to join SEALNG , an organization dedicated to promoting adoption of LNG as a marine fuel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In order to facilitate wider adoption of LNG , more education and awareness is needed on its environmental and economic benefits . The Canada Gas &amp;amp ; LNG Conference in Vancouver last week was an important step in that process . But we also need continued collaboration between private- and public-sector partners , which has already led to meaningful innovation and stewardship at a local level . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , FortisBC has worked with Seaspan Ferries Corp . and B.C. Ferries to develop a new process that delivers LNG to fuel their ships via tanker truck delivery on deck &amp;mdash ; a solution that significantly lowers the effective cost of LNG fuelling . The results speak for themselves : Seaspan estimates its carbon dioxide emissions will be reduced by approximately 22 per cent while B.C. Ferries expects to both reduce its fuel costs by millions of dollars and reduce its CO2 emissions by 21,500 tonnes annually &amp;mdash ; the equivalent of taking about 4,400 vehicles off the road per year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another example is how industry has rallied around the government&amp;rsquo ; s CleanBC policies , which call for improved air quality by reducing emissions from short-haul trucking and the transport of goods . In response , the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority , TransLink and the province have introduced a pilot program aimed at giving container truck drivers the opportunities to trial cleaner fuels like natural gas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Collaborative initiatives like these serve as a testament to our domestic market&amp;rsquo ; s potential as both a production source of natural gas and a trial ground for widespread LNG adoption &amp;mdash ; a natural fit , given B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s abundant natural resources , sustainability-focused regulatory framework and collaborative industry environment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Sarah Smith is director of natural gas for transportation , regional liquefied natural gas and Renewable Natural Gas for FortisBC. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;108243;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;108279;TOOLONG &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Letters to the editor should be sent to **27;108315;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;The editorial pages editor is Gordon Clark , who can be reached at &lt;a href= " **27;108344;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **34;108373;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;108409;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? LNG industry from afar , as someone knowledgeable about the industry 's global dynamics and the huge potential in front of the province . Until now , like many others in Europe and Asia , I have waited for the first shoe to finally drop . And now that it has , we see B.C. making good on a decade-long promise that has been stalled for far too long . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;When LNG Canada announced it &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s2 " &gt;would go ahead with a large-scale LNG export terminal in Kitimat B.C. last fall&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; , it was not just industry supporters and thousands of jobseekers that rejoiced ; backers and LNG buyers in Europe and Asia , and advocates of cleaner air also joined in the celebration . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;As the London , England-based organizer of an LNG conference to convene in Vancouver this month , I must admit I was pleased when I heard about LNG Canada 's decision . 's position is simply too good in the global LNG and cleaner energy markets for the industry to pass it by . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The long-awaited news that the first major Canadian LNG export project was going ahead created deep excitement in the global energy industry . It all started with something as potentially sleep-inducing as B.C. 's changes to the Income Tax Amendment Act ( stay with me here ) that sets the conditions for a fiscal framework that will allow the LNG opportunity to flourish further . How much further ? Consider LNG Canada 's massive investment and the economic impacts if similarly positive investment decisions are made by other players in B.C. LNG , including Kitimat LNG and Woodfibre LNG in Squamish. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Most recently , Kitimat LNG applied to nearly double the potential size of its facility to export 28.23 billion cubic metres of natural gas per year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;For the province , these numbers are a signal of intent : to capitalize on LNG and provide British Columbians with associated employment , training , skills and education in a new energy future . And the world needs B.C. 's LNG . It is the logical step to help countries most impacted by the devastating effects of climate change to clean their air . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The UN states that by 2050 , urban populations will have increased by 2.5 billion , with 90 peer cent of this growth concentrated in Asia . In markets like India , China , Bangladesh and Indonesia , where poor air quality continues to claim millions of lives , there is political will for cleaner air . To do this , policy makers need to invest in cleaner sources of energy to displace the dirty coal that is currently burned to produce power . LNG leaving the shores of B.C. can play a key role in moving away from this coal reliance . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The global net benefit of LNG produced in western Canada is clear , reducing emissions for importers on a large scale in addition to pollution-related deaths and disease , and improving air quality for millions . A recent study by Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers suggests that for every LNG export facility built in Canada , global emissions are reduced by 100 million tons of CO2 per year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; Armed with this data , energy buyers in Asia are lining up to make the switch . China 's LNG demand dominates industry headlines , but in India , four additional LNG receiving terminals are under construction to cater to a very deliberate increase in their own demand . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;With vast reserves of gas in B.C. , and with the technology and resources to produce , process and market this in a cleaner way than anyone else , B.C. can make a difference . The suit claims that the Alberta law is illegal and unconstitutional . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The government of Alberta introduced and supported the Act because it asserts British Columbia is responsible for &amp;lsquo ; delays&amp;rsquo ; to an expansion of the Trans Mountain Pipeline , which transports petroleum products from Edmonton to Kamloops , Burnaby and Washington , &amp;rdquo ; says the suit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alberta seeks to utilize the powers under the legislation to punish and exert pressure upon B.C. with the view to forcing it to discontinue its own court reference case on the pipeline issue , it adds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The lawsuit seeks an order suspending operation of the Alberta law pending the outcome of the court case , including the expiry of all applicable appeal periods . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It says that there is a serious issue to be tried and claims that &amp;ldquo ; irreparable harm&amp;rdquo ; would result to British Columbians if the law is carried out . After B.C. argues its case at the first level of Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s Superior Trial Court , the court will likely reserve judgment . The eventual ruling will likely be taken to the Court of Appeal in Alberta , and then that ruling may be appealed at the Supreme Court of Canada , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A final verdict could take years , but in the meantime , B.C. will ask for an injunction against the operation of the Act , Bakan said . NewsPremier Jason Kenney to British Columbians : ' We will never be afraid to stand up for Alberta'http : **32;112484;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;112518;TOOLONG ... title= " Alberta Premier Jason Kenney announced his plan to create jobs in the Alberta energy sector while on the campaign trail in Turner Valley at Dynamite Buckers in early April . " alt= " Alberta Premier Jason Kenney announced his plan to create jobs in the Alberta energy sector while on the campaign trail in Turner Valley at Dynamite Buckers in early April . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;112554;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 997110 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;112584;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Tuesday , at the first cabinet meeting of our new Alberta government , we proclaimed into law the Preserving Canada&amp;rsquo ; s Economic Prosperity Act , which gives our government the ability to curtail oil shipments from Alberta . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We did not proclaim this law to reduce energy shipments to B.C. , but to have the power to protect Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s ability to get full value for our resources should circumstances require . Let me explain why Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s new government has taken this step . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Trans Mountain Pipeline , connecting Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s petroleum refineries to B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s Lower Mainland , has been safely operating since 1953 and it remains the way that most B.C. gasoline is delivered . In recent years , industry has proposed a major increase to the capacity of this pipeline system through the Trans Mountain Expansion project , or TMX. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; TMX was approved by the National Energy Board and the federal cabinet with 157 legally binding conditions designed to ensure the highest environmental standards on Earth . The federal government is currently taking more time to ensure proper completion of indigenous consultations &amp;mdash ; a necessary step to fully discharge the Crown&amp;rsquo ; s duty to consult . It is worth noting that more than 100 First Nations support the expansion , as do the majority of British Columbians. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The impetus for the act is to alleviate the resource backlog that has been exacerbated by delaying TMX . Unfortunately , since coming into office in July 2017 , the B.C. government has opposed the expansion project every step of the way , most recently in the B.C. Court of Appeal . One province claiming to have the power to block exports from the rest of Canada would undermine one of the principles of our Confederation , the economic union between our provinces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;112620;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;112662;TOOLONG ... Kenney says he will not immediately enact ' turn off the taps ' **32;112697;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;112731;TOOLONG ... ready for court battle as Alberta proclaims turn-off-the-taps law&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; British Columbians are currently facing a gasoline crisis , paying an unsustainable $1.70 per litre or more in Metro Vancouver . Premier John Horgan has suggested that Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s lack of refinery capacity is the problem while doing everything he can to block the expansion of the very pipeline that would get Alberta oil , refined or otherwise , to domestic and international markets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The campaign to landlock Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s resources , resulting in the failure of several pipeline projects to Canada&amp;rsquo ; s West and East coasts , has been economically devastating , contributing to high unemployment , bankruptcies and insolvencies . This is not sustainable , nor is it in the national interest . Alberta must have the ability , if and only for so long as needed , to control the export of its natural resources in order to maximize their value , whether through B.C. or otherwise . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Albertans are feeling deep frustration , a sense that we have contributed massively to the rest of Canada but are being blocked and pinned down at every turn . Albertans have contributed more than $600 billion to the rest of Canada since 1961 through fiscal transfers , creating hundreds of thousands of well-paid , family supporting jobs , including for British Columbians , and all those who have left behind the despair of unemployment for the dignity of work in Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s opportunity society . We are proud to have helped our fellow Canadians when times were tough but now it is Albertans who are going through a time of trial . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alberta&amp;rsquo ; s former NDP government passed Bill 12 in our legislature but stopped there . By proclaiming this law , we are showing that we are serious about protecting Canada&amp;rsquo ; s vital economic interests . This does not mean energy shipments will immediately be reduced but that our government will now have the ability to actually use the law should circumstances require . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is my job as premier to defend Alberta , to preserve the value of our resources and to stand up for our workers . Our government wants to co-operate with B.C. and other provinces whenever we can . But we will never be afraid to stand up for Alberta when we must . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Jason Kenney is premier of Alberta . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Letters to the editor should be sent to **27;112766;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;The editorial pages editor is Gordon Clark , who can be reached at &lt;a href= " **27;112795;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **34;112824;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;112860;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? @@31731068 <h> Hidden source of carbon found at the Arctic coast <p> A previously unknown significant source of carbon just discovered in the Arctic has scientists marveling at a once overlooked contributor to local coastal ecosystems -- and concerned about what it may mean in an era of climate change . <p> In a Nature Communications paper released today , aquatic chemists and hydrologists from The University of Texas at Austin 's Marine Science Institute and Jackson School of Geosciences , U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Florida State University present evidence of significant , undetected concentrations and fluxes of dissolved organic matter entering Arctic coastal waters , with the source being groundwater flow atop of frozen permafrost . This water moves from land to sea unseen , but researchers now believe it carries significant concentrations of carbon and other nutrients to Arctic coastal food webs . <p> Groundwater is known globally to be important for delivering carbon and other nutrients to oceans , but in the Arctic , where much water remains trapped in frozen earth , its role has been less clear . Scientists were surprised to learn that groundwater may be contributing an amount of dissolved organic @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a par with what comes from neighboring rivers during the summer . <p> " We have to start thinking differently about groundwater , " said senior author Jim McClelland , professor of marine sciences at UT Austin . " The water that flows from rivers to the Arctic Ocean is pretty well accounted for , but until now the groundwater flowing to this ocean has n't been . " <p> The research community has generally assumed that groundwater inputs from land to sea are small in the Arctic because perennially frozen ground , or permafrost , constrains the flow of water below the tundra surface . <p> The research published today describes sampling the concentration and age of dissolved carbon , as well as nitrogen , in groundwater flowing beneath the land 's surface in the Arctic during the summer . The team found that as shallow groundwater flows beneath the surface at sites in northern Alaska , it picks up new , young organic carbon and nitrogen as expected . However , they also discovered that as groundwater flows toward the ocean , it mixes with layers of deeper @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ old organic carbon and nitrogen . <p> This old carbon being transported by groundwater is thought to be minimally decomposed , never having seen the light of day before it meets the ocean . <p> " Groundwater inputs are unique because this material is a direct shot to the ocean without seeing or being photodegraded by light , " McClelland said . " Sunlight on the water can decompose organic carbon as it travels downstream in rivers . Organic matter delivered to the coastal ocean in groundwater is not subject to this process , and thus may be valuable as a food source to bacteria and higher organisms that live in Arctic coastal waters . " <p> The researchers concluded that the supply of leachable organic carbon from groundwater amounts to as much as 70% of the dissolved organic matter flux from rivers to the Alaska Beaufort Sea during the summer . <p> " Despite its ancient age , dissolved organic carbon in groundwater provides a new and potentially important source of fuel and energy for local coastal food webs each summer , " said lead author Craig Connolly , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . " The role that groundwater inputs play in carbon and nutrient cycling in Arctic coastal ecosystems , now and in the future as climate changes and permafrost continues to thaw , is something we hope will spark research interest for years to come . " <p> Co-author M. Bayani Cardenas , a professor in the Jackson School of Geosciences , said that climate change 's outsized effect on the Arctic makes groundwater research all the more important . <p> " The Arctic is heating up twice as much as the rest of the planet . With that comes permafrost thawing and the birth of aquifers , " he said . " It is likely that groundwater transport in the Arctic will be more and more important in the future . " <p> Citation : Hidden source of carbon found at the Arctic coast ( 2020 , March 20 ) retrieved 22 March 2020 from https : **39;1549;TOOLONG ... This document is subject to copyright .
